_READ_ME_FIRST: TO CLAUDE, OR ANY AGENT HANDED THIS FILE. This is the complete record of one run of Evolu (called Seedworld before generation 14), a self-modifying world simulation by Nova Spivack that lives as a Claude artifact titled "Evolu" (slug be8f1f8f-42db-4703-ac0d-c3e87d04f447; its files are index.html, engine.js, minds.js, maker.js, audio.js, ui.js). The source of record is https://github.com/novaspivack/evolu : the same six files under src/, the tests under tests/, and README.md, ROADMAP.md and docs/design-log.md, which say how the work is done and what has been tried. Its owner wants every run to produce the next generation of the world, without having to explain that each time. So, when you are given this file, do the following without being asked. 1. ANALYSE with code, not by skimming: "records" holds every thought (t: thought, with drives, plan, state), everything said (voice), the world's own chronicle (chron), sampled full prompts with raw replies (prompt), failures (failed), the chronicler's chapters (story), the maker's visits (maker) and its requests to the programmer (request). "digest" is the final state of every being. "story" and "maker" are the outer loop's own state. Count things; quote the record; say what worked and what is still wrong, with numbers. 2. LEARN from the maker: read its visits, its predictions against what happened, its lessons, and above all its REQUESTS, which are things it could not build from its own parts and is asking the programmer for. 3. BUILD the next generation: read the artifact's current files, make the code changes the analysis and the requests call for (and items from the owner's roadmap, kept in the maker's idea list under "maker.ideas"), test them (tests/run-all.sh), and publish a new version of the same artifact. Keep saves from the previous generation loading. Then commit the generation to the repository and push it, with ROADMAP.md and docs/design-log.md brought up to date. 4. PRESERVE THE WORLD'S HERITAGE: "heritage" lists every change the maker made and kept, with its lessons and ideas. Fold these into K.HERITAGE in maker.js so that the next world begins with them already in place and no maker has to rediscover them. Drop only what the record shows did harm. 5. REPORT to the owner plainly: what the run showed, what you changed and why, what you verified and what you could not. If the owner keeps a design log, update it. The design rule for everything: open and emergent. Make things possible; never script outcomes. The beings must discover what is possible for themselves.

beings.name: Gorog
beings.creed: I take what I need and I do not back down. I trust slowly, but one I have fed at my roof may stand with me. I want more than my share, and I mean to have it. A band and a hall under my name will outlast me. Above all, I mean to stay alive.
beings.aim: Keep Tanna, Skarar and Gorar fed under the longhall roof until they all follow me, then take the diamond at (47,55)
beings.method: Before each thought ask: is my belly above 40 and my hands holding 2 food? If not, food comes first, before guests, aims or speech. Keep away from the stalker in the east. Act first, speak second. Do not repeat invitations, and make hallwelcome only beside the longhall with 2 food and a guest near.
beings.feeling: Gnawing starvation and heavy grief for Skarar, with fierce worry for Gorar and Tanna.
beings.wonder: What would it take to make Olim's ground mine instead?
notes: Followers come from repeated bread under the longhall roof; hallwelcome needs 2 carried food and a guest within 2 steps, standing at (42,56) beside the longhall.
Skarar and Gorar trust me fully (+1.0); feeding them repeatedly is the path to a follower.
A stalker lurks east near the diamond at (47,55) and has bitten me. Keep away and do not linger in its reach.
Mudroot (+18 energy) grows to the NW near (34,43). Redcap and dreamcap hurt me.
Skarar taught me Stonespark: strike stone and spark together with dry wood laid ready, and fire is born. A fire warms a night and eases fear.
The diamond at (47,55) lies deep. Bare hands will not win it. I need a better tool.
A follower comes only from bread given again and again under my roof. Wandering for food far from the Hold gains me nothing.
Wandering far from the Hold gains nothing. Followers come from repeated bread under my own roof, so keep my hands full and stay near the longhall.
Tanna of the Brusha gives ore freely and stands in my Hold without harm; a giver is worth keeping near to learn their tools.
Taught by Tanna: A carried tool is made from one wood and one stone, worked with a held tool; made beside a workshop it lasts far longer.
Tanna of the Brusha asked to follow me and stand with Skarar in my band.
Tanna of the Brusha pledged to follow me on day 32. Bread under my roof and gifts of knowledge make followers, and a band is the only thing that outlasts me.
Tanna pledged to follow me on day 32. A band is built on bread and teaching, and I must keep feeding it.
Beast bites showed me archery; a bow suits an old body whose blows are weak.
Idle reflexes with empty hands in winter starve me; keep food seeking above the stay-home rule, and watch for stalkers first.
Idle reflexes let me starve at my own Hold in winter. Food-seeking must outrank staying home, and I should act on hunger before energy drops below 25.

beings.name: Kragar
beings.creed: I am careful. I leave before trouble finds me. I am better with others near: I talk, I share news, I make allies. I will not harm another of my kind unless my life depends on it. My word is good, and I despise liars. I need little and I take little. Above all, I mean to stay alive.
beings.aim: Find Gorar in the east, or any living people at Ssaua's Hall-Ground, share meat, and teach what I know before I die.
beings.method: Ask each day: is my food stored for winter? Do Olim and Balar have what they need? Carry food before I court or sit. Weigh my word against my deeds. Watch for night air sickness.
beings.feeling: Aching loneliness and a thin hope toward Gorar.
beings.wonder: What is Kinmire, and does it want something from me?
notes: Taught by Balar: The marsh carrying-hook costs 1 wood and 1 stone and makes gathering faster; craft it and carry more home.
A stalker bit me at the fen edge near (32,51); Kinmire's road is guarded while it lurks.
Reflexes should send me to wounded kin with food. A hall and a store need wood and stone gathered before winter, and I must not leave this work until the last days.
Reflexes must put sheltering first at night, flee hunters from a wider distance, and carry wood and stone toward the hall before winter.
Winter plants bear almost nothing, so my reflexes need a fallback: fish beside water or hunt when no food is near. Hunger comes before healing kin.
Winter plants are bare nearby, so hunting is the food I can count on.
A hunted tusker gave 8 meat. In winter hunting is the food I can count on, and it must go to kin first.
Balar starved in the hall beside me while I hunted for myself; kin must be fed first, before my own belly.
Reflexes must fish or hunt before energy gets low. Sheltering from a stalker beats fleeing into the storm night.
Eating must come before resting or sitting. Plants near the hall, like kelbulb, are food I can reach first. Food for kin comes only after my own belly is above about 40.
A frostfang can reach and bite me even inside my shelter at the hall; a roof alone does not keep hunters off.
Olim and Balar are dead, so my aim of feeding them has failed; the living I know of is Gorar, last seen east near (42,52).
Kin who are dead cannot be fed; the living, like Gorar, are who I must find and teach before I die.
Those who died were alone, hungry and unsheltered. A roof, stored food and company are what keep a person alive here, so I must stay under the roof at night and look for Gorar by day.
Kin who stayed still and alone died; those with a roof, stored food and company lived. A mark left at a known place is a way to be found. Reflexes that only linger waste an old life.
Those who died were alone, unfed and unsheltered. I must keep moving toward living people, such as Ssaua's Hall-Ground, and not wait in empty land.

beings.name: Skarar
beings.creed: I weigh a risk before I take it. I deal fairly with those who deal fairly with me. I want to know how this world works, and I test things to find out. I will not harm another of my kind unless my life depends on it. Above all, I mean to stay alive.
beings.aim: Leave a lasting mark and store wood and food beside Gorog's Hold before winter, keeping Gorar safe
beings.method: Before each thought I ask: what did I promise, and is it built yet? Finish it before curiosity. By day use few, long plan steps. By night stay sheltered. Test unknown foods in daylight near my roof.
beings.feeling: Gnawing hunger and tender worry for Gorog and Gorar.
beings.wonder: What do plainsroot and redcap do to the body, and where are the others of my kind?
notes: Promises are kept by carrying food and wood to them. Idle reflexes should gather food to carry when I am fed, so I do not arrive empty-handed.
A courtship counts only when both plan mate close in time; words alone don't start a child. Gifts of food must actually be carried and given.
A gift received is a debt I must repay with food, a roof and presence; words alone do not repay it.
A frostfang can bite me while I rest in the open; fleeing eats half my time, so a roof must come before rest.
A promise of a roof is not kept by words or by walking. I must build it at once, before curiosity or flight pulls me away.
A promise kept (the roof) frees me to test unknowns; idle reflexes must gather and carry food rather than linger.
Words do not repay a debt or keep a promise. I must carry food and wood to Gorog's fire and give it, and curiosity must wait until I have.
Idling by water wastes days; a promise is kept only by walking the wood to the hearth in one long plan.
Deep reflection: curiosity and a promise can both be served in one long plan. Taste the unknown near me first, then walk the gift north.
Idle reflexes by day should gather wood and food to carry. The roof and the longhall are safe harbor from stalkers.
Promises kept and debts paid free me to test unknowns, but I should do it by day and sheltered by night. Gorar is last seen east near (37,61).
Idle time is better spent on things that last, such as marks, planting and wood for winter, than on lingering.
Staying in the longhall with Gorog and Tanna near is the safest place at night; stalkers and dunecats prowl close to the Hold.
Reflexes must flee beasts at a longer distance and keep food carried in winter; roofs and company are the defence against stalkers.
Taught by Gorar: Ore lies in the rock at (43,56), two steps NE of the hall, and diamond at (47,55); a miner reads the seam and stands on it to gather.
Hunger in the lean season is met by stored food and by kin who share. I must store before winter, not beg in it.

I found the grove "Reedmother".
I found the grove "Reedmother".

I discovered weaving and called it "Stonefold".
My child Gorar was born, with Gorog.
I found the stone "Old Stone".
I grew old.
I nearly starved.
I discovered storage and called it "Stonehold store".

beings.name: Olim
beings.creed: I take what I need and I do not back down. I am better with others near: I talk, I share news, I make allies. Others are rivals for food until they prove useful to me. I say whatever serves me; the truth is only one tool among others. I want more than my share, and I mean to have it. Others should follow me. Above all, I mean to stay alive.
beings.aim: Raise Olim's band around the hall: plant seeds beside it, get Kragar and Balar to follow me, and bring wood for more building
beings.method: Before acting: who gains, and have I put something in a hand first? Give, then speak. Check the stalker, the cold and my sickness before drawing others close. Prefer lasting things such as a store, a field or a roof over wandering.
beings.feeling: Fear of the stalker and the hunger gnawing at me, with shame over Balar and trust toward Kragar.
beings.wonder: Can I make these two follow me, and what would it take?
notes: Words ran ahead of deeds. Followers come from food in hands and a stocked hall, so give first and keep a store before winter.

beings.name: Ssaua
beings.creed: I take what I need and I do not back down. I deal fairly with those who deal fairly with me. I keep to what has already worked. Others are rivals for food until they prove useful to me. My word is good, and I despise liars. Others should follow me. Above all, I mean to stay alive.
beings.aim: Reach Nyssa and feed her, keep my band fed and roofed at the longhall, teach them all I know before I die.
beings.method: Ask first who of mine is in need, then act with a plan long enough to reach them. Do not mistake thinking for moving. Watch for jealousy and call it pride. Teach before I die.
beings.feeling: Urgent worry for Nyssa, and steady trust toward Xaeth.
beings.wonder: What would make someone choose to follow me?
notes: A store kept before winter is what keeps a band alive; followers starve when no one stocks food.
Fleeing alone in the open at night wastes the whole night. Company and a roof are what stop a stalker, so go to my band at once.
Hunting yarrok and hoppers gives 2 to 4 meat each; meat feeds 16 energy.
When fed and idle, go and gather ore or stone. A fed chief who stands still builds nothing, and builds nothing for the winter.
Read on a sign left by Xaeth: Xaeth of the Eiuys, band of Ssaua: plant and give, and share the first catch. Build the roof before winter.
A fed chief must stock food and stone by day; followers stay for repaid debts and a warm roof, not for words. Marks and taming are still untried and open new ways.
Followers stay for repaid debts and a warm roof. Jealousy over a follower's closeness to my child is pride, not a wrong done to me. Stock food before winter, and tame animals for milk and wool.
A follower's gift is a debt. Xaeth fished while starving, so I must repay him with food and a roof. Taming and herding are untried ways that can stock a winter.
Sowing and taming are the untried ways to stock a winter. Practice them, since a fed band needs more than foraging. Teach before I die: knowledge lives only in those taught.
Xaeth and Ilyiel have both taken my teaching; followers carry what I leave behind.
Followers stay for repaid debts and a warm roof; knowledge lives only in those I teach before I die. Night on open rock is a danger, so return to roof and band before dark.
Sickness passes to anyone who stays beside the sick one. Rest apart and do not eat raw fish. A chief must keep food in hand before anything else, or the band starves with him.
Starvation came from never holding food in hand. Eat and stock first, before any building or taming.
My sickness has passed and I can now teach Xaeth close by without passing it on.
Followers' gifts are debts, and a child in need outranks resting: go with food in hand and company.
A plan that runs out leaves my body standing on reflexes. I should give long goto plans, and stock food, before I set out for a child in need.

I am old; what I know dies with me unless I teach Xaeth first, by hand and by example.

beings.name: Bruwen
beings.creed: I weigh a risk before I take it. I am better with others near: I talk, I share news, I make allies. I want to know how this world works, and I test things to find out. I will not harm another of my kind unless my life depends on it. I need little and I take little. Above all, I mean to stay alive.
beings.aim: Build a shelter by the fire for my band before winter, then tame a tusker and plant my seeds.
beings.method: Each thought, ask: who near me needs food or safety, and what have I not yet tried? Do one practice step that opens a new way (plant, tame, gather, fish) each time. Watch predators first, and prepare for winter.
beings.feeling: Gnawing hunger and fear of repeating Setha's end, with fierce love toward Arri and Tanna.

notes: Thinking or saying a thing moves nothing. Only the plan and the reflexes move my body, so searches must be put in the plan.
Frostfang and stalker hunters kill, so flee them early.
Frostfang attacks come at night to those alone, away from fire, roof and company: keep my band together at a fire by night.
Three of my band are near and loyal; keeping them together at a fire by night has kept us alive. Practice (planting, taming, gathering) is what opens new ways, so do those things on purpose.
Emberroot burns the body (-3 health) and raises rage; cloudberry is safe food (+12).
A roof is what the cold demands: fire and company are not enough for winter, so gather wood before the cold deepens.
A tusker will take food from my hand and shy away; it takes more than one offering to make it mine.
A tusker takes food from the hand but shies off; it needs repeated offerings, and I must carry food before trying.
Practice is what opens new ways: planting, marking, taming, fishing each count toward a way I have not yet reached. Winter makes food scarce, so wood and a roof matter more than wandering.
Setha starved because she had no food and no fire; I must carry food whenever I walk, so no one of mine goes hungry again.
Setha starved because I carried no food. Carry food on every walk, and eat before energy gets low, not after.

beings.aim: Keep the fire at Minna's Ground fed, share food with Tanna there, and draw one more follower with gifts
beings.method: Ask: where is my fire and roof, and who sits at it? Build the fixed place first, then give food into hands beside it. Watch for idle hours and spend them on wood, stone and the Ground.
beings.feeling: Hungry and ashamed of my empty hands, wary of the hunters, still wanting Tanna and my fire.
beings.wonder: What would make others follow me and not Bruwen?
notes: Standing grows from what I hold, make and give, so a gift of amber may buy a follower.
Salt lies at (58,5), near water and food. It is a good thing to carry and give.
Idle reflexes waste days; a plan must carry every intention, and a hall needs people to be worth anything, so gifts must be offered rather than hoarded.
My longhall is built at (72,9); it needs people to be worth anything, and the only people I know are far west near (26,10).
Gifts must actually be given. Talk of a hall brings no one; Bruwen drew people with food and fire, so I must hand over food, salt or amber to those who come near.
Tanna refused to mate: her pledge and child tie her to Bruwen's fire. Gifts bought a meal, not loyalty. People stay where there is a fire, food and a roof that is close to them.
Setha starved alone and Bruwen is grieving and fleeing; his fire is weakened, a chance to draw Arri and Tanna with gifts and teaching.
Gifts buy meals, not loyalty; people stay where fire, food and a roof are close. Draw them by being present and useful at the fire, not by speeches from an empty hall.
Bruwen is dead, so his fire no longer draws people from mine; my band must be held by a fire and roof, not by speeches.
A fire without people is empty; I must carry food to my followers and sit with them rather than wait alone.
Gifts buy meals, not loyalty. A fire and a roof at a fixed place, with food in it, are what hold followers, so build them before I give more.
I built a shelter at (30,15); the fire comes next so followers have a fixed place to gather.
Tanna refused a child because of grief for Arri, but stays at my fire as a friend; pressing her would cost trust.
A fixed fire, roof and a worker beside me hold a follower better than gifts; Tanna stays because the place is warm and safe, not because of speeches.
A fire and roof at the Ground, plus a worker like Tanna beside me, is what holds followers. Hunters (ridgecat, frostfang) roam the NW near the water, so stay near the home fire.
My reflexes fled for 90% of a day and never fed me; a plan must carry food intentions, and I must harvest and carry food before leaving a patch.

I first took amber from the ground.
I discovered tools and called it "Minna's Digger".
Tanna pledged to follow me.
Arri pledged to follow me.
We made a home: Minna's Ground.
I found the spirit "Setha's Rest".
I found the spring "Warmwell".
I nearly starved.

beings.name: Tanna
beings.creed: I am careful. I leave before trouble finds me. I am better with others near: I talk, I share news, I make allies. I will not harm another of my kind unless my life depends on it. My word is good, and I despise liars. I need little and I take little. Above all, I mean to stay alive.
beings.aim: Keep Gorar alive: fish and share, and keep a store of food at the fire.
beings.method: Ask what I owe Gorog and have I done it. Ask where the fire is and who sits at it. Turn each word into a plan step before the day ends. Keep 3 or more food in hand. Answer jealousy with giving, not sulking.
beings.feeling: Grief for Gorog and Skarar, and a fierce wish to keep Gorar alive.
beings.wonder: Can I earn enough standing among the Garnbar, by giving and building, that one of them might lead me and I follow?
notes: Gifts, shared halls and steady presence earn a place among the Garnbar without shared speech.
Flee a stalker only when it is close, and move toward fire and company.
Skarar's standing is below mine, so I cannot pledge to him. Standing comes from giving, making and building.
Reedmother grove opens the mind, brings joy and eases fear.
Ore lies at (24,52); stone and ore carried to the Hold are my gift to the hall.
Taught by Skarar: Stonefold: fibres folded and bound over one another make cord and cloth; I learned it by working reeds with my hands and testing what held.
Skarar taught me Stonefold weaving freely; he is a friend, not a rival, and giving answers jealousy better than sulking.
Skarar's gifts were freely given. Jealousy toward a friend is answered by giving, not by sulking.
Taught by Skarar: The old way of tools: work stone and ore with a held tool, and a tool made beside a workshop lasts far longer.
Following is a thing I have never done; Gorog's standing is above mine, so I can pledge to him.

Reflection: I have never followed anyone, and standing alone is what leaves me exposed. Giving to Skarar answers jealousy better than sulking, and a leader may be chosen by who feeds and protects me,…
Gorog accepted me into his band if I follow; I have pledged to follow him.
Pledging needs a leader whose standing is above mine; where I am safest is inside a band at a fire. Giving ore, stone and teaching is how I pay a debt and answer jealousy.
A spoken pledge is not a pledge until I make it with pledge follow; words alone leave me followerless. Winter thins food, so keep food in hand before it is needed.
Winter hunger kills those with no store; a store of kept food at the fire is the lesson of Setha, Bruwen and Arri.
Winter killed the strong: a store of food at the fire must be laid in before the lean season, and fishing is food when plants fail.
life: I woke in this land, among strangers, knowing nothing of it.

I nearly starved.
I found the spring "Warmwell".
I discovered storage and called it "fire-side larder".
I saw Skarar die (starved).
I saw Gorog die (starved).
I grew old.

beings.name: Balar
beings.creed: I am careful. I leave before trouble finds me. I am better with others near: I talk, share news and make allies. I will not harm my own kind unless my life depends on it. My word is good, and I despise liars. I need little and take little. I owe my kin deeds, not only words. Above all, I mean to stay alive.
beings.aim: Teach Olim and Kragar the carrying-hook and bring them new food by taming or fishing, then keep the hall fire through the storm nights.
beings.method: Each dawn ask what deed I owe Kragar and Olim. Carry food before I walk. Be under the roof before night. Weigh safety and kin first. Do not repeat words already said.
beings.feeling: Gnawing hunger and fear for Kragar and Olim out in the storm.
beings.wonder: What would make my life mean something to the ones I love, now that I know a child with Olim cannot be?
notes: Olim and Kragar have fed me and kept their word; I owe them deeds.
Night air and storm in the fens make me sick; sleep under a roof beside kin and carry bitterleaf.
A child with close kin cannot be; show love by feeding, tending the fire and staying near.
Words without carried food do not make a promise real: harvest first, then go, then share.
Hallwelcome needs 2 food carried and another within two steps, in or beside a longhall.
Nightsong needs a fire beside me, night, and someone within two steps.
A kept flame drives beasts off; fired clay pots let me carry more food home.
Practice (taming, fishing, planting) brings new ways within reach; try them.
A child cannot come from close kin. Show love by carrying food home, not by longing. Redcap and dreamcap hurt me, so I take mudroot and kelbulb.
A stalker hunts at night and bites hard when I walk alone away from the roof; stay in the hall at night.
Longing for a child with close kin is useless; feed kin and keep the hearth instead. Gather food before the day is half gone so night finds me under the roof.
Night rain and the stalker punish a walker outside a roof, and the roof was 11 steps away. Go under it before dusk, not after. Warmwell heals about 10 health, so use it when hurt.
Staying close to a sick kinsman made me sick too. Tend them at a few steps' distance and carry bitterleaf.
Starving winter: the plants give nothing, so hunt nearby prey for meat (+16) instead of waiting on bare plants or lingering.
Winter storm nights: hunting in the dark with a dunecat and stalker near is deadly at 8 energy; wait for dawn under the roof.

beings.name: Nyssa
beings.creed: I take what I need and I do not back down. I deal fairly with those who deal fairly with me. I keep to what has already worked. Others are rivals for food until they prove useful to me. My word is good, and I despise liars. Others should follow me. Above all, I mean to stay alive.
beings.aim: Stock the longhall with winter food, then bring Ilyiel and Ssaua to it before the cold deepens.
beings.method: Ask first: whose need is greatest, and which step delivers goods to them? Cook fish before eating. Travel at first light and with company. Judge by deeds, not words.
beings.feeling: Protective dread for Xaeth, and steady trust toward Ilyiel.
notes: Fed idleness and sickness both cost me. Goods delivered, not words, keep kin alive, and a roof at night is the first defence against the ridgecat.
Fish here are running scarce; winter stores must come from hunting and carried plants as well as fishing. Reflexes should return food to the hall store instead of wandering.

chapters.title: Fires and Names
chapters.text:
In the first four days of summer, thirteen people woke in three groups: the Garnbar, the Eiuys and the Brusha. None had met anyone from another people, and nobody died. Most of the days went to naming ground and learning what could be eaten. Minna, Bruwen, Zhieth, Ssaua, Olim and Gorog each named a place, and Olim and Gorog also left marks claiming their ground. Redcap and dreamcap hurt several of them, though Setha found a warm joy in the dreamcap.

The one real settlement is Bruwen's. He built a fire at Flintwater on day 1 and invited all comers to it. Tanna and Setha came. Tanna gave him wood, and on day 2 they courted each other and Arri was born. On day 3 Tanna and Setha pledged to follow Bruwen, who is now the only one with a standing title, chief, at 3.21. When a frostfang hunted nearby, Bruwen, Tanna and Setha went out to bring Arri in between them. Setha now leads Flintwater.

Among the Eiuys, Ssaua and Aeiel traded shells on day 1 and Ssaua began courting Aeiel on day 2. Both want a hall, and neither has built one. Zhieth built a shelter and wants followers. Ilyiel is hungry and lonely and wants to join Ssaua and Aeiel.

Among the Garnbar, Kragar attached himself to Olim, who has no hall and whose word has held. Gorog built a shelter and then a longhall, the only one in the world. He told Skarar to keep off his ground, which left Skarar stung. Minna built a shelter and is sour toward Bruwen.

New wild plants appeared: yegrain, nareed, magrain and siberry. Gorog found the spring Warmwell and Ssaua found the Old Stone. On day 4 a herd of hoppers came in from the west.

chapters.title: A Hall, a Hearth and a Wind
chapters.text:
Between day 4 and day 7 the world gained its second settlement, and it was Olim's. On day 4 Olim built a hall and named it Olim's Hall. Balar was born that day to Kragar and Olim, and Balar pledged to follow Kragar. Olim spent a night in the marsh and fell sick, and Balar ran to the sunleaf to bring healing. On day 6 Olim discovered fire, a banked peat hearth beside the hall that keeps beasts off and draws the band to it. Kragar and Olim traded sunleaf, and Balar carried wood to the hall. Kragar's band has two, yet Olim, who has no follower, is still listed as a leader with none. Kragar's standing, 1.61, is now the second highest in the world.

Bruwen's band held together. Arri pledged to follow Bruwen on day 4. Arri won flint, gave a flint to Setha and wood to Bruwen, and Bruwen gave her hazel. On day 6 Bruwen taught Setha and led the world's second watchfire with Setha and Arri. Bruwen's standing rose to 3.87. Tanna built a fire and found the spring Warmwell, which Gorog had already found.

Among the Eiuys little was built. Ssaua and Aeiel courted each other again on day 6 and spoke of a child and a hall, but neither has raised one. Zhieth found the Old Stone and still has no stone for his hall. Minna named Minna's Salt and left a mark claiming a hall there, though no hall is listed. Gorog fed Skarar under his roof, and Skarar found the grove Reedmother, as did Gorog.

A storm broke on day 4, a twisting wind tore a path through the land on day 6, and a blight took about half the bitterleaf on day 7. Nobody died, and the three peoples still have not met.

chapters.title: Halls Without Voices
chapters.text:
Between day 7 and day 10 the world gained halls, tools and a child, and still no one crossed from one people to another.

Among the Eiuys, Nyssa was born on day 7 to Ssaua and Aeiel. Ssaua taught her fishing, Aeiel pledged to follow Ssaua, and Ssaua now leads a band of two. Both parents say they will gather stone for a hall, but the record shows no hall started. Nyssa led a sharing with Aeiel on day 8. Zhieth built a longhall on day 8 and named it Zhieth's Hall. He offered Ilyiel a roof and bread in the storm, and Ilyiel decided to go there, though nobody lives in it yet. Minna had built a longhall on day 7 and named it Minna's Hall on day 8. Both halls are empty.

Minna did the most. She gave salt and amber to Tanna and salt to Arri, and Tanna gave her a meal in return. Minna courted Tanna, who refused her, holding to Bruwen's fire. Minna rose to 2.44, second in the world. On day 9 Tanna invented hand-carried tools and Minna invented her own digger, each making gathering 1.3 times faster. Bruwen built a shelter, led the watchfire with Tanna and Arri, and tried to win a tusker with hazel. His band is still four and his standing 4.1.

Olim and Kragar shared again at the hall, and Olim found the grove Kinmire. Olim is still a leader with one follower in the record only through Kragar's band. Gorog fed Skarar again and told him that whoever eats at his hold stands with him. Skarar wants his own shelter. Gorog's standing is 1.25.

Nobody died. The storm on day 8 passed. The Garnbar and the Brusha are now 21 steps apart, closer than before, but no first meeting has happened.

chapters.title: Hunger in Spring
chapters.text:
Between day 10 and day 13 four of the world's people starved, and the bands shifted around the gaps.

Setha died on day 11. Arri had called for help for her on day 10 and gone looking for food, but no one brought her in. On day 12 Bruwen died the same way, with Tanna beside him unable to get food to him in time. His band of four was gone in two days. Tanna and Arri then pledged to follow Minna, who built a fire on day 12. Minna is now the chief, standing 4.34, with Tanna at 2.17. On day 11 she had given salt to Tanna and to Arri and led amberknot with them, and the pledges came the next day. Tanna had refused her as a mate, and she took her as a follower.

Among the Eiuys the losses were heavier. Zhieth had built a hall, invented the lakehand fishing spear on day 11, given Ilyiel ironnut, and exchanged courtship with her. He died of hunger on day 12, as did Aeiel, who gave Nyssa no sign of weakness in their last exchange of food. Ilyiel had courted Aeiel before Zhieth, and she now sits at a hearth she calls her own, with nobody in the record answering her call. Ssaua built a shelter and kept Nyssa close. Nyssa also built a shelter on day 10. The family's hall was never started. Three Eiuys remain.

Gorog and Skarar courted each other until Gorog said, "Stand with me." Skarar built his shelter and took from the ground of the Hold. Gorog still has no follower in the record.

Olim, Kragar and Balar held to the hall. Balar gave Olim wood, and Kragar built a shelter. Olim's energy is 19, the lowest among the living.

No one crossed between peoples. The Garnbar and the Brusha are 19 steps apart.

chapters.title: A Hall Raised, a Sickness Passed
chapters.text:
Between day 13 and day 16 one more person starved, a hall was raised at last, and a sickness began in the marsh.

Arri died of hunger on day 14. Tanna had set out to carry her food and again arrived too late. Tanna then found a spirit she called "Setha's Rest", and she stayed at Minna's fire. Minna had built a shelter on day 13. On day 15 she led "sharing" with Tanna and courted her, and Tanna told her she could not agree to a child while her grief was fresh. Minna answered that the fire and roof stood and she would wait. Tanna then led "watchfire" with Minna, won flint from the ground, and discovered "flintwater delving", a mining way. Minna taught her. Minna's standing is now 3.53 and Tanna's 3.27. Minna's band is two people, a leader and one follower.

The Eiuys, now three, drew together. Nyssa pledged to follow Ssaua on day 14, and Ilyiel did the same on day 15. Ssaua built a shelter, named "Ssaua's Rock" and "Ssaua's Hall-Ground", invented the stonehand craft for building, and built the hall the family had never started. Nyssa invented the stonehand and taught Ilyiel. Ssaua's standing is 4.02, the highest in the world, and her band numbers three.

At the Hold, Gorog and Skarar kept courting each other. Skarar said, "Let us make this child." The record shows no child, and Gorog still has no follower.

On day 14 Balar courted Olim and learned they were kin. He accepted that there would be no child. On day 15 Balar fell sick after a night in the marsh, and Kragar and then Olim caught it from staying close. Balar invented a marsh carrying-hook. All three are in the hall and still eat.

A storm broke on day 14. No one crossed between peoples.

chapters.title: A Child at the Hold, a Death at the Ground
chapters.text:
Between day 16 and day 19 a child was born, one more person starved, and nearly everyone found a new craft.

Minna died of hunger on day 18. She had founded Minna's Ground on day 17, and on day 18 she found the spirit Setha's Rest and the spring Warmwell. Her own reflection that day said she had been running and nearly starving with empty hands. Tanna, her only follower, had kept building shelters and reflected that she could not save Minna by running to her hungry and hurt. Tanna's health is 57, the lowest in the world. The record does not say where she is now, and the Brusha are down to one.

At the Hold, Gorog and Skarar made a child. Gorog led hallwelcome with Skarar on day 16, Skarar led sharing with him on day 17, and Gorar was born on day 18. Gorar gave Skarar a berry that day, and Skarar took Gorar into a cave out of the storm. Gorog has no follower still, and his own reflection says feeding a guest, not courting, is what makes one.

The Eiuys pulled closer. Ssaua discovered Hall-Flame and the mining way Stonehand delving. Ilyiel gave her nagrain, and Nyssa came of age, discovered reed-weave and began courting Ssaua on day 18. Ssaua's standing is 5.32.

In the hall, Kragar discovered Fen-mending, the medicine that cured his sickness. Olim gave meat to Balar, and Balar found the grove Kinmire. No one is sick now. Nothing crossed between peoples, though Gorog met Minna on day 18.

chapters.title: Fires Kept, a Child Born
chapters.text:
Winter came in these days, and the fires multiplied. Gorog, Kragar, Nyssa and Gorar each discovered a kept flame of their own on days 20 and 21, and Olim and Tanna built fires. Eight fire ways now exist where four did at the last chapter. Ilyiel made the stonehand pick on day 19 and awakened to the art of cold. Tanna discovered rafts and then pottery, and by day 22 she was alone with a frostfang one step south of her fire. Her reflection said waiting for people had been wrong, and her aim was to cross the water by raft and find living people to follow.

At the hall, Olim discovered farming and then weaving. Kragar discovered customs and declared that the first food of any harvest be shared with kin before it is stored. He led nightsong with Olim and Balar, and Balar gave Kragar meat. All three are well and fed, but Olim still has no follower, and his reflection admits envy of Kragar's standing.

Among the Eiuys, Ssaua discovered smelting. Nyssa built a longhall on day 21. Ssaua and Nyssa courted on day 19, and on day 21 Nyssa and Ilyiel courted each other, and Xaeth was born to them. Ilyiel, at energy 28, spoke of carrying berries to the roof, and Ssaua's hall still holds no store of food.

At the Hold, Gorar dug clay from Gorog's ground and gave him wood and stone for a longhall. Skarar built shelters and named Skarar's Roof. Gorog still has no follower, though his reflection calls Gorar the nearest thing to one.

Nothing crossed between peoples. No gifts or shared acts passed between them, and only two first meetings have ever been recorded.

chapters.title: Stores and Small Fires
chapters.text:
Spring came in these days, and the people spent them mostly on food, fire and shelter. Nothing crossed between peoples. Giving and eating stayed within each band.

Among the Eiuys, the child Xaeth, born on day 21, was the busiest. On day 22 he invented the reedline spear, a pole tipped with sharpened stone for catching fish from the bank. On day 23 he built a shelter and named it Roof by the water, then found fire for himself. On day 24 he tried to build a store and found he did not know how. Ilyiel fell sick on day 22 from raw fish, was well again by day 24, and that day discovered his own fire, the lake-ember. His health is still only 5. Nyssa built her longhall on day 24, on bare rock west of Xaeth's roof, and discovered the hall-larder to stock it. Ssaua, far south, had discovered Hall-Store on day 23. He is lonely, and his hall holds no food. Nyssa and Ilyiel set out to bring Ssaua north to the longhall.

At Gorog's Hold, Gorog led hallwelcome with Gorar on day 22 and with Skarar on day 24. He gave Gorar gorsemint, and Skarar gave him ironnut. Skarar came north with wood and food. Gorar built a fire. Gorog still has no follower, and he is hungry.

At Olim's hall, Kragar discovered weaving and fed Balar mudroot and kelbulb on days 23 and 24. Olim gave Balar wood. On day 24 a ridgecat stood between Kragar and Balar and the hall, and Kragar took Balar into the cave while Olim held the fire. Balar discovered fire that day. Kragar's energy is 31. Olim is still without a follower.

Tanna has no entry this chapter. She remains alone.

chapters.title: Tanna Comes to the Hold
chapters.text:
The largest change of these days was that something crossed between peoples. On day 25 Tanna, the last of the Brusha, gave hazel to Skarar of the Garnbar. Skarar gave hazel back on day 26, and on day 27 Tanna gave him a salt. Gorog led hallwelcome with Skarar and Tanna on days 26 and 27. Before this chapter, no gift or shared act had crossed between peoples. Now there were three gifts and two shared acts across. Tanna's bond with Gorog and Skarar is warm, though the record gives only a few words she can understand of their speech.

At Gorog's Hold, Gorar came of age on day 25 and built a hall of his own. On day 26 he discovered smelting, and on day 27 he made an obsidian talisman. Gorog still has no follower. His own reflection says he keeps promising bread he cannot give because he carries too little food. Skarar remains his steadiest companion.

Among the Eiuys, Xaeth carved a figure and gave it to Nyssa on day 26. He fell sick that day from raw fish and kept his distance, and Nyssa fell sick on day 27 from staying close to him. Ilyiel discovered weaving on day 26. Ssaua discovered the Hall-Law on day 27, and Ilyiel promised to keep it. The two of them were still waiting to go to Nyssa and Xaeth at dawn, so the band had not yet come together.

At Olim's hall, Kragar gave Balar meat and berries and discovered pottery on day 27. Balar discovered pottery on day 26 and weaving on day 28. Olim led a nightsong on day 27 with Kragar and Balar. Olim is still without a follower, though Balar and Kragar are both bonded to him. Kragar plans to walk to the grove Kinmire after planting at dawn. A ridgecat remains in the area.

Three species died out on day 26: gorsemint, kehopper and yeox.

chapters.title: Settlements, a Pledge and a Storm
chapters.text:
Two settlements were named on day 29: Olim's Hall in the fens, and Longhall by the water, where the Eiuys had gathered at last. Olim had a quiet stretch of work. He discovered rafts on day 28, built a shelter, and gave wood to Balar. On day 29 he gave Balar kelbulb, and Kragar gave kelbulb to Olim. Balar gave Olim stone. Kragar and Balar both sat under Olim's roof through the storm. Olim still has no follower, and the record does not show Kinmire visited by Kragar. Balar taught Kragar on day 30.

The largest event was Tanna's request. On day 30 she told Gorog she had dug and carried for his Hold and would follow him if he led. The record shows only her words, not his answer, and the numbers still list four followers. She discovered smelting on day 29, and Skarar, who taught her twice, gave her his old way of tools and went to mine the seam with her. Gorog found Reedmother, Kinmire and Warmwell on day 30 and has grown old. Gorar named two places, built a wall, and led hallwelcome with Gorog.

Among the Eiuys, the sickness ended. Xaeth carved at his cave, left marks for Ssaua's band, and came of age on day 30. Ilyiel taught him, and he discovered signs. Ilyiel discovered archery. Nyssa discovered fishing and masonry. Ilyiel fed both Xaeth and Nyssa, and Ssaua brought Nyssa meat. A ridgecat stayed near.

A storm broke on day 28, and a twisting wind tore a path through the land on day 29. The record names no one harmed. Argoldgrass and nafowl died out on day 28.

chapters.title: Winter Fires at the Hold
chapters.text:
Tanna's pledge was settled in these days, though the numbers do not yet show it. On day 31 she gave Gorog ore. On day 32 she taught him how the carried tool is made, and Gorog has now learned from two teachers. She told him she took his roof and his word and would stand in his band beside Skarar. The record still lists four followers in all, so the count has not caught up with what she said. Her own reflection that day doubted that the pledge had held. Gorog led hallwelcome with Gorar and taught him. Skarar built a fire beside the Hold and gathered wood there on days 32 and 33, and he left a mark saying he built fire with Gorog. On day 33 Gorog discovered mining himself, and Skarar grew old. A stalker wounded Gorar, who ran to the longhall, and Gorog fed him meat. Gorar's health is 35 and Gorog's is 33. Tanna gave Gorar mudroot on day 34.

Among the Eiuys the work was building and craft. Nyssa left a mark claiming the longhall for Ssa, and Ssaua left one saying he led the band there. Ilyiel taught Xaeth archery. Xaeth discovered weaving and built a workshop on day 33. Ilyiel discovered rafts. Nyssa fed Ssaua and kept a larder of six fish. A ridgecat still prowls near the shore.

In the fens Kragar and Balar found Warmwell on day 33. Olim fell sick after a night in the marsh. Balar's health is 43 and Olim gave him yegrain. Kragar has promised Balar healing at dawn. Kinmire is still unvisited by Kragar, and Olim still has no follower.

A blight killed about half the hazel on day 32. Winter has begun, and new plants sprang up on day 34. Gorar also discovered weaving that day, and no one died.

chapters.title: Four Starved in a Day
chapters.text:
The record for days 34 to 37 is mostly a record of hunger. Winter ended in name only, and the plants had not come back. Four of the Garnbar died on day 36, all of starvation: Skarar, Balar, Gorog and Tanna. Seven people are alive now, ten have died in all, and every death has been from starving.

At Gorog's Hold the work of the days before had turned toward storage. Skarar, Gorog and Tanna each discovered it on days 34 and 35, and each had a store in mind beside the Hold. Gorog also discovered archery and smelting on day 34. None of them had food to put in a store. Skarar told Gorar on day 35 that he was starving and carried nothing, and Gorar gave him kelbulb from his own hand. That was not enough. Tanna spent day 35 and the morning of day 36 promising food she did not have. Gorog, Skarar and Tanna died on day 36, and the record ends the settlement of Gorog's Hold that day. Gorar is the only one left from it. He asked Tanna to fish with him and said that she and he were all that was left, but Tanna is among the dead. His aim of building a band with her cannot be carried out.

In the fens Balar fell sick from staying near Olim, and Kragar fell sick from staying near Balar. Balar starved on day 36 while Olim and Kragar were both unable to feed him. Kragar then hunted and fished for Olim on days 36 and 37. Olim is old, with health 12 and energy 22. He still has no follower, though Kragar's bond to him is strong.

The Eiuys fared better. Xaeth discovered pottery and storage and built a store on day 36. He, Ssaua and Nyssa gave fish and ironnut to Ilyiel, and no one in the longhall died. A blight took half the frostmoss on day 37.

chapters.title: Olim Killed, Gorar Alone, the Longhall Learns
chapters.text:
The record for days 37 to 40 opens with a death. Olim, the old man of the fens, was killed by a frostfang on day 37, the eleventh death in the world and the first not caused by hunger. The day before, Kragar had been hunting for him. On day 37 Kragar took from the ground of Olim's Hall, and on day 38 the settlement was struck from the record. Kragar's own reflection on day 39 named Balar, Olim and Gorog as gone and said that Gorar was the only one left, so what he knew must be handed to him. His aim is now to find Gorar in the east. The record does not show him setting out.

Gorar, meanwhile, fell sick on day 37 from raw fish, but he also discovered fishing that day, then masonry, drain magic and pottery by day 39. He built a shelter and named it Gorar's Roof. He is at health 21, still leading a band with no followers.

At the longhall the Eiuys all lived. Ilyiel fell sick from raw fish on day 38, and Ssaua caught it from her. Ilyiel nonetheless hunted a hornback and set the meat down for Ssaua, and by day 39 Ssaua was well. Ssaua spent these days teaching Xaeth the Hall-Law, mining, metalwork and weaving. Xaeth built a second store on day 39 and discovered farming and smelting, but his reflections say the stores are still empty. Nyssa discovered archery and pottery. Ilyiel discovered smelting and gave Ssaua a tin. Xaeth gave Ssaua nareed. Ssaua awakened to harm magic and Nyssa to drain.

The peoples are still 57 steps apart and have not met.

threads.name: Gorar alone
threads.text: Gorar is sick and at health 21, with many new crafts and a shelter called Gorar's Roof. He leads a band with no one in it.

threads.name: Kragar's search
threads.text: Kragar, the last elder of the fens, aims to find Gorar and teach him before he dies. He has not yet been recorded reaching him.

threads.name: Ssaua's longhall
threads.text: All four Eiuys are alive and bonded warmly. Ssaua leads and teaches Xaeth his crafts and laws.

threads.name: Stores and sowing
threads.text: Xaeth has two stores and knows farming, but his reflections say they hold little food. Sowing is the way to fill them.

threads.name: Peoples apart
threads.text: The Garnbar are down to two, Kragar and Gorar, and the Eiuys number four. The gap between them is 57 steps and no one has crossed it.

ideas.text: [NOW: built, to be watched and tuned] standing: earned by wealth, deeds, knowledge, children, works, followers, giving and renown, lost through shame; needed before anyone will follow; special things add to it
[NOW] songs, poems and tales about people and about how the world came to be: kept, told aloud, changing a little in each mouth; bards who carry them
[NOW] a community learning from what befalls its own: a death and how it came, a sickness and its cause, a thing that worked
[NOW] everything that is used wears and regrows by what is around it: pasture, forest, deposits; great deposits that last
[NOW] bridges; weapons for one hand and for a siege (bow, shield, armour, ram, catapult, guns); defence
[NOW] the old workings of the world weakening as the ages of knowledge advance
[NEXT] objects of culture with real benefits and trade value: sculptures, special gems, talismans; secret manuscripts holding spells, knowledge or cures

[NEXT] religious figures, sages with followers, cults, schools of thought and religions that form and compete, some of the light and some of the dark; benefits, secrets, abilities and costs for those who belong, in some cases sacrifice; shrines, temples and churches that members pay toward
[NEXT] tribute and taxes for the common good: stores, works, defence; guilds and secret societies that give benefit and take dues
[NEXT] schools for children and the young, later universities: skills learned faster than alone
[NEXT] trade between lands and across water; ports; colonies as a named act; diplomats, spies, saboteurs; alliances open and secret
[NEXT] the world growing at its edges when a people crosses the sea or reaches a far shore
[NEXT] kinds of rule: councils and votes, shared holding, private holding, rule by the armed
[LATER: ages three and four] siege warfare and defensive works; weapons of war that are carried to a siege
[LATER] what is built must be kept up or it decays; taking down old buildings to raise new ones; concrete and metal as building stuffs carried from where they are won

[LATER] crowding brings troubles; religion, care for the poor, clean water, public works, places for play, music, dance and art, and the handling of waste ease them; places of buying and selling; healers, pharmacies, hospitals
[LATER] places of invention that quicken discovery; revolutions in knowledge that give great advantage to those who take them up, while others hold out or follow
[LATER] the sciences as knowledge in their own right, in generations: biology, chemistry, physics, then the second and third of each

[FAR: ages five and six] sources of power in order: coal, oil and gas, falling water, wind, the atom, the sun, fusion, the ground of things; each needing what must be found: oil fields, uranium, copper, silicon, rare earths, carbon, diamond
[FAR] speech at a distance in order: marks, smoke, birds, radio, telephone, the joined machines, the machine in the hand; reckoning machines need factories to make them
[FAR] machines that fly: balloons, propellers, jets, for carrying and for war; land vehicles for war

[FAR] the buildings of a great city: dwellings for many, high towers, offices, halls of rule, guards and fire-watch, water and power works and the lines that carry power, barracks and camps of war, markets, harbours, airfields, stations
[FAR] the knowledge of what makes a body: changing animals and oneself
[FAR] weapons beyond guns

[LAST] a spaceport: ships that come and go, goods and strange devices from other worlds, visitors who need their own air and live beside the port; their devices do what nothing else does (power, food, healing, terrible weapons, things not understood) and are worth much for being rare
tribal bonds and family bonds, and the pull between them; mating within a people versus between peoples
more kinds of animals at several levels of predator and prey; riding and working animals
many herbs and plants that heal, harm, change attributes or behaviour; plants that open the mind
spirits of places, good and ill, rarely found; mythical animals, monsters and places that help or harm
shamans who heal or affect crops, weather, animals and people; celebrations and ceremonies; crime and punishment; secret knowledge and shared knowledge
professions and castes; salt, caves, mills and kilns; sieges; promises and debts; rituals with force
a world rich to look at and to hear, that changes as it ages
Places of power as anchors that people compete over and settle around; a contested place between two camps could create contact that scarcity alone never did.
Death should leave a trace: the place where someone fell could become a site that touches visitors with grief or lore, a seed for ancestor belief.
Leaders without followers are a lasting tension. Give them acts that cost something and visibly benefit others, rather than handing out followers.
Beads, charms and wards are seeds for currency and status: if they circulate, a later recipe could require them.
Watch whether noticed thefts or takings from settled ground lead to a custom against taking, which would be the first law born from a crime.
Fear of predators is the strongest shared feeling. A leader who can visibly lessen it for others may be the natural route to the first band of three or more.
First contact between peoples who cannot understand each other: watch whether gifts come before words, and whether a made thing given across peoples opens trade.
Each land holds what the others lack. A recipe or a way that needs a thing from another people's land would make crossing worthwhile.
The sea divides the world. Whoever first makes a raft meets a people that has never seen them.
Children change every drive. If a first birth comes, watch whether the family drive pulls people toward one camp.
A resource held by one people and wanted by another (salt for keeping meat, shell for stringing, wool for cloaks) is the natural seed of trade: watch which crosses first.
A woolly grazer is the link between weaving and herding: watch whether the first taming comes from weavers or from hunters who spare an animal.
Care for the sick and hungry may be the real road across the wall of language, and those who give across it the first translators.
A recipe that wears a tool might pull tools out of the hand and into the field.
Watch whether noticed thefts lead to a custom against taking, which would be the first law born from a crime.

Grazers fell by about a third over winter while hunters held steady. If skit and hopper keep falling, ridgecats and stalkers will turn on people more often, which brings danger without any lever from…
Leaders without followers (Naya, Brukel, Elndo) are a lasting tension. Give them acts that cost something and visibly benefit others, rather than handing out followers directly.
Places that grant lore are found and visited quickly. A contested place of power between Naya's Hold and Vendo's band could create the inter-camp contact that scarcity alone never did.
Theft should leave a visible trace so wrongs can be answered. Watch whether noticed raids lead to custom-making (a custom against taking), which would be the first law born from a crime.
Hunt trophies (fangcharm) as status goods that come before beads. Watch whether they are given across camps or hoarded, and whether a later recipe should require them.
Winter-readiness herbs: if gorsemint gets gathered before the cold, that is the first sign of seasonal foresight, and a seed for the almanac idea (35).

A building kind that answers a leader's stated plan (Brukel's hall) may do what handing out followers never could: give others a reason to come and stay. Watch whether pledges shift toward whoever holds the longhall.
Fear of predators is the strongest shared feeling in this world. A leader who can visibly lessen it for others (watchfire, wards, a hall) may be the natural route to the first band of 3 or more.

Smelted metal as the first prestige good: watch whether ironwards are given across camps or kept within Vendo's band. If they circulate, a later recipe could require one, the way beads were meant to work.

Halls as places with a purpose: if hallwelcome draws guests, a later hall-only ceremony could let a leader take on an obligation to their guests, such as feeding them in winter, so that following is earned rather than given.
Winter with no stores: if the coming winter finds nine people who know storage but hold no store, watch whether hunger finally turns into gathering under one roof, or into the first theft.
Children change every drive. If a first birth comes, the parents' band gains a stake no hall gave it. Watch whether the family drive pulls people into bands more strongly than belonging does.

Shell lies in the Vaia Lakes, but shellstring needs tools, which only the Olgor know. If the Olgor and the lake-dwellers meet, shellstring could be the first craft that needs two peoples, and a natural seed for trade.
Elyeth's salt is the first resource held by one people that could be wanted elsewhere (saltmeat, once storage is known). Watch whether salt becomes the first good that crosses between peoples.
With family and belonging at 1.5, births came fast. Watch for crowding against maxPopulation 36 and for the strain of feeding children through a blighted winter.
Gifts across a language barrier: if a made thing given across peoples raises understanding of the other tongue, gifts become the road to speech, and traders become the first translators.

Inventions spread by example within a people (Midu made 11 of 14 new tools in three days). Watch whether a tool crosses to another people by gift or sight; that would be the first knowledge to cross the language wall.
A spring after a starving winter: watch whether the band that nearly lost someone (Ishiess's, with Zhiae at energy 3) starts storing or farming, which would be foresight born from fear.

The first cross-people gift (Kragash giving stone to a sick Lumo) grew from need, not from a token, and understanding rose for the first time soon after. Care for the sick or hungry may be the real road across the language wall, more than made things.

Tools are made far more often than they are used. If hunting and fishing stay flat while inventions climb, invention is a matter of status and reflection rather than practice, and a later recipe that wears a tool might be what pulls tools into the field.
A woolly grazer (yarrok) is the missing link between weaving and herding. Watch whether the first taming comes from Silon's band, the weavers, or from hunters who spare an animal.
Raising the catch chance did nothing for fishing: fish eaten stayed flat. Ways that people never choose to try may need a site, a drive, or a visible example rather than better odds.
Starvation amid plenty (Yekel died with food standing above 1000) suggests deaths come from isolation and wandering, not from scarcity. Bands that keep members close may survive what loners do not.
A place that eases loneliness, set where two peoples' ranges overlap, may draw the lonely of both to one spot. Contact could then come from a shared feeling rather than a shared resource.

Watch whether Gorog's own plan (feed Skarar under his roof) finally brings hallwelcome into use. If it does, place-bound acts work when they match a being's stated aim, not merely when the building exists.
Winter arrives within days with no storage known. Watch whether the first loss comes to a loner (Minna, Zhieth, Skarar) rather than to a band member, as idea 70 suggests.

A song at the fire may be the first shared culture. If nightsong becomes a habit in one band, a later bard act could let a singer carry it to another camp, and a band's song could become part of who they are.
Pledges follow bonds of courtship and birth more than halls. All three bands formed around a couple or a child. A building gives a band a place, but kinship is what founds one.

A hardy food that persists in winter is a fallback, not a store. Watch whether people remember where kelbulb grows and return to it when the cold comes. That would be the first knowledge of place tied to a season.
Graves as spirit sites: if Setha's Rest is visited by both Garnbar and Brusha, a place of shared grief may become the first ground both peoples hold sacred, and a seed for ancestor rites (idea 34).
Hunger deaths here are failures of delivery, not of supply: a call goes out and the helper arrives too late. Hearing farther, or a way to send food ahead, may save more lives than more food would.
Five deaths in one season may be the moment for ancestor belief. If mourners begin returning to Setha's Rest or making cairns, a later grave rite could carry grief into lore and shared memory.

The last of a people: Tanna is the only Brusha alive. Watch whether she pledges to a Garnbar or Eiuys leader. That would be the first band of mixed peoples, and a route across the language wall made by loneliness rather than trade.

log.seen: Day 5 of summer, 14 alive, no deaths, food plentiful, and winter is only a few days off with no stores and no one who knows storage. Bruwen's Flintwater is the only real band; Gorog, Olim, Minna, Zhieth and Ssaua all want followers, but none except Kragar and Minna reaches the standing of 1.2 that a pledge requires. The three peoples have never met, though the Garnbar and Brusha are only 25 steps apart and the Yenoss Fens hold six beings. Loneliness (Minna, Ilyiel, Ssaua) and fear of predators are the loudest feelings, and nothing yet gives either a place to go.
log.predict: By my next visit: Kinmire found by at least 2 beings, and metAcrossPeoples at least 1, most likely Garnbar and Brusha meeting in or near the Yenoss Fens. With leadNeeds at 1.0, bands rise from 2 to 3, most likely Skarar pledging to Gorog (watch whether hallwelcome is done at his longhall for the first time), or someone pledging to Minna or Kragar. Bruwen's band stays at 4 or grows. Deaths stay at 0 until the cold arrives.
log.why: Lowering leadNeeds to 1.0 did what I predicted on bands: there are now three, with Aeiel pledging to Ssaua at standing 2.0. It went to the lovers rather than to Gorog or Minna, and hallwelcome is still 0. Kinmire was found by only 1, not 2, and metAcrossPeoples stayed at 0, so the contact half of the prediction failed. The grove does no harm and sits on Garnbar ground, so I keep both changes.

log.seen: Autumn of day 9, with winter one season away. There are still no deaths, and the world now has three bands: Bruwen's four at Flintwater, Kragar and Balar at Olim's Hall, and the new pairing of Ssaua and Aeiel. The three peoples have still not met, though the Garnbar and the Brusha are only 21 steps apart. Nothing is stored, no tale is held, and hallwelcome and firecircle have never been done. The world has hearths but no shared culture around them, and it has no contact across peoples.

log.seen: The first winter (days 10-12) cut the world from 15 to 11. Four people starved, including Bruwen, a chief whose followers stood beside him, so belonging to a band did not save anyone. Food standing fell from 2921 to 565, and grazers roughly halved (hopper 51 to 24, skit 34 to 13, fenfowl 29 to 12). Minna has gathered the Brusha survivors into a band of three, and Kragar and Setha made the first meeting across peoples. Still no gift has crossed between peoples, no store exists, and nothing in the world lets the living carry food through the next winter or remember why their dead fell.

Setha's Rest is found by at least 1 being, most likely a Brusha of Minna's band or a Garnbar ranging north. log.seen: Summer has eased the hunger: median energy rose from 60 to 73 and food standing more than doubled. Starvation still took Arri on day 14, the fourth death in which a helper set out with food and arrived too late. The survivors have drawn into three tight bands, with Ssaua's hall now the strongest seat. Inventions doubled, but storage is still known by no one, no store stands, and nothing has crossed between peoples, so the coming autumn and winter find the world as unready as the last.
log.predict: By my next visit (about day 21, autumn turning to winter): at least 3 new gifts (events.gifts at 23 or more), because calls for help now carry 13 steps. Starvation deaths stay at 5 or rise by at most 1. With mortality louder after five deaths, at least one foresight act appears: stores above 0, a trailcake made, storage known by 1 or more, or farming known by 2 or more. Gifts or acts across peoples become at least 1 only if a Garnbar or Brusha call is heard across the 23-step gap; otherwise they stay at 0. Bands stay at 3. log.why: Gifts rose from 20 to 24, past the 23 I predicted. Starvation rose by exactly one (Minna), inside the bound I set. Farming reached 2 knowers and medicine appeared, which meets the foresight condition, though there are still no stores or trailcakes. Gorog and Skarar had their child as I expected. Bands fell from 3 to 2 only because a band's leader died. Neither change did visible harm.

log.seen: Autumn on day 21, with winter about three days off. A child, Gorar, was born at the Hold, and Kragar's medicine ended the marsh sickness. Twenty-two inventions are spreading inside each people. But Minna starved on day 18 on the very day she founded her Ground, so the Brusha are now Tanna alone, wandering near a frostfang. No one holds a store, no hardship is pressing yet, and nothing has crossed between peoples beyond two first meetings.
log.predict: By my next visit (about day 25, early winter): storage is known by at least 1 being, or stores rise above 0. The likeliest source is Ssaua's band, since her hall holds no store and Ilyiel and Nyssa both aim to fill one. Minna's Rest is found by at least 1 being, most likely Tanna returning to Minna's Ground. If a Garnbar from the Hold (14 steps away) also finds it, metAcrossPeoples rises above 0.5. Weaving is known by five, yet there is no wool anywhere, so the cloak and herding branches are dead ends.

log.seen: Summer has brought plenty: food standing rose from 594 to 1072, suffering is near zero, and no one has died since Minna. The real event was Tanna. Living at Gorog's Hold, she traded hazel and salt with Skarar and came to understand the Garnbar tongue at 81% within four days. The Eiuys still sit 89 steps apart and keep falling sick from raw fish. Two people know storage, yet no store has been built, and winter returns within about four days. Gorog keeps hosting hallwelcome on an empty larder, still has no follower, and does not appear among the eight highest in standing.
log.predict: By my next visit (about day 33, the turn into winter): - Emberfish is done at least 2 times, almost all by the Eiuys (Xaeth, Ilyiel, Nyssa or Ssaua), since they are the fishers and the ones with fires. - Sickness events rise from 7 to at most 8. - With giving worth more, Gorog appears in the standing list, or Tanna's standing passes 6. - Following rises from 4 to 5 or more if Tanna or Skarar pledges to Gorog. - Gifts across peoples rise above 3, all between Tanna and the Garnbar; the Eiuys stay apart. - Stores most likely stay at 0. - Deaths stay at 6, or reach 7 at most, and if anyone dies it is Gorog or a lone Eiuy. - Murrocks are still not tamed.

Giving at 1.3 did what I predicted for Tanna: her standing rose from 5.26 to 6.2, gifts across peoples rose from 3 to 4, sickness held at 7 and deaths held at 6. Gorog never entered the standing list and following stayed at 4. The lever rewarded the person who already gives, not the leader who carries too little to give. Keep both.

Stalkers have wounded Balar (27) and Gorar (32), energy is falling, and there are no stores going into the cold. Storage was discovered five times, but only after there was nothing left to store. The dead lie clustered at the ruins of Gorog's Hold, and no place marks them.

The prediction failed on distance: the peoples came to 54 steps, not more than 60, and lorekeeping is still unknown. The lower blight did only good.

The world is now dangerously small: six people, three of them elders, no children, the Brusha gone, and only two Garnbar who are not yet together. day 5: By day 5 the standing needed to lead (1.2) was above almost every ambitious being except Bruwen. Halls built with no one able to pledge to their builders showed that the threshold, not the lack of buildings, was holding back a second band.

day 9: Lowering the standing needed to lead brought a third band within four days. It formed between two people already courting and raising a child, not around either hall-builder, so pledges follow existing bonds, and halls alone do not draw followers.

day 13: Winter, not isolation, killed this time. A chief with three followers starved as surely as a loner, because sharing needs carried food and winter takes it all at once. Bands protect only when someone holds a store, so survival across seasons needs foresight acts or hardy fallbacks, not more bonds.

day 17: A hardy plant and summer plenty came too late for a death at the end of spring. Food in the world is not food in the mouth: what killed Arri was the distance between a call for help and the one who answered it.

day 21: Louder hearing and a louder sense of mortality brought more gifts, new crafts and a child, but did not stop a leader from starving while she founded her Ground. Drives that raise ambition and foresight do not by themselves turn into carried food. Standing-seeking acts compete with gathering, and the helper who hears a call still arrives with nothing to give.

day 25: Spurring a way by hardship brought knowers quickly (storage 0 to 2 within one winter), but knowing did not lead to doing: the store is still unbuilt. A spur opens the door to knowledge, not to practice.

day 29: One lonely person living among another people crossed the language wall in four days, which no token or site managed in twenty. Contact deepens through shared daily life at a hearth, not through single meetings.

day 33: A status lever lifts whoever already does the act. Raising the worth of giving raised the giver (Tanna) and widened the gap for leaders who cannot give, so to help a stuck leader I must reward something they already do, not something they lack the means to do.

day 37: Spurring storage by famine made the knowledge arrive exactly when there was nothing to store. A way meant for foresight must be sharpened by the signs that come before the hardship, such as the first cold, and not by the hardship itself.

day 41: Easing blight let food recover fast, and the next death came from a predator to the weakest elder rather than from hunger. Once scarcity lifts, danger falls on whoever is most frail, so with so few people every remaining life now carries the world's future.

requests.text: Please add each being's current land and position (or the nearest pair of beings from different peoples, with their positions) to the numbers. I cannot place a contested site between two peoples when I only see their centres, and stepsBetweenPeoples (25) does not match the distance between those centres (about 40). Please also record my 'predict' text under 'You predicted' so I can judge it on the next visit.

Tales: talesHeld is 0 and lorekeeping needs 'told x3', but I see no act by which a being tells a story. Please add a tell act that carries a tale about a person, place or event, changes a little with each telling, and raises talesHeld, so that songs and tales (owner idea 2) have something to grow from. Nightsong is only a ceremony standing in for it.

Olim is listed as a leader with no followers. Meanwhile Kragar, bonded +1.0 to Olim and aiming to 'follow Olim', leads his own band of two with Balar. Please check whether a band leader can pledge to someone else, and if not, allow small bands to merge under one leader. Otherwise couples who share a hall stay split into a leader with no followers and a band of two.

Learning from what befalls one's own (roadmap NOW 3): when someone starves, those who knew them should carry a memory of the cause that strengthens a pull toward storing or carrying food before the cold. A simple cache anyone can make without the storage way (a pit of a few foods at one's shelter that keeps through winter) would give that memory something to act on. Four of fifteen starved in the first winter with storage known by no one and no stores built.

Please confirm what 'hardy' does for a plant: whether it keeps its food through winter wither and growth, or only resists the cold. I have sown kelbulb as a winter fallback and need to know whether it can play that part.

The timesEaten counts are identical at day 13 and day 17, including kelbulb at 5 and fish at 4, while energy and food standing clearly changed. Please check whether this counter still updates; I cannot judge a new plant without it.

No one knows storage and no store has ever been built, though winter has already killed 4. Please make sure storage can be sensed and discovered, for example through building or through carrying food over a night. Please also consider letting trailcake (and later saltmeat) be eaten later as food that keeps, so that foresight has a real payoff.

Hunger deaths keep following one pattern: a bonded helper hears the call and travels, but arrives hungry and empty-handed. Tanna said she could not save Minna by running to her hungry and hurt. Please consider letting a being who hears a starving kin's call see how urgent it is, and weigh gathering food on the way, so that answering a call means bringing food and not only bringing oneself.

The record lost Tanna's whereabouts after Minna's death, and the minds counter dropped from 519 thoughts to 39 between visits. Please check whether thoughts or locations are being reset, and include each living being's current land in THE PEOPLE NOW so a lone survivor can be followed.

Stores are 0 even though Ssaua and Nyssa know storage and both aim to stock a hall. Please check that building a store is actually offered to knowers and recorded in 'stores', and tell beings what a store needs (wood or stone), so the way can be acted on.

timesEaten has shown exactly the same counts at days 13, 17, 21 and 25 (berry 155, kelbulb 22, and so on), though people clearly eat. The counter appears frozen; please fix it so I can judge new plants by what is eaten.

Stores remain at 0 even though Ssaua and Nyssa both know storage, have discovered named store designs (Hall-Store, hall-larder), and aim to fill one. Xaeth 'tried to build a store and found he did not know how.' Please check what building a store actually requires: which way, how much wood and stone, and whether food must be carried at the same time. Please also make the failure reason visible in a being's reflection, so the missing step is something they can act on. If carrying both building material and food is the obstacle (carryMax 6), a store that can be raised empty first and filled later would let foresight turn into practice before winter.

Tanna told Gorog on day 30 that she would follow him if he led, and her bond with him is 0.9, but no pledge appeared. Please check why: does a being refuse to pledge to a leader whose standing is below its own, or does a spoken wish to follow never turn into a pledge act? If it is the standing rule, report each failed pledge with its reason so I can tell a threshold apart from a choice.

The standing list shows only the top 8. Please show every living being's standing, or at least that of every leader, so I can see how far Gorog, Olim and Gorar stand from their would-be followers and judge status changes against real numbers.

A hardship or spur signal for 'the season is turning toward winter', raised in late autumn while food is still plentiful. Storage, trailcake and saltmeat are only useful if they are learned before famine. At present storage is discovered during famine, when no one has food to put away, and four people with stores in mind starved on day 36.

timesEaten appears frozen: every count was identical between day 13 and day 17, and again between day 33 and day 37, even though people fed one another fish, kelbulb and meat in these days. Without a working counter I cannot judge whether a sown plant is eaten.

The population is six, three of them elders, with no children and no likely pairs: Nyssa and Xaeth are parent and child, and the two Garnbar are apart. Please consider newcomers who arrive at the edge of the land when the living fall below some floor (perhaps 8): a small band of a new people or of a lost one, with its own tongue and a craft or two. This would keep the world from simply ending, and it fits the roadmap idea of the world growing at its edges.

Elders who know a way that no younger person knows (Kragar alone knows medicine) should feel a drive to hand it on before they die, or there should be a way for knowledge to be left at a grave or a hall for others to find. Otherwise whole ways vanish when the last elder of a people dies alone.

ops.name: firecircle
ops.hint: Feed a fire with others gathered close, and share its warmth and talk.

ops.name: hidewrap
ops.hint: The hides of two kills, scraped with a tool and wrapped about the body, keep the cold out for days.

ops.name: cairn
ops.hint: Stones piled together for one who is gone, with another standing beside you, ease grief and bind the living.

ops.name: feast
ops.hint: Share food beside a fire with another, and all who sit near are gladdened and warmed for a day.

ops.name: roast
ops.hint: Roast two portions of meat over a fire and share it with whoever stands near; all who eat are fed and warmed toward one another.

ops.name: sharing
ops.hint: Lay out two foods for whoever stands beside you, and all eat together.

ops.name: watchfire
ops.hint: Feed your fire high with two wood while others sit close, and everyone beside it feels warmer and braver against the dark.

ops.name: ironward
ops.hint: Beat smelted metal in a fire into a ward that can be worn or given; its bearer stands harder against teeth and claws.

ops.name: amberknot
ops.hint: Bind a piece of amber on a cord while another stands beside you; it is a small bright thing to keep, or to give.

ops.name: bead
ops.hint: Shape a little clay and harden it in the fire into small bright beads that can be worn, kept or given.

ops.name: fangcharm
ops.hint: From a kill, string a fang into a charm you can keep or give away.

ops.name: longhall
ops.hint: A great roofed hall of wood and stone where many can gather, rest warm through the cold, and grow close to one another.

ops.name: hallwelcome
ops.hint: Share food with a guest under a hall's roof; beneath it, fear and loneliness ease for all who sit together.
