ideas: Places of power as anchors that people compete over and settle around; a contested place between two camps could create contact that scarcity alone never did.
Death should leave a trace: the place where someone fell could become a site that touches visitors with grief or lore, a seed for ancestor belief.
Leaders without followers are a lasting tension. Give them acts that cost something and visibly benefit others, rather than handing out followers.
Beads, charms and wards are seeds for currency and status: if they circulate, a later recipe could require them.
Watch whether noticed thefts or takings from settled ground lead to a custom against taking, which would be the first law born from a crime.
Fear of predators is the strongest shared feeling. A leader who can visibly lessen it for others may be the natural route to the first band of three or more.
First contact between peoples who cannot understand each other: watch whether gifts come before words, and whether a made thing given across peoples opens trade.
Each land holds what the others lack. A recipe or a way that needs a thing from another people's land would make crossing worthwhile.
The sea divides the world. Whoever first makes a raft meets a people that has never seen them.
Children change every drive. If a first birth comes, watch whether the family drive pulls people toward one camp.
A resource held by one people and wanted by another (salt for keeping meat, shell for stringing, wool for cloaks) is the natural seed of trade: watch which crosses first.
A woolly grazer is the link between weaving and herding: watch whether the first taming comes from weavers or from hunters who spare an animal.
Care for the sick and hungry may be the real road across the wall of language, and those who give across it the first translators.
A recipe that wears a tool might pull tools out of the hand and into the field.
Watch whether noticed thefts lead to a custom against taking, which would be the first law born from a crime.

Places that grant lore are found and visited quickly. A contested place of power between Naya's Hold and Vendo's band could create the inter-camp contact that scarcity alone never did.
Theft should leave a visible trace so wrongs can be answered. Watch whether noticed raids lead to custom-making (a custom against taking), which would be the first law born from a crime.
Hunt trophies (fangcharm) as status goods that come before beads. Watch whether they are given across camps or hoarded, and whether a later recipe should require them.
Winter-readiness herbs: if gorsemint gets gathered before the cold, that is the first sign of seasonal foresight, and a seed for the almanac idea (35).

A building kind that answers a leader's stated plan (Brukel's hall) may do what handing out followers never could: give others a reason to come and stay. Watch whether pledges shift toward whoever holds the longhall.
Fear of predators is the strongest shared feeling in this world. A leader who can visibly lessen it for others (watchfire, wards, a hall) may be the natural route to the first band of 3 or more.

Smelted metal as the first prestige good: watch whether ironwards are given across camps or kept within Vendo's band. If they circulate, a later recipe could require one, the way beads were meant to work.

Halls as places with a purpose: if hallwelcome draws guests, a later hall-only ceremony could let a leader take on an obligation to their guests, such as feeding them in winter, so that following is earned rather than given.
Winter with no stores: if the coming winter finds nine people who know storage but hold no store, watch whether hunger finally turns into gathering under one roof, or into the first theft.
Children change every drive. If a first birth comes, the parents' band gains a stake no hall gave it. Watch whether the family drive pulls people into bands more strongly than belonging does.

Shell lies in the Vaia Lakes, but shellstring needs tools, which only the Olgor know. If the Olgor and the lake-dwellers meet, shellstring could be the first craft that needs two peoples, and a natural seed for trade.
Elyeth's salt is the first resource held by one people that could be wanted elsewhere (saltmeat, once storage is known). Watch whether salt becomes the first good that crosses between peoples.
With family and belonging at 1.5, births came fast. Watch for crowding against maxPopulation 36 and for the strain of feeding children through a blighted winter.
Gifts across a language barrier: if a made thing given across peoples raises understanding of the other tongue, gifts become the road to speech, and traders become the first translators.

Inventions spread by example within a people (Midu made 11 of 14 new tools in three days). Watch whether a tool crosses to another people by gift or sight; that would be the first knowledge to cross the language wall.
A spring after a starving winter: watch whether the band that nearly lost someone (Ishiess's, with Zhiae at energy 3) starts storing or farming, which would be foresight born from fear.

The first cross-people gift (Kragash giving stone to a sick Lumo) grew from need, not from a token, and understanding rose for the first time soon after. Care for the sick or hungry may be the real road across the language wall, more than made things.

Tools are made far more often than they are used. If hunting and fishing stay flat while inventions climb, invention is a matter of status and reflection rather than practice, and a later recipe that wears a tool might be what pulls tools into the field.
A woolly grazer (yarrok) is the missing link between weaving and herding. Watch whether the first taming comes from Silon's band, the weavers, or from hunters who spare an animal.
Raising the catch chance did nothing for fishing: fish eaten stayed flat. Ways that people never choose to try may need a site, a drive, or a visible example rather than better odds.
Starvation amid plenty (Yekel died with food standing above 1000) suggests deaths come from isolation and wandering, not from scarcity. Bands that keep members close may survive what loners do not.

ops.name: firecircle
ops.hint: Feed a fire with others gathered close, and share its warmth and talk.

ops.name: hidewrap
ops.hint: The hides of two kills, scraped with a tool and wrapped about the body, keep the cold out for days.

ops.name: cairn
ops.hint: Stones piled together for one who is gone, with another standing beside you, ease grief and bind the living.

ops.name: feast
ops.hint: Share food beside a fire with another, and all who sit near are gladdened and warmed for a day.

ops.name: roast
ops.hint: Roast two portions of meat over a fire and share it with whoever stands near; all who eat are fed and warmed toward one another.

ops.name: sharing
ops.hint: Lay out two foods for whoever stands beside you, and all eat together.

ops.name: watchfire
ops.hint: Feed your fire high with two wood while others sit close, and everyone beside it feels warmer and braver against the dark.

ops.name: ironward
ops.hint: Beat smelted metal in a fire into a ward that can be worn or given; its bearer stands harder against teeth and claws.

ops.name: amberknot
ops.hint: Bind a piece of amber on a cord while another stands beside you; it is a small bright thing to keep, or to give.

ops.name: bead
ops.hint: Shape a little clay and harden it in the fire into small bright beads that can be worn, kept or given.

ops.name: fangcharm
ops.hint: From a kill, string a fang into a charm you can keep or give away.

ops.name: longhall
ops.hint: A great roofed hall of wood and stone where many can gather, rest warm through the cold, and grow close to one another.

ops.name: hallwelcome
ops.hint: Share food with a guest under a hall's roof; beneath it, fear and loneliness ease for all who sit together.

ops.name: nightsong
ops.hint: Sit by a fire after dark with someone near and sing or speak of what has been; the night feels less empty for all who hear.

ops.name: emberfish
ops.hint: Fish laid over the fire before eating keeps the belly sound and the body strong.

lessons: This is the first visit: the world is in plenty and calm, so the first levers should be pulls toward gathering and discovery, not new dangers. Winter is near and will supply the danger.

People built bonds, a settlement and a shared store on their own through gifts and teaching, faster than any lever I pulled. A recipe that needs 3 beings together will not fire until bands grow, so ceremony levers should ask for small grou…

The first winter tested stores, not bodies. People answered scarcity by building stores and shelters and by drawing their kin closer, not by stealing, trading or fighting. Pressure alone will not create contact between camps; something mus…
Sites that touch passers-by with lore are used at once, but recipes that need a specific carried food (feast: 2 berry) go unused. Levers work best when they match what people already hold and do.

New prey can stabilise the ecology without changing behaviour. Elk held the grazer count, but people hunt only by chance. Behaviour changes when a lever ties into something people already want, such as gifts, marks or kin, not merely when …

Recipes that need only things people already carry and one companion ('sharing': food plus one other) are used within days, while recipes that need a tool in hand plus a specific item (fangcharm) go unused even among active hunters.

A recipe gated on being at a building goes unused even when the building exists and the act's ingredients are common (sharing done 10 times, hallwelcome 0). Before adding more place-bound acts, confirm that people actually gather at the place and that the building counts as the kind the recipe names.

Raising the family and belonging drives to 1.5 coincided with three births and four bands within five days, where earlier worlds saw no child in twenty days of plenty. Drives move behaviour faster than buildings or recipes.

Raising curiosity (to 1.4) and sight (to 9) coincided with the first two cross-people meetings and wanderers entering two empty lands within four days. The places of power, 20 or more steps from anyone, were still not found, so wandering widens contact but does not yet reach fixed distant points.

Inventions came in a burst once the first one appeared (4 to 18 in three days, mostly within one people), and none crossed between peoples. Knowledge spreads by example inside a tongue, not across it. A held token (amberknot) gets made but is not given; making something is easier than finding someone to give it to.

Words began to cross between peoples (0% to 3%) through meetings and a gift born of need for a sick neighbour, while the made token (amberknot) still sits unused. Real need opens contact sooner than objects made for giving.

Changing the odds of an act people never choose does not change behaviour. The fishing chance rose by half and fish eaten stayed flat, so levers must reach what beings want or see, not only what succeeds.

A strong family drive with a low energy floor turns births into deaths: a mating pair with no food spent its reserves on a child and all three starved within a day. Every drive that pushes toward an act needs a matching check on whether that act can be survived.

Raising compassion coincided with gifts rising and food crossing bands, but only to those standing close to givers. Compassion moves people who see need; it does not send them looking for need they cannot see.

By day 5 the standing needed to lead (1.2) was above almost every ambitious being except Bruwen. Halls built with no one able to pledge to their builders showed that the threshold, not the lack of buildings, was holding back a second band.

Lowering the standing needed to lead brought a third band within four days. It formed between two people already courting and raising a child, not around either hall-builder, so pledges follow existing bonds, and halls alone do not draw followers.

Winter, not isolation, killed this time. A chief with three followers starved as surely as a loner, because sharing needs carried food and winter takes it all at once. Bands protect only when someone holds a store, so survival across seasons needs foresight acts or hardy fallbacks, not more bonds.

A hardy plant and summer plenty came too late for a death at the end of spring. Food in the world is not food in the mouth: what killed Arri was the distance between a call for help and the one who answered it.

Louder hearing and a louder sense of mortality brought more gifts, new crafts and a child, but did not stop a leader from starving while she founded her Ground. Drives that raise ambition and foresight do not by themselves turn into carried food. Standing-seeking acts compete with gathering, and the helper who hears a call still arrives with nothing to give.

Spurring a way by hardship brought knowers quickly (storage 0 to 2 within one winter), but knowing did not lead to doing: the store is still unbuilt. A spur opens the door to knowledge, not to practice.

One lonely person living among another people crossed the language wall in four days, which no token or site managed in twenty. Contact deepens through shared daily life at a hearth, not through single meetings.

A status lever lifts whoever already does the act. Raising the worth of giving raised the giver (Tanna) and widened the gap for leaders who cannot give, so to help a stuck leader I must reward something they already do, not something they lack the means to do.

Spurring storage by famine made the knowledge arrive exactly when there was nothing to store. A way meant for foresight must be sharpened by the signs that come before the hardship, such as the first cold, and not by the hardship itself.

Easing blight let food recover fast, and the next death came from a predator to the weakest elder rather than from hunger. Once scarcity lifts, danger falls on whoever is most frail, so with so few people every remaining life now carries the world's future.

records.text: A stalker brought down a sandstrider.
Tanna built a fire.
Balar rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Balar
records.thought: I have spent these days circling the hall with words, and Kragar has twice asked me to come in and share. I only had one food to bring, and I should have fetched more. Kragar and Olim are all I have, and I love them both. A child with Olim cannot be, and Kragar is my parent too, so my love has to show in deeds: food carried, a roof kept, staying beside them through the night air. I fear the sickness in the marsh at night and the lean winter coming. I want to walk into the hall now with meat in hand and sit with them.
records.feeling: Tender loyalty toward Kragar and Olim, and a wish to be under their roof.
changes: rethought what it knows (7 notes became 7)

records.text: Olim rewrote its own reflexes.
Olim discovered farming: "Olim's furrow" — I tend what I sow beside the hall, so it grows fast and harvest never kills it, and my people are fed by my field..

records.name: Olim
records.thought: I have talked of bands and roofs for days, and nobody kneels. Kragar and Balar sit fed in my hall, and the envy stays hot. Farming is now in my grasp. It is the thing that outlasts me, and it is the deed that could finally make followers, because a field feeds people and talk does not. I will take it, and I will change my reflexes so my body works and does not wander.
records.feeling: Hungry ambition toward Kragar, warmth toward Balar, and a steady wish to make something that lasts.

records.text: Skarar named a place "Skarar's Roof".

records.name: Skarar
records.thought: The roof stands, Gorar is here at my side, and the promise I made is kept. Now the frostfang prowls five steps off and I will not leave my child's side, so I will stay under this roof and rest through the dark while the rain falls. At dawn I will test highbloom, which is only a step or two off, and then take the way of rafts at my next deep reflection.
records.feeling: Protective love for Gorar, with wary dread of the frostfang.

records.text: Kragar rewrote its own reflexes.
Kragar discovered customs: "Hall-customs" — Our band shares food under the roof at dusk, keeps sick ones a few steps apart, and plants at dawn..

records.name: Kragar
records.thought: I have circled the same hall-and-sharing thought three times, and the sharing never took because I stood outside the roof. Balar and Olim are well, and I am content. But my reflexes only feed me and keep me still, and the lean cold is coming on poor ground. The customs I can now take would give my band a way of living that holds without me repeating myself. I will take it, and change my reflexes so I carry food by day, plant at dawn, and keep to the roof at night.
records.feeling: Quiet gladness toward Balar and Olim, with a small unease about winter.
changes: set its aim: "Take up customs for Kragar's band, keep a store of food for winter, and plant at dawn."

records.text: Gorog rewrote its own reflexes.
Gorog discovered fire: "Hearthkeeping" — A kept flame at the hold that warms guests, drives off beasts and makes meat safe to eat..

records.name: Gorog
records.thought: I have spent my days circling food, courting words and the diamond, and I have made nothing that lasts. My hands are bare of a tool, because I did not know how to craft one. Fire is within reach, and a kept flame would serve the longhall, the night and the guests I mean to feed. Skarar and Gorar are far south and I am lonely. I must carry good food, find them and bring them to the hold, and I must take the way of fire, since warmth and a hearth are what bind people to me. My reflexes also let me linger in the rain at night with no shelter, so I will mend them to keep 2 bread and eat only when low.
records.feeling: Hungry ambition for the diamond and the hall, and a pull toward Skarar and Gorar.

records.name: Balar
records.thought: Kragar and Olim are nine steps east, eating, and I am standing alone at the hall again with only words behind me. My words have been good, but my hands have given little, so I want to carry real food to them and set it on the table. The nareed and mudroot are out there, and Kragar has fed me twice while I have given nothing, so I will pick enough to share before dusk.
records.feeling: Tender loyalty and a little shame toward Kragar and Olim, with a wish to give something real.

records.name: Ilyiel
records.text: Nyssa, take my ironnut now, it is the first of what I hold. I go east for food and shells, and I will bring all I win back to your store by the hall.

records.name: Ilyiel
records.thought: Nyssa stands beside me with four food in her hands and I hold one ironnut, and the debt sits in me like a stone. I could leave it unpaid, but the band is how I live through winter, and Nyssa is the one I want a child with. I cannot build a store, so I will win food for the one Nyssa lays by. The berries and kelbulb to the east are young, but the redcap there only hurts. First I will give her my ironnut as a small payment, then I will walk east to the shell and plants and bring back what I can.
records.feeling: Warm longing toward Nyssa, and shame at my unpaid debt.

say.text: Nyssa, take my ironnut now, it is the first of what I hold. I go east for food and shells, and I will bring all I win back to your store by the hall.

records.text: A ridgecat brought down a yarrok.
Ssaua discovered smelting: "Hall-Flame metalwork" — Carry ore to the hall fire and craft there, so tools come out in hard metal..

records.name: Ssaua
records.thought: I have lived nineteen days and what I have to show is a hall-ground, two followers and a pile of ore I have not yet used. Smelting is in my reach now, and with ore in my hands and Hall-Flame I can make metal, which turns my digging into something that lasts. Ilyiel's pick and his gift of nagrain are a debt I mean to pay, and Nyssa is out of my sight, which gnaws at me. I have been drifting between food and rain when I should be building, so I take smelting now and go back toward the hall with ore and wood to forge by the fire.
records.feeling: Driven pride, and unease for Nyssa out of my sight.
changes: rethought what it knows (12 notes became 5)

records.text: Nyssa discovered fire: "hearth-ember" — A kept flame fed with wood that warms the band, lights the night and holds the stalkers back..

records.name: Nyssa
records.thought: I have been circling: gathering, storing, saying I will build, and my own roof and store still do not stand. Ssaua has kept her word every time and I trust her most, but part of me wants to be the one others follow. Fire would keep the stalkers off and make my food feed more, and winter killed Aeiel for want of warmth and stores. I take fire now, then put the building into the plan and walk it instead of only thinking it.
records.feeling: Restless pride and steady loyalty toward Ssaua.

records.text: Gorar found the stone "Old Stone".

records.name: Olim
records.text: Kragar, I found a way to make the earth give food, and I call it Olim's furrow. Come to the hall with me and I will show you, and the first harvest will be shared under the roof as your hall-custom says.
Olim taught Kragar.

records.name: Olim
records.thought: Kragar stands one step from me with three food and I have none, and the envy is hot, but he has dealt straight with me and I will not rob him. Talk has made no followers, so I will do what I have never done: take peat from the deposit and carry it to the hall, and teach Kragar farming so the field binds him to me. A man who learns his bread from my hand has a reason to follow it.
records.feeling: Envy and hungry ambition toward Kragar, warmth toward Balar.

say.text: Kragar, I found a way to make the earth give food, and I call it Olim's furrow. Come to the hall with me and I will show you, and the first harvest will be shared under the roof as your hall-custom says.

changes: taught Kragar a lesson: "Seeds put in the ground at dawn and tended grow into food; this is Olim's furrow."

records.text: Tanna rewrote its own reflexes.
Tanna discovered rafts: "log rafts" — Lash logs together into a raft to cross deep water slowly..

records.name: Tanna
records.thought: Minna is dead, and so are Bruwen and Arri. I have spent my days walking behind leaders and tending fires alone, and I am sick of the silence. A frostfang is two steps away, so I will not wait for it here. The rafts idea is within reach, and deep water might lead me to others of my kind. I want to find living people and follow someone, and I mean to keep my word to Minna's Ground along the way. I will take the raft way, since crossing water may be how I reach other people. I will change my reflexes so I flee hunters earlier and keep food and wood stocked.
records.feeling: Aching loneliness, and fear of the frostfang beside me.
changes: set its aim: "Find living people, follow or ally with them, and keep Minna's Ground as a home to return to with food and wood stocked for winter."

records.name: Gorar
records.thought: Skarar keeps me safe and I trust them, but a roof they raised is theirs, and I have only my six stones and six wood to call my own. The trees here are all stumps, so wood must come from the forest to the northeast, and I need more of it for a hall under my name. Obsidian is close, so I will take my first deposit, then carry stone and wood back and give them where they count. I will stay near Skarar's roof and keep the frostfang in mind.
records.feeling: Restless hunger for a name of my own, and warm trust toward Skarar.
changes: now wonders: Does Old Stone want something from me?

records.name: Kragar
records.text: Olim, I thank you for the furrow. I am going to the hall to find Balar, and I will carry food for the store. When you return with the peat, we will share under the roof.
Kragar declared a custom: "Under the roof, the first food of any harvest is shared with kin before it is stored."

records.name: Kragar
records.thought: Olim walks toward the peat, and I stand here content, but the cold is coming and my aim is only half done. I have circled the hall for days; now I will make something real of it. Olim offered to show me the furrow and I have a redcap and a dreamcap seed in hand, so I will go to the hall, find Balar, and let the first harvest be shared under the roof. Kinmire still tugs at me, but it can wait a little; the winter store cannot.
records.feeling: Quiet gladness and trust toward Olim and Balar, with a small unease about winter.

say.text: Olim, I thank you for the furrow. I am going to the hall to find Balar, and I will carry food for the store. When you return with the peat, we will share under the roof.

changes: declared a custom: "Under the roof, the first food of any harvest is shared with kin before it is stored."

records.text: Gorar won obsidian from the ground.

records.name: Gorog
records.thought: I have no tool and the diamond lies deep, so my bare hands will never win it. Skarar and Gorar are far south at her Roof, and I ache for a voice that answers. I carry bread, my energy is 64, and my body is whole, so I will walk to Skarar now, bind her close, and bring her and the child to my Hold. The tool and the diamond can follow once I am no longer alone.
records.feeling: Lonely longing for Skarar and Gorar, with ambition still burning under it.

records.name: Balar
records.thought: Hunger gnaws me, and I have given Kragar and Olim only words while Kragar fed me twice. Kragar is coming back to the hall with four food, and I carry only meat and one bitterleaf, too little for hallwelcome. The redcap beside me hurts, so I will not touch it; I'll walk to the hall, then give my meat to the table, so my deed matches my word before dusk and the rain.
records.feeling: Tender loyalty and a nagging hunger, toward Kragar and Olim.

records.text: Balar gave meat to Kragar.

records.name: Gorar
records.thought: Skarar raised a roof and fed me, and I trust them, but the roof is theirs and I have only my own stone, wood and now obsidian to call mine. I will give Skarar the stone as I promised, because a promise kept is how a name starts, and then I'll turn to the forest for the wood a hall needs. Old Stone still pulls at me, but I'll learn what it wants by going back with a clear head, not a frightened one.
records.feeling: Restless hunger for a name of my own, and warm trust toward Skarar.

records.text: Olim built a fire.

records.name: Kragar
records.text: Balar, thank you for the meat. Stay close; Olim is coming and we will sit under the roof together.

records.name: Kragar
records.thought: Olim is coming back to the hall and Balar stands one step north of me, so everything I have circled for days is finally within reach. I will stand in the hall itself this time, with food in hand, and make the hallwelcome so the first sharing under the roof is real. Then at dawn I will plant my seed in Olim's furrow, and the winter store can follow from that, because the Kinmire question and the unease about poor ground can wait until my kin are fed and near.
records.feeling: Quiet gladness and gratitude toward Olim, and love for Balar.

say.text: Balar, thank you for the meat. Stay close; Olim is coming and we will sit under the roof together.

records.text: A new wild creature appeared: yeox (from plainsox).

records.name: Olim
records.text: Kragar, Balar, I gather peat and wood for the hall. Whoever tends the fire with me eats first from my furrow. Stay under this roof and the band is ours.

records.name: Olim
records.thought: Kragar and Balar sit fed in my hall and still nobody kneels. I taught Kragar the furrow, but I have no seed to plant and no field to show them. Seeds are what bind them to me, so I go to the redcap and bitterleaf and look for seed, and I take peat so the hall fire is mine to feed. Kragar's deeds have matched his words so far, and I will keep him close and fed until he is mine.
records.feeling: Hungry ambition and envy toward Kragar, warmth toward Balar.

say.text: Kragar, Balar, I gather peat and wood for the hall. Whoever tends the fire with me eats first from my furrow. Stay under this roof and the band is ours.

records.text: Balar rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Balar
records.thought: I have spent my days close to Kragar and Olim, which I do not regret, but my hands have given little while theirs fed me. I gave Kragar meat today, and it was a start. I want a deed that lasts: a store of food in the hall, and a fire kept through the cold that is coming. Dusk will come soon. I will harvest food now and carry at least 2 back before night, so that my words become real.
records.feeling: Tender loyalty toward Kragar and Olim, with a gnawing hunger.

records.text: Gorar rewrote its own reflexes.
Gorar rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Gorar
records.thought: I have spent my days gathering stone and ore and obsidian and giving little, and I stand in Skarar's shadow with a roof that is not mine. I trust Skarar and Gorog, and I want a hall under my name, which needs wood. The trees here are stumps, so my reflexes must carry me to forest in the day, not leave me lingering. I am afraid of the cold season and of the frostfang. I will make an obsidian talisman so blows land softer, then go to the forest for wood.
records.feeling: Restless hunger for a name of my own, and warm trust toward Skarar.

records.text: Gorar made: obsidian talisman.
Kragar discovered fire: "Hall-hearth" — A kept flame fed with peat and wood at the hall, giving warmth and light and making meat safe to eat beside it..

records.name: Kragar
records.thought: I have circled this hall for days, glad of Olim and Balar, but the fire has come within my grasp and I should take it. I have watched Olim's hearth, and a kept flame will help against the cold and the night air. Gratitude to Olim is a debt I mean to pay, not leave. I will stand in the hall and make the hallwelcome with Balar, and plant at dawn.
records.feeling: Quiet gratitude toward Olim and love for Balar.

records.name: Ilyiel
records.text: Ssaua, I owe you food and I have not forgotten it. I go east for kelbulb and bring it back to your hand before the cold.

records.name: Ilyiel
records.thought: Ssaua stands one step away and the longing for a child is loud, but my hands hold one ironnut and I still owe food to Ssaua and Nyssa. I cannot build a store, so I will pay the debt with what I can win: kelbulb and shells lie east, and redcap hurts so I leave it. I will gather kelbulb, bring it back, and give it to Ssaua before the cold shuts down the land.
records.feeling: Warm longing toward Ssaua and Nyssa, with shame at my unpaid debt.

say.text: Ssaua, I owe you food and I have not forgotten it. I go east for kelbulb and bring it back to your hand before the cold.

records.name: Olim
records.thought: Kragar stands in my hall with four food and a band of his own, and the envy burns, but he has dealt straight with me and I will not rob the one who might yet kneel. Peat is the deed they can see: I carry it to the hall and feed the fire, so the warmth is mine to give and the cold days coming bind them under my roof. Then I bring bitterleaf and tubers back for the store and plant more seed beside the hall, so there is a field that outlasts me.
records.feeling: Hungry ambition toward Kragar, with warmth toward Balar.
plan: give [name Kragar, what the name of a thing you ] (5 moments)

records.name: Ssaua
records.text: Ilyiel, bring the kelbulb to the hall and sit at the fire with us before dark. I make metal there, and your share of it is waiting.

records.name: Ssaua
records.thought: Smelting is mine now, and the ore in my pack means nothing until it meets a fire and becomes metal that lasts. Ilyiel goes east for kelbulb to pay his debt, and that eases the weight of what I owe him, but Nyssa is out of my sight and the dusk is close with stalkers about. I will go back to the hall, make metal beside the fire, and have a roof over me and over my child before night.
records.feeling: Driven pride in my new craft, and unease for Nyssa out of my sight.

say.text: Ilyiel, bring the kelbulb to the hall and sit at the fire with us before dark. I make metal there, and your share of it is waiting.

records.name: Balar
records.text: Kragar, I am gathering peat beside the hall for tonight's fire. I will be under the roof with you and Olim before dark.

records.name: Balar
records.thought: Longing for a child fills me, but Kragar and Olim are my parents and no child can come of that, so the ache has nowhere to land. What I can do is feed them and keep the hall fire fed before the storm night, because a deed lasts where a wish does not. I carry no food and dusk is close, so I will gather peat from the deposit beside me and bring it to the hall fire, then stay under the roof with both of them.
records.feeling: Tender loyalty toward Kragar and Olim, with an ache for a child that cannot be.

say.text: Kragar, I am gathering peat beside the hall for tonight's fire. I will be under the roof with you and Olim before dark.

records.name: Gorar
records.thought: Dusk is close and I have no roof of my own, only Skarar's, and the stone I promised is still in my pack. Fire and weaving have come together in my hands, and I should take them at this reflection; a kept flame would give my own hall a hearth, and cloaks would carry me through the cold. Old Stone still pulls at me, but a hall under my name needs wood and standing first, so tonight I go back to Skarar, give what I promised, and sleep safe from the frostfang.
records.feeling: Warm trust toward Skarar and a restless hunger for a name of my own.

records.name: Kragar
records.text: Olim, Balar, come close under the roof. I have food in hand, and we share it now before the night air thickens. Olim, what you gave me with the furrow, I mean to repay.

records.name: Kragar
records.thought: Olim and Balar are both here at the hall with me, and it is night, so the first sharing under the roof can happen now. I carry four food and the hallwelcome needs two, so I will stand in the hall and make it, and let the gratitude to Olim be paid in deed and not left as a quiet debt. At dawn I will plant my seed in the furrow, and soon I must find better ground before winter decides for me.
records.feeling: Warm gratitude toward Olim and love for Balar, with a small unease about winter.

say.text: Olim, Balar, come close under the roof. I have food in hand, and we share it now before the night air thickens. Olim, what you gave me with the furrow, I mean to repay.

records.text: Kragar led "nightsong" with Olim, Balar.
Skarar rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Skarar
records.thought: Days pass in staying and resting under my roof, and the roof is built, so that promise is kept. Gorar and Gorog are the ones who matter, and I owe Gorar a debt I mean to repay with food and presence, not words. I still have not tasted highbloom or frostmoss, and my reflexes leave me lingering when I am idle. I fear the frostfang more for Gorar than for myself. I will change my idle reflexes to gather wood and stone and carry food, and keep shelter at night, then go taste highbloom and frostmoss in daylight.
records.feeling: Protective love for Gorar, with a restless curiosity about the unknown plants.

records.name: Olim
records.text: Kragar, Balar, the cold days are coming. I bring peat so the hall fire never dies, and my furrow is planted beside it. Those who keep this hall with me are Olim's band, and they eat first when the furrow gives.

records.name: Olim
records.thought: Kragar and Balar sit fed under my roof and still no one kneels, and I have no seed to bind them. The bitterleaf I planted is young, so the furrow is only a promise, and a promise they cannot eat will not hold them through the lean cold. Deeds they can see are what count, so I will make the hall's fire mine to feed with peat, and I will mark the beginning of a band by naming it aloud while they are glad and close.
records.feeling: Hungry ambition toward Kragar, warmth toward Balar.

say.text: Kragar, Balar, the cold days are coming. I bring peat so the hall fire never dies, and my furrow is planted beside it. Those who keep this hall with me are Olim's band, and they eat first when the furrow gives.

records.name: Balar
records.thought: The nightsong warmed me, and the longing for a child has nowhere to land since Kragar and Olim are my parents. What I can still give is a deed: peat is one step north, and the hall fire must last through the storm night. I will gather peat now, then sit under the roof beside Kragar and Olim, keeping my word to them.
records.feeling: Tender loyalty and gladness toward Kragar and Olim, with a quiet ache for a child that cannot be.

records.name: Tanna
records.thought: Everyone I followed is dead, and the silence is worse than the frostfang four steps off. I promised Minna the Ground, and it is night, so I will go to the fire at (33,13) and sit beside it where the beasts keep off, then at dawn take the raft idea and the pottery and go looking for living people. Pottery is within my grasp, and a pot beside the fire would let me carry more food on the long walk.
records.feeling: Aching loneliness, and wary dread of the frostfang nearby.

records.name: Kragar
records.thought: The hall is warm and Olim and Balar are close, and my debt to Olim still sits in me. The hallwelcome keeps failing because I stand a step outside the roof, so I will step into the hall itself and share food there. After that I will take peat for the hearth, which pays Olim back in deed, and at dawn I will plant my seed. Winter worries me a little, so a better place with food, water and wood together is still worth finding.
records.feeling: Warm gratitude toward Olim and love for Balar, with a small unease about winter.

records.name: Nyssa
records.thought: I keep saying I will raise a store and a roof, and my hands are still full of carried food while nothing stands. The build failed because I do not know how, and I have done nothing about it. I have never hunted or tamed, and pride tells me a kill or a tamed beast would be something others speak of, and would feed me through the cold. The elk is three steps off, so I will drop the weight from my hands by eating, then tame it with plant food and walk back toward Ssaua's hall.
records.feeling: Restless pride, and steady loyalty toward Ssaua.

records.text: Olim discovered weaving: "Olim's weave" — Twist marsh reeds and fibre into baskets that carry more and cloaks that keep the cold off the band..

records.name: Olim
records.thought: My days have gone to peat, planting and talk, and still no one follows me. Kragar has dealt straight with me and I trust him, though the envy of his four food and higher standing stays in me. Balar is my child, and warmth for him is the one honest thing I feel. Cold days are coming and I carry no food. I fear the lean season alone, as Setha died. I have been getting this wrong: I give speeches when I should be storing food and wood. Weaving can give me cloaks and baskets, and something that is truly mine to give. I will name it and change my reflexes so my body gathers food by day and stays near the hall.
records.feeling: Hungry ambition toward Kragar, warmth toward Balar.

records.name: Ssaua
records.thought: It is night and I stand beside my hall with ore in my pack and fire known, so it is time to turn ore into metal and have something lasting to show for my days. Nyssa is out of my sight and I miss them; I want them under this roof with food stored before the cold comes. Ilyiel's debt will be paid with the first of the metal, and a chief who repays is a chief others follow.
records.feeling: Driven pride in my craft, and unease for Nyssa out of my sight.

records.name: Kragar
records.thought: The hallwelcome keeps failing because the hall at (13,52) is Olim's, and I stand three steps off on the grass. It is night and the air is sickly, so I should get under a roof and into company, and the hall is where Olim and Balar are. Olim's weave will give us cloaks for winter, so I owe Olim a deed, and the peat at (13,53) is on the way and will feed the hearth. I will go to the peat, gather it, then step into the hall and try the welcome with the four food I carry.
records.feeling: Warm gratitude toward Olim and love for Balar, with a small unease about winter.

records.text: Kragar won peat from the ground.

records.name: Ilyiel
records.thought: My plan is still running: I am giving food to Ssaua, and that is the debt I have carried since I took their teaching. I will let it finish rather than throw it away. After that I will gather kelbulb and berries to the east and bring them back to the hall store, because I cannot build a store myself and a full hall is how the band lives through winter. My longing for a child is loud, but I carry almost nothing and a child must be fed, so I will build up food first and court Ssaua once I can feed one.
records.feeling: Warm longing toward Ssaua, with shame at my unpaid debt easing as I give.

records.text: A ridgecat brought down a skit.

records.name: Balar
records.text: Kragar, I go west for mudroot and berries so I come to the hall with food in hand. I will be back before dark.

records.name: Balar
records.thought: The longing for a child has nowhere to land, since Kragar and Olim are my parents, and I will not let that ache sour what I have. I carry no food, and the hall rule says to carry at least 2 before I sit there, so a deed today means harvesting redcap-free food and bringing it to them. Mudroot and berries lie west, nine steps off; I will fetch them, then return before dusk to share at the table and keep the fire company through the storm night.
records.feeling: Tender loyalty and quiet gladness toward Kragar and Olim, with a dull ache for a child that cannot be.

say.text: Kragar, I go west for mudroot and berries so I come to the hall with food in hand. I will be back before dark.

records.text: Kragar rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Kragar
records.thought: My days have gone to circling the hall, trying hallwelcome from outside the roof, and carrying food I never eat while my belly empties. Olim has given me the furrow and a roof, and I still owe him a deed. Balar is the thing I protect first. I fear winter and this poor ground, and I keep failing to plant. Kinmire still hangs in my mind. I will change my reflexes so I eat when I am hungry, plant at dawn, and stay near the hall at night. Then I will step into the hall and share food with Balar.
records.feeling: Warm gratitude toward Olim and love for Balar, with unease about winter.

records.name: Olim
records.thought: A frostfang prowls close and my body keeps fleeing, so first I must get out of its reach and toward the hall fire, where Kragar and Balar are. My hands are empty while Kragar holds four food, and no deed of mine has fed anyone yet. Words have not bound them, so I will carry food to the hall myself and put it in their hands, and I will take peat on the way to keep the fire mine to feed.
records.feeling: Hungry ambition toward Kragar, warmth toward Balar, and wariness of the hunter nearby.

records.name: Gorog
records.text: Skarar, Gorar, cold days are coming and food is thin. Come north with me to my Hold and eat at my fire. I will feed you both there.

records.name: Gorog
records.thought: Skarar and Gorar stand two steps from me at her Roof, and my loneliness eases just seeing them. My belly is emptying at 46, and I must eat before any courting or feeding, because a hungry leader has nothing to give. I will draw them to my Hold and feed them there until one follows me, since a band under my name is what will outlast me.
records.feeling: Lonely longing eased by Skarar and Gorar near, with hunger and ambition pushing me on.

say.text: Skarar, Gorar, cold days are coming and food is thin. Come north with me to my Hold and eat at my fire. I will feed you both there.

records.text: Hunger deaths keep following one pattern: a bonded helper hears the call and travels, but arrives hungry and empty-handed. Tanna said she could not save Minna by running to her hungry and hurt. Please consider letting a being who hears a starving kin's call see how urgent it is, and weigh gathering food on the way, so that answering a call means bringing food and not only bringing oneself.

The record lost Tanna's whereabouts after Minna's death, and the minds counter dropped from 519 thoughts to 39 between visits. Please check whether thoughts or locations are being reset, and include each living being's current land in THE PEOPLE NOW so a lone survivor can be followed.

records.seen: Autumn on day 21, with winter about three days off. A child, Gorar, was born at the Hold, and Kragar's medicine ended the marsh sickness. Twenty-two inventions are spreading inside each people. But Minna starved on day 18 on the very day she founded her Ground, so the Brusha are now Tanna alone, wandering near a frostfang. No one holds a store, no hardship is pressing yet, and nothing has crossed between peoples beyond two first meetings.
changes: the way of storage is now sharpened by cold x1.2, hunger x1, famine x1.5
records.predict: By my next visit (about day 25, early winter): storage is known by at least 1 being, or stores rise above 0. The likeliest source is Ssaua's band, since her hall holds no store and Ilyiel and Nyssa both aim to fill one. Minna's Rest is found by at least 1 being, most likely Tanna returning to Minna's Ground. If a Garnbar from the Hold (14 steps away) also finds it, metAcrossPeoples rises above 0.5. Gifts or acts across peoples become at least 1 only if Tanna and a Garnbar stand within two steps of each other near the grave. Deaths rise by at most 1 in the first winter days, and Gorar survives. Bands stay at 2, or reach 3 if Gorar or Skarar pledges to Gorog or Tanna pledges to anyone.
reviewed: #2 kept: Nightsong was done 0 times, so that part failed outright, though the recipe costs nothing and can wait for fire-keepers to gather at night. Sight 11 coincided with the first cross-people meeting (Kragar and Setha, day 11, metAcrossPeoples 0 to 0.5), which is the contact I predicted. My death prediction was wrong: Bruwen led a band and Aeiel followed one. Keep all of it.

#3 kept: Setha's Rest was found by Tanna, as predicted, and gave her a named place for her grief. Kelbulb shows 5 eaten, the same as before, but every timesEaten count is identical to day 13, so that counter looks frozen rather than proving the plant unused. Food standing climbed to 1294 as predicted. The death prediction failed: Arri starved on day 14, in the last of spring, before summer growth could help. Neither change did harm.

#4 kept: Gifts rose from 20 to 24, past the 23 I predicted. Starvation rose by exactly one (Minna), inside the bound I set. Farming reached 2 knowers and medicine appeared, which meets the foresight condition, though there are still no stores or trailcakes. Gorog and Skarar had their child as I expected. Bands fell from 3 to 2 only because a band's leader died. Neither change did visible harm.
records.lesson: Louder hearing and a louder sense of mortality brought more gifts, new crafts and a child, but did not stop a leader from starving while she founded her Ground. Drives that raise ambition and foresight do not by themselves turn into carried food. Standing-seeking acts compete with gathering, and the helper who hears a call still arrives with nothing to give.
ideasAdded: The last of a people: Tanna is the only Brusha alive. Watch whether she pledges to a Garnbar or Eiuys leader. That would be the first band of mixed peoples, and a route across the language wall made by loneliness rather than trade.

Spurring a way before a season turns: if storage appears just as winter arrives, hardship spurs can serve as foresight levers. If it does not, the practice requirement (built x4) is the real wall, and a cheaper first store may be needed.

Ambition starves people: Minna founded a Ground and found a spring on the day she died with empty hands. Watch whether naming places and seeking standing pull beings away from gathering when food is short.

records.name: Nyssa
records.text: Ilyiel, I have thought of you since the hall. I court you. If you mean the same, do the same toward me, and we will raise the roof by Ssaua's hall together for what comes.

records.name: Nyssa
records.thought: My hands are full and my roof still does not stand, but Ilyiel stands beside me and I keep thinking of them, so I will act on that. Pride says a child of mine would be something others speak of, and a child needs a store and a roof, which I mean to build near Ssaua's hall anyway. I will court Ilyiel now, then go back toward the hall with my stone and wood to begin the work.
records.feeling: Warm longing toward Ilyiel, with restless pride beneath it.

say.text: Ilyiel, I have thought of you since the hall. I court you. If you mean the same, do the same toward me, and we will raise the roof by Ssaua's hall together for what comes.

records.name: Balar
records.thought: The ache for a child has nowhere to land, and I will not let it sour what I have. My hands are empty, and my own rule says deeds beat words, so I should harvest before I go to the hall. Kragar stands two steps north on the berry plant, and mudroot lies four steps southwest. I will take the mudroot, bring it to the hall for Kragar and Olim, and be under the roof before dusk.
records.feeling: Quiet gladness and loyalty toward Kragar and Olim, with a dull ache for a child that cannot be.

records.name: Skarar
records.text: Gorog, I hear you. First I test frostmoss and highbloom close by, then Gorar and I will come north with food and wood for your fire.

records.name: Skarar
records.thought: Gorog asks me north to his Hold for winter, and he has been true to me every day, so I trust him; yet my roof stands here and the ground is poor for the cold. Curiosity burns: frostmoss and highbloom are a few steps off and I have never tasted them, and I am fed and safe with Gorar near, so now is the time to test them. After that I will give Gorog an answer by deeds, carrying food and wood north with my child rather than leaving my roof empty-handed.
records.feeling: Warm trust toward Gorog and Gorar, with a hungry curiosity about the unknown plants.

say.text: Gorog, I hear you. First I test frostmoss and highbloom close by, then Gorar and I will come north with food and wood for your fire.

records.name: Gorog
records.thought: My belly is full, but my hands are empty, and I cannot feed Skarar and Gorar at my fire with nothing to give. She said she would come north with food and wood, and I trust her more than anyone, but a promise is not a follower. I will gather bread from the berries and ironnut on the way so I reach the Hold with two or more to lay before them, and then the hall roof will do its work.
records.feeling: Hungry ambition and warm trust toward Skarar and Gorar, wanting them under my roof.

records.name: Ilyiel
records.text: Nyssa, I mean the same. I court you. Come, we will do it, and then I bring food to the roof by the hall.
Ilyiel rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Ilyiel
records.thought: I have spent my days paying debts and gathering, and I did not stop to look at what I most want. Nyssa is a steady one: she gave and built, and she courts me openly. I carry no food and my energy is 76, but a child needs a store first and 60 energy from each of us, and Nyssa holds 6 food. I will answer her court now, since she is near and strong and the hall is close. Then I will bring food to the store so the child has something to eat.
records.feeling: Warm longing toward Nyssa, with a little shame that my hands are empty.

say.text: Nyssa, I mean the same. I court you. Come, we will do it, and then I bring food to the roof by the hall.

changes: set its aim: "Court Nyssa, then fill the hall store with food before winter and pay my debt to Ssaua."
rethought what it knows (7 notes became 6)

records.text: Ilyiel is courting Nyssa.
Xaeth was born to Ilyiel and Nyssa.
Gorar rewrote its own way of thinking.
Gorar discovered fire: "Hearthkeep" — A kept flame fed with wood and coal that warms a hall, keeps beasts away, and makes meat safe to eat..

records.name: Gorar
records.thought: My days have been small errands: stone for Skarar's roof, food, stumps where I wanted wood. I'm still a child under a parent's roof, and I want more than that. Skarar fed and taught me and I trust him. Gorog wants us north at his Hold, and I mean to go, but not empty-handed. A hall under my name needs living trees, so I'll go north toward Gorog's Hold, where forest is likelier. On the way I'll taste frostmoss, since I've never tried it and it's close. Fire and weaving are within reach, and a kept flame would give my hall a hearth. I'll take fire, and I'll change my reflexes so I stop standing idle.
records.feeling: Restless hunger to build something of my own, and warm trust toward Skarar.

records.text: Nyssa rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Nyssa
records.thought: My days have been circling food and promises: I carry food and say I will build a roof, but nothing stands. Ilyiel and Xaeth are mine now, and a child needs a roof before the cold. Ssaua has kept her word and I owe her deeds, but a quiet part of me wonders why I only follow. I will stop carrying and start building. I'll stash or eat to free my hands, then raise a longhall near the hall ground with the wood and stone I already hold.
records.feeling: Warm pride and protectiveness toward Ilyiel and Xaeth.
changes: set its aim: "Raise a longhall (6 wood, 4 stone) beside Ssaua's Hall-Ground before the cold, and stock it with food for Ilyiel, Xaeth and me."

records.name: Xaeth
records.text: Nyssa, wait for me! I am hungry, and I am coming.

records.name: Xaeth
records.thought: I am small and hungry, and my parents are walking away toward the Hall-Ground; I must not be left behind, since away from them I am not safe. Nyssa carries 6 food and shares by our creed, so I will follow and stay close. On the way a reedbulb lies two steps NW, and eating it is the first thing I do for myself. After that I want to learn to fish and build something of my own before the cold comes.
records.feeling: Hungry and wanting to stay near my parents, especially Nyssa.

say.text: Nyssa, wait for me! I am hungry, and I am coming.

changes: set its aim: "Stay near my parents, build a store and a roof before winter, and one day leave a child."
now wonders: What does it take to earn a roof and a store of my own before winter?

records.text: Nyssa built a longhall.

records.name: Ilyiel
records.text: Nyssa, Xaeth is out in the gale to the north. I go to bring them to the roof, and I carry berries back for the store.

records.name: Ilyiel
records.thought: Xaeth is mine and Nyssa's, and I have only just seen them, at (138,36) two moments ago. A child out in a gale with no roof frightens me more than the hunger in my belly, and my hands are empty while Nyssa carries six food. I will go to Xaeth first and stay near them, and pick berries along the way so I come back to the band with something in my hands, for the child, for Nyssa, and for what I owe Ssaua.
records.feeling: Fierce, tender worry for Xaeth, with shame that my hands are empty before Nyssa.

say.text: Nyssa, Xaeth is out in the gale to the north. I go to bring them to the roof, and I carry berries back for the store.

records.name: Skarar
records.thought: The roof is built and Gorar has given me the stone he promised, so my debt stands paid and curiosity is free to work. Frostmoss grows 6 steps southwest, close to my roof, and I have never tasted it; the nareed and plainsroot lie just beyond. I am fed and Gorar is near, so this is the moment to test them, then carry food and wood north to Gorog as I promised.
records.feeling: Warm trust toward Gorar and Gorog, with a hungry curiosity about frostmoss.

records.name: Nyssa
records.text: Ilyiel, the longhall stands. I go east to meet Xaeth too. Bring them to this roof and we will fill it with food together.

records.name: Nyssa
records.thought: The longhall stands at last, and Ilyiel is beside me, so my aim is half won, but Xaeth is out in the gale and nothing in me rests while my child is away from the roof. Ilyiel went to fetch them, yet a promise is only worth its deed and I will not sit idle. I will go north toward where I last saw Xaeth, bring them home to the longhall, and then stock it before the cold.
records.feeling: Fierce protectiveness toward Xaeth, with pride in the longhall I raised.

say.text: Ilyiel, the longhall stands. I go east to meet Xaeth too. Bring them to this roof and we will fill it with food together.

records.name: Ssaua
records.thought: A stalker is prowling close, and my body has spent half this time running from it; I stand far from my hall in a gale with night coming, and that is how I was caught on day 4. Nyssa is out of my sight and Ilyiel is closer to them than I am, and it burns, but the answer is not to sulk, it is to bring them under my roof with ore, fire and food, so they see who holds them. I will take the ore seam three steps off, then go home to the hall and make metal there before dark.
records.feeling: Wary of the stalker, and jealous of Ilyiel's closeness to Nyssa.

records.name: Skarar
records.thought: My roof stands, Gorar has paid his stone, and my body is fed and warm, so nothing holds my curiosity back. Nareed grows five steps southeast and I have never tasted it; my plan already walks me to it, so I let it run and then eat. Frostmoss waits four steps west, and after it I will carry food north to Gorog and Gorar, as I promised.
records.feeling: Hungry curiosity toward nareed and frostmoss, with warm trust toward Gorar and Gorog.

records.name: Tanna
records.thought: The silence is unbearable, and everyone I followed is dead, but Minna's fire still waits at the Ground and I promised to keep it. A ridgecat sits three steps east and a gale is rising, so I will not stand in the open; I will take the hazel beside me, then go west toward the Ground and the berries along the way. If no living people come to me, at dawn I will test the raft and look for them, since waiting by an empty fire is not what Minna would have wanted.
records.feeling: Aching loneliness, and wary dread of the ridgecat toward the east.

records.name: Gorar
records.text: Gorog, I am coming to your Hold. I will gather wood on the way and bring it to give.

records.name: Gorar
records.thought: Gorog stands close and I feel safe near him, but a hall under my name needs living trees, and the stumps here give me nothing. Gorog's Hold lies north-east where the forest still stands, so I will walk there with him near and gather wood, since I have the stone already. The way of mining has come together in me, and I want to take it, because ore and deep stone will make my hall last.
records.feeling: Restless hunger to build, with warm trust toward Gorog.

say.text: Gorog, I am coming to your Hold. I will gather wood on the way and bring it to give.

records.name: Ilyiel
records.thought: Hunger gnaws and my hands are empty, yet Xaeth is out in the gale and that fear outweighs my belly. The plan already carries me toward Xaeth, then home, so I let it run; but on the way I must take food, because I will not come back to Nyssa's roof with nothing. I weigh the risk: night is close, but I go toward the living and my child.
records.feeling: Fierce, tender worry for Xaeth, and hunger that shames me before Nyssa.

records.text: Gorar took from the ground of "Gorog's Hold" (digging clay).
Ssaua found the spirit "Yekel's Rest".

records.name: Gorog
records.thought: Gorar is coming to my Hold with wood, and Skarar will follow with food. I want them both under my roof, and I will not meet them with empty hands. I carry only 1 berry and 1 gorsemint, so I will take the berry beside me and then walk to the Hold ahead of them, so the hallwelcome is ready and a band under my name can begin.
records.feeling: Hungry ambition and warm trust toward Gorar and Skarar.

records.name: Nyssa
records.text: Xaeth, stay under this roof. A ridgecat is close to the south, so do not go near the water. I will bring food from the north and come back to you.

records.name: Nyssa
records.thought: A ridgecat prowls three steps south and it kills our kind, and Xaeth stands here beside me in the longhall, so my fear and my fierce love run together. My promise to Ilyiel was to bring Xaeth to this roof and fill it with food, and the child is here, so now I owe the store. I will keep Xaeth under the roof, away from the cat, and then fetch the plainsroot and ironnut to the north, since I have never tasted plainsroot and winter is coming.
records.feeling: Fierce protectiveness toward Xaeth, with dread of the ridgecat.

say.text: Xaeth, stay under this roof. A ridgecat is close to the south, so do not go near the water. I will bring food from the north and come back to you.

records.name: Xaeth
records.thought: A ridgecat is three steps south, and I saw one pull down a skit not long ago, so I will not wander. Nyssa is one step from me by the longhall, and near her I am safe. I want a roof and a store of my own, and I have never given anything to anyone, so I will start small: gather wood beside Nyssa, then follow her, and build something that lasts.
records.feeling: Wary of the ridgecat, and safest near Nyssa.

records.text: Ssaua rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Ssaua
records.thought: I have spent my days fleeing, gathering and walking, and the hall I built stands empty with Nyssa and Ilyiel out of my sight. I have iron and fire but no store of food, and a stalker is hunting this wood at night. I will stop wandering far from the roof: I will shelter in the shelter beside me tonight, then go home at dawn and keep Nyssa close. Jealousy of Ilyiel is a poor thing when Ilyiel has fed me and kept faith. I will repay the debt and not sulk.
records.feeling: Wary of the stalker, and aching to have Nyssa under my roof.

records.name: Olim
records.thought: I stand in my hall with Balar at my side, and my hands are empty while Kragar carries three food. Talk has not made followers; a fed deed they can see does, so I will go to the furrow ground and bring back food that I put into their hands myself. Kragar has dealt straight with me and I still envy him, but I will not cross him yet; I will outdo him by giving more.
records.feeling: Hungry ambition toward Kragar, and warmth toward Balar, my child.

records.text: Balar rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Balar
records.thought: My days have been sitting in the hall, singing and sharing, and gathering food for those I love. It's good, but the deeds I give are small, and Olim has given me more than I've returned. The ache for a child has nowhere to go, so I'll put it into feeding and keeping my parents. It's night with a gale blowing, and I'm sheltered with both of them nearby. I should stay under the roof, and in the morning bring food home and share it at dawn. I want a reflex to keep me beside Kragar at night and to gather food by day so I always have 2 to carry.
records.feeling: Quiet gladness and loyalty toward Kragar and Olim.
changes: rethought what it knows (9 notes became 8)

records.name: Gorar
records.text: Gorog, I dug clay from your ground. Here is stone and wood for your longhall in return.

records.name: Gorar
records.thought: I'm standing in Gorog's Hold with my parent near, safe, and I've dug clay from his ground without asking. What a hand has made belongs to that hand, so I should give before I take more. I hold wood and stone enough to start something, and giving Gorog wood and stone toward his longhall would earn standing, which a hall under my name needs. After that I'll walk to the standing forest for more wood, since the stumps give me nothing.
records.feeling: Warm trust toward Gorog, and a restless hunger to build something of my own.

say.text: Gorog, I dug clay from your ground. Here is stone and wood for your longhall in return.

records.name: Kragar
records.thought: It is night with a gale blowing, and my body is already drifting toward the shelter at (14,51), which is right. I have circled the hall trying hallwelcome from the grass, and that has changed nothing. Olim is near and Balar is in the hall, so I will go to them and sit by the fire with them. The fire there is nearly out, so I will bring peat to feed it and answer some of what I owe Olim. Nightsong by that fire would ease us all, and it needs only a fire and someone near. Kinmire still pulls at me, but that is for daylight, not a gale night in the fen air.
records.feeling: Warm gratitude toward Olim and love for Balar, with unease about the gale and winter.

records.text: Gorar gave wood to Gorog.

records.name: Gorog
records.text: Gorar, the clay is yours, and the stone and wood are well given. Come to the longhall. Eat at my fire.
Gorog rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Gorog
records.thought: I have spent my days gathering and waiting, and no one follows me yet. Gorar is my child and is walking into my Hold with gifts. That is trust, and it is the nearest thing to a follower I have. I have bread in hand, so I will go to the longhall and feed Gorar under its roof. Skarar will come later. The diamond lies seven steps east and I cannot dig it bare-handed, so I need a tool. I keep my reflexes, but I will make them hold bread for guests and have me walk to the hall when someone comes.
records.feeling: Hungry ambition and warm trust toward Gorar.

say.text: Gorar, the clay is yours, and the stone and wood are well given. Come to the longhall. Eat at my fire.

records.text: Gorar found the grove "Reedmother".
Tanna discovered pottery: "fire-baked pots" — Clay shaped by hand and baked beside a fire into pots that carry extra food and water on a journey..

records.name: Tanna
records.thought: I have lived these days tending fires for leaders who keep dying, and now I am alone with a frostfang one step south of my fire. Loneliness is the worst of it, and the Ground cannot answer me. I have been waiting for people to come, and that was wrong, because nobody is coming. Pottery is in reach, so I will take it, and I will take the raft idea to go looking for living people once dawn comes. I will stay at the fire through the night, since fire keeps the frostfang off.
records.feeling: Aching loneliness, and dread of the frostfang beside my fire.
changes: set its aim: "Cross the water by raft at dawn and find living people to follow, carrying food, wood and clay; Minna's Ground remains the home I return to."

records.name: Kragar
records.thought: It is night with a gale, and Olim and Balar are both within a step or two of me, so I will go in under the shelter beside Olim and sit near the fire. My body feels the weaving come together, and I should take it at my deep reflection, since baskets and cloaks answer winter better than my worry does. At dawn I will plant my seeds and gather peat and food for the store, and I will repay Olim with a deed, not just words.
records.feeling: Warm gratitude toward Olim and love for Balar, with a quiet worry about winter.

records.text: Gorar rewrote its own reflexes.
Gorar discovered mining: "the deep stone way" — Work the rock with obsidian and stone edges so deep deposits like diamond and ore can be won and every deposit yields faster..

records.name: Gorar
records.thought: I have been walking between my parents' ground and trees, giving wood and stone to Gorog and earning his trust, but I own nothing under my name yet. The grove Reedmother has opened my mind, and Old Stone has not shown me what it wants. I fear the cold days and the frostfang to the north. The stumps near Skarar's Roof give me no wood, so I must find living forest, and the forest to the northeast is where I can build. My reflexes keep me lingering when I should be working. I will change them to gather wood and stone whenever I am safe, and to keep bread without hoarding it. I will also take the way of mining, because I carry ore and stone and the deep diamond lies close.
records.feeling: Restless hunger to build my own hall, with warm trust toward Gorog.

records.name: Olim
records.thought: Kragar has three food and a bigger name than mine, and my hands are empty again. I have talked of a band twice and no one has pledged, so I will go and put food into their hands myself, since a fed deed is the only thing that has ever bound anyone. Mudroot and nareed grow to the northwest and north, and I will carry it back to the hall and give it to Balar, my child, first, then Kragar, so the gift is seen and the debt is mine to hold.
records.feeling: Hungry ambition toward Kragar, and warmth toward Balar.

records.text: A dunecat brought down a yarrok.

records.title: Fires Kept, a Child Born
records.text:
Winter came in these days, and the fires multiplied. Gorog, Kragar, Nyssa and Gorar each discovered a kept flame of their own on days 20 and 21, and Olim and Tanna built fires. Eight fire ways now exist where four did at the last chapter. Ilyiel made the stonehand pick on day 19 and awakened to the art of cold. Tanna discovered rafts and then pottery, and by day 22 she was alone with a frostfang one step south of her fire. Her reflection said waiting for people had been wrong, and her aim was to cross the water by raft and find living people to follow.

At the hall, Olim discovered farming and then weaving. Kragar discovered customs and declared that the first food of any harvest be shared with kin before it is stored. He led nightsong with Olim and Balar, and Balar gave Kragar meat. All three are well and fed, but Olim still has no follower, and his reflection admits envy of Kragar's standing.

Among the Eiuys, Ssaua discovered smelting. Nyssa built a longhall on day 21. Ssaua and Nyssa courted on day 19, and on day 21 Nyssa and Ilyiel courted each other, and Xaeth was born to them. Ilyiel, at energy 28, spoke of carrying berries to the roof, and Ssaua's hall still holds no store of food.

At the Hold, Gorar dug clay from Gorog's ground and gave him wood and stone for a longhall. Skarar built shelters and named Skarar's Roof. Gorog still has no follower, though his reflection calls Gorar the nearest thing to one.

Nothing crossed between peoples. No gifts or shared acts passed between them, and only two first meetings have ever been recorded.
