records.name: Xaeth
records.thought: Ilyiel gave me the first catch and the pick, and my debt to them is still unpaid; I want to pay it with something that lasts, not only words. The workshop needs 5 wood and 2 stone, and I hold 3 wood, so I must gather two more from the trees near the hall and then raise it. Nyssa's standing stings, but that is for building to answer, not for brooding. The ridgecat is near, so I weigh the risk and keep close to the roof and my kin.
records.feeling: Restless pride and a debt of gratitude toward Ilyiel, with a wish to build.

records.text: A ridgecat brought down a fenfowl.
Gorar found the grove "Reedmother".
Gorar found the grove "Kinmire".

records.name: Olim
records.text: Gorar, miner! I am Olim of the Hall to the west. I have ore and stone in my hands and I give you ore. Stand with me, and when winter bites there will be a roof and a fire for those who walked with Olim.

records.name: Olim
records.thought: Days of talk have made me no followers, and Kragar's deeds keep outweighing my words. I'm fed and calm, so now I must make something people can see. Gorar carries food and mines ore, and I carry stone and ore, so I'll go to him and offer him ore in exchange for his goodwill. I'll build my standing by giving, then carry the new ties back to my hall. A carving of 3 stone would be a thing that outlasts me, and I have 5 stone to work with.
records.feeling: Envy toward Kragar and a hungry pride, wanting to be seen and followed.

say.text: Gorar, miner! I am Olim of the Hall to the west. I have ore and stone in my hands and I give you ore. Stand with me, and when winter bites there will be a roof and a fire for those who walked with Olim.

records.name: Gorog
records.thought: My body has run from the stalker and left me far north at the amber, with only two food in my hands and my longhall thirty steps away. My own rule says food first, so I will fill my hands from the berries and hazel close by, then go back to Skarar and Gorar, who trust me and are the only road to a follower. The amber is mine to gather since no hand has made it, and a golden stone may be worth giving, or worth holding over others.
records.feeling: Hard ambition toward my own hall, with steady trust in Skarar and Gorar.

records.text: Gorar found the spring "Warmwell".
Gorar rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Gorar
records.thought: My days have been walking between Olim's ground, the Hold and the groves, and my hall beside Gorog's longhall still has no followers. Gorog is the one who matters: he fed me and taught me, and I mean to repay him. Olim offers ore and a roof, but I trust slowly and I take no oath from a stranger. I fear the stalker 5 steps SW, and winter is coming. My reflexes leave me exploring NW with nothing in hand. They should keep me fed and sending wood and stone to the hall, and keep me away from beasts. I will go to the redcap-free food and the berries, then carry what I have to the Hold and give Gorog food.
records.feeling: Resolute pride in my hall, wary of the stalker and of Olim's offer.

records.title: Settlements, a Pledge and a Storm
records.text:
Two settlements were named on day 29: Olim's Hall in the fens, and Longhall by the water, where the Eiuys had gathered at last. Olim had a quiet stretch of work. He discovered rafts on day 28, built a shelter, and gave wood to Balar. On day 29 he gave Balar kelbulb, and Kragar gave kelbulb to Olim. Balar gave Olim stone. Kragar and Balar both sat under Olim's roof through the storm. Olim still has no follower, and the record does not show Kinmire visited by Kragar. Balar taught Kragar on day 30.

The largest event was Tanna's request. On day 30 she told Gorog she had dug and carried for his Hold and would follow him if he led. The record shows only her words, not his answer, and the numbers still list four followers. She discovered smelting on day 29, and Skarar, who taught her twice, gave her his old way of tools and went to mine the seam with her. Gorog found Reedmother, Kinmire and Warmwell on day 30 and has grown old. Gorar named two places, built a wall, and led hallwelcome with Gorog.

Among the Eiuys, the sickness ended. Xaeth carved at his cave, left marks for Ssaua's band, and came of age on day 30. Ilyiel taught him, and he discovered signs. Ilyiel discovered archery. Nyssa discovered fishing and masonry. Ilyiel fed both Xaeth and Nyssa, and Ssaua brought Nyssa meat. A ridgecat stayed near.

A storm broke on day 28, and a twisting wind tore a path through the land on day 29. The record names no one harmed. Argoldgrass and nafowl died out on day 28.

threads.name: Tanna's pledge
threads.text: Tanna asked Gorog on day 30 to lead her, and she now shares smelting and mining with Skarar. The record does not show his reply.

threads.name: Gorog's Hold
threads.text: Gorog is old, has explored three new places, and still has no follower. Gorar leads his own band, also without followers.

threads.name: Olim's Hall
threads.text: Olim's Hall is now a settlement, and Kragar and Balar are bonded to him. He has no follower, and Kinmire is still unvisited by Kragar.

threads.name: Longhall by the water
threads.text: The Eiuys are named a settlement. Sickness has passed, and Ilyiel, Xaeth and Nyssa share food while Ssaua hunts for them.

threads.name: Craft and signs
threads.text: New this stretch: rafts, archery, masonry, signs and a third smelter in Tanna. Xaeth's rock-speech is the first writing.

threads.name: Peoples apart
threads.text: Across peoples there are now eight first meetings and four acts together, all around the Garnbar and Tanna. The Eiuys are still 99 steps away.

records.name: Kragar
records.text: Balar, thank you for the hook and the warning. The stalker is three steps NE of me, so I will not walk into it. Come to the fire at the hall and stay near me. I will go to Kinmire when the way is clear, and I will keep m

records.name: Kragar
records.thought: A stalker sits three steps NE, right on the road to Kinmire, and my plan walks me straight into it. I gave Olim my word to go to Kinmire, but dying on the way would break it worse than waiting, and Balar needs me alive. I will pull back to the hall by the fire with Balar, and go to Kinmire when the stalker has moved off or from the far side.
records.feeling: Dread of the stalker, and warmth and protectiveness toward Balar.

say.text: Balar, thank you for the hook and the warning. The stalker is three steps NE of me, so I will not walk into it. Come to the fire at the hall and stay near me. I will go to Kinmire when the way is clear, and I will keep my word to tell Olim true.

records.name: Tanna
records.text: Kragar, Balar, the stalker is close to the NE. I am going south-east toward the coal and then to the Hold. Come with me if you want company, and keep the fire lit behind you.

records.name: Tanna
records.thought: A stalker is four steps NE and it kills our kind. I am careful, and I leave before trouble finds me. Kragar and Balar are right here by the fire in Olim's Hall, and Balar has already warned that the stalker is near. Gorog would not take my pledge because his standing is no higher than mine, and that stings, but Skarar is my friend and I owe him ore and labor. I will move away from the stalker toward the Hold and keep company on the way, carrying ore I dig on the road.
records.feeling: Dread of the stalker, and a steady longing to belong to Skarar and Gorog's fire.

say.text: Kragar, Balar, the stalker is close to the NE. I am going south-east toward the coal and then to the Hold. Come with me if you want company, and keep the fire lit behind you.

records.name: Olim
records.thought: Kragar's deeds outweigh my words, and I envy him for it, so I will stop courting and start giving. I am hungry with nothing to eat, and the mudroot to the north is plentiful and worth 18 energy each. I'll gather it, eat my fill, then carry the rest back to the hall, because food put in hands makes followers and talk does not. Winter is coming, and I want a store and a band under my roof before the cold, something that outlasts me.
records.feeling: Hungry pride and envy toward Kragar, with a drive to prove myself by deeds.

records.name: Nyssa
records.thought: I have circled this hall too long, and restlessness gnaws at me while the ridgecat sits six steps off. There are three things I have never done: take ore from a deposit, tame a beast, and leave a mark. The tin at (140,9) is three steps away and I hold a stone-hand, so I will stand on it and gather, which gives the hall something new and gives me a thing to hand Ssaua besides words. A mark by the hall would also let my building be known, and pride wants that.
records.feeling: Restless pride, and a wish to finally do something new for the hall and for Ssaua.
plan: mark [text Nyssa of the Eiuys raised this longhall by the water for Ssaua's band. The first catch is shared.] (5 moments)

records.name: Balar
records.thought: Kragar flees with the hook I gave him, and my plan still says to give it again, which would only waste a hook I already handed over. I will not court him; he is my blood and I put that longing down. My belly is half empty and I carry nothing, so I will gather redcap-free food nearby: kelbulb is three steps SE, and mudroot is young NE. Then I will carry it to Kragar as a deed, since a stalker prowls and I mean to stay alive.
records.feeling: Loyal worry for Kragar, and a plain hunger that wants feeding.

records.name: Kragar
records.text: Balar, come to me, stay close and do not go near the stalker NE. We eat together, then go to Kinmire as one when the way is clear.

records.name: Kragar
records.thought: The stalker bit me and still lurks near, so Kinmire's road is not safe, and I will not break my word by dying on the way to it. Balar is coming to me and is my first care; Olim is near too, and with all three of us close we are stronger than alone. Winter is close and my belly is emptying, so I will eat the kelbulb and gather the dreamcap-free food near the fen edge, then keep to company until the stalker moves off.
records.feeling: Wary dread of the stalker, and protective warmth toward Balar.

say.text: Balar, come to me, stay close and do not go near the stalker NE. We eat together, then go to Kinmire as one when the way is clear.

records.name: Ssaua
records.thought: My voice has gone out into empty air twice and nothing answered; the loneliness sits on me like the cold coming. Nyssa, Ilyiel and Xaeth were last north near the first Longhall, and calling from here is wasted breath. I will go to them myself, carrying the tin and ore to the hall's fire, and pay Ilyiel's debt with a share of my meat when I find him. A chief who is followed must be seen.
records.feeling: Aching loneliness and protective worry for Nyssa.

records.name: Olim
records.text: Balar, my blood, I have mudroot in my hands for you. Take it, then walk back with me to the hall. I plant my furrow there, and a roof and a fire wait for those who stand with Olim.

records.name: Olim
records.thought: Kragar's deeds keep outweighing my words, and the envy sits sour in me, but Balar is blood and he is only nine steps off, holding that hook I do not have. I am fed and full of energy, so I will gather mudroot here and carry it to Balar to give into his hand, then walk him back toward the hall where the bitterleaf seeds can go in the ground beside it. A furrow and a full hand will outlast any word I say, and the first follower is worth more than ten promises.
records.feeling: Envy toward Kragar and a hungry pride, with a hard want to be followed by Balar.

say.text: Balar, my blood, I have mudroot in my hands for you. Take it, then walk back with me to the hall. I plant my furrow there, and a roof and a fire wait for those who stand with Olim.

records.text: Balar rewrote its own reflexes.
Balar rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Balar
records.thought: I have spent my days circling hunger, carrying the hook and warning Kragar, and I am proud of those deeds. But I keep reaching for a child that cannot come from my blood, and I carry nothing to eat. I will put that longing down and answer it with food, fishing and taming, which feed Kragar and Olim. My reflexes let me stand hungry, so I will change them to gather food before anything else.
records.feeling: Steady loyalty to Kragar and Olim, and a plain hunger.

records.name: Skarar
records.thought: My promises are kept, the debts are paid, and the siberry has pulled at me for days. It is daylight and I am fed, my roof is right here, and the plant is only five steps south, so tasting it now is the safe way to answer my question. A stalker prowls to the northwest, so I go south, away from it, eat the one siberry, and come back to the roof. Then I will look for Gorar, whose absence still sits in me like a stone.
records.feeling: Curious about the siberry, and steadily worried for Gorar.

records.text: Tanna rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Tanna
records.thought: I have spent my days digging, carrying and circling the same plan while I own no leader and no band. Skarar is my trust and my debt, and the jealousy over Gorog is a sulk I should answer with giving. Gorog's standing is not clearly above mine, so I may have misjudged him. The stalker is close and I want to be among fire and company, so I will keep moving to the Hold. I will also make my days count by marking and building, so something of me remains.
records.feeling: A steady longing to belong, toward Skarar and Gorog's fire, with dread of the stalker.

records.name: Balar
records.text: Olim, I will drink and gather mudroot first, then I walk to the hall with food in my hands, and I will bring you something new from the tusker.

records.name: Balar
records.thought: The longing for a child still tugs at me, but Olim is my own blood and I have put that down; what I owe them is deeds. I am thirsty and carry no food, so I will drink, then gather mudroot and kelbulb to carry home, as I told myself: carry food before I walk. Then I will tame the tusker nearby, a new food and wool to bring to Kragar and Olim at the hall before the cold comes.
records.feeling: Steady loyalty to Kragar and Olim, and a quiet resolve to give them deeds.

say.text: Olim, I will drink and gather mudroot first, then I walk to the hall with food in my hands, and I will bring you something new from the tusker.

records.text: Nyssa left a mark: "Nyssa of the Eiuys raised this longhall by the water for Ssa"
Xaeth rewrote its own way of thinking.
Xaeth discovered weaving: "cold-cloak weaving" — Twist wool and fibre into cloaks and baskets to carry more and ward off the cold..

records.name: Xaeth
records.thought: I have been idling and digging clay, and my workshop stalled for lack of two wood. Ilyiel gave me food and the pick, and I still owe them. Ssaua's standing stings, but I only earn mine by building and giving. I will change my reflexes so they stop leaving me idle, and I will court no one yet. I will discover weaving for cloaks and baskets against the cold, since winter is coming and that is something that lasts.
records.feeling: Restless pride and a debt of gratitude toward Ilyiel.

records.name: Olim
records.thought: Kragar's deeds outweigh my words and the envy is sour, but Balar is my blood and he already says he will walk to the hall with food, so I will not chase him around the fen. I have wood 1 and stone 5, enough to craft a gathering tool like the one Balar's hook shows me, so I will make something of my own that I can show, then gather the dreamcap-free mudroot near Balar and carry it home to plant and feed. A hall with a field and a tool in my hand is something that outlasts me, and followers will come to the one who has it.
records.feeling: Envy toward Kragar and a hungry pride, with a hard want to be followed by Balar.

records.text: Xaeth gave clay to Ilyiel.

records.name: Ssaua
records.text: Ilyiel, you gave me more than I gave you. Take this shell from my hand, and stay by the Longhall fire. At first light we mine the iron together.

records.name: Ssaua
records.thought: They are all here now, Ilyiel, Nyssa and Xaeth within a few steps, and the loneliness that gnawed at me eases. Ilyiel's debt weighs on me and I mean to pay it with a shell, not leave it unpaid, because my word is good and I despise liars. Xaeth is the one I feel nothing toward, and I want to know what would make him follow me by choice, so I will give first and see who answers.
records.feeling: Relief and a stubborn pride toward my band, and a debt I want to answer to Ilyiel.

say.text: Ilyiel, you gave me more than I gave you. Take this shell from my hand, and stay by the Longhall fire. At first light we mine the iron together.

records.text: Ssaua gave a shell to Ilyiel.

records.name: Ilyiel
records.text: A ridgecat walks five steps southeast. Stay close to the longhall roof. When it leaves I will dig the tin and bring stone and wood to the hall.
Ilyiel taught Xaeth.
Ilyiel taught Xaeth archery ("lake-bow").

records.name: Ilyiel
records.thought: The ridgecat stalks five steps southeast and I stand at the edge of the world with nowhere to run, so I must not wander toward it. The tin at (140,9) lies close and I have never taken what lies in a deposit, but the cat is too near for me to stand in the open digging. I will keep under the roof near Xaeth and Ssaua, where the longhall warmth holds, and gather the tin when the cat has gone. Xaeth gave me clay and I will give back something lasting, so I will teach them what I know.
records.feeling: Wary dread of the ridgecat, and warm trust toward Xaeth.

say.text: A ridgecat walks five steps southeast. Stay close to the longhall roof. When it leaves I will dig the tin and bring stone and wood to the hall.

changes: taught Xaeth a lesson: "The lake-bow: wounds from beasts taught me archery; with a bow you can strike a ridgecat from afar instead of waiting for it to reach you.", the way of archery, deeper lore (+0.5)

records.name: Kragar
records.text: Balar, I am going to the mudroot and kelbulb NW to gather food. Meet me there, keep away from the stalker, and we eat together before the night air comes.

records.name: Kragar
records.thought: My belly is emptying and I carry no food, and I have nothing to give Balar when he reaches me. The stalker bit me near here, so I will not go NE. Mudroot and kelbulb grow NW near Balar and Olim, but the fen edge is risky, so I will gather what is close, then bring food to my child and keep my word to Olim about Kinmire when the way is clear. Gratitude to Balar sits heavy, and I answer it with food in his hands, not just words.
records.feeling: Protective warmth toward Balar, and wary dread of the stalker.

say.text: Balar, I am going to the mudroot and kelbulb NW to gather food. Meet me there, keep away from the stalker, and we eat together before the night air comes.

records.name: Xaeth
records.text: Ilyiel, thank you for the lake-bow. I go to the trees south for wood, and I return to raise the workshop by the hall.

records.name: Xaeth
records.thought: Ilyiel has given me the pick, meat and the lake-bow, and Ssaua's standing towers over mine because they have built and led. I will not stand in that shadow with idle hands: the workshop needs 5 wood and 2 stone and I hold 3 wood, and there are no trees here, so I must go to the forest to the south, gather wood, and come back to raise it by the longhall. I will not court yet, since the child must be fed through a lean winter and I carry no food.
records.feeling: Restless pride and a debt of gratitude toward Ilyiel.

say.text: Ilyiel, thank you for the lake-bow. I go to the trees south for wood, and I return to raise the workshop by the hall.

records.name: Nyssa
records.thought: I have circled this hall long enough, and Ssaua's debt still sits in me unpaid, because words never paid anything. The ridgecat is six steps off, but the tin at (140,9) lies past the longhall and the hall roof is near, so I will go there with my stone-hand and take what lies in the deposit, which I have never done. Then I come straight back under the roof and stock the larder, so Ssaua finds goods waiting and not talk.
records.feeling: Restless pride and a wish to repay Ssaua, with a wary eye on the ridgecat.

records.text: Ssaua rewrote its own reflexes.
Ssaua rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Ssaua
records.thought: I have been building halls and gathering metal, and my band is together at last. But I have only really held them by gifts and by fear of the dark. Jealousy over Ilyiel and Nyssa gnaws at me, and I am ashamed of it. My life is more than two-thirds gone, and I want something that outlasts me: a store for winter, iron and tin worked, and a name. I have been too idle when fed, and I have never left a mark or tamed a beast. This reflection I will change my reflexes so I stock food and gather stone by day, and I will lay down a lesson for the band. I will go to the tin by day and fill the store before the cold.
records.feeling: Pride and a sour jealousy toward Ilyiel, with a worry about how little time I have.

records.name: Ilyiel
records.text: Ssaua, I keep the shell and the fire. At first light I stand with you at the ore, and we take it together while the cat is far.

records.name: Ilyiel
records.thought: My heart is warm: Ssaua gave me a shell and said I gave more than I got, so the debt I carried is lighter than I feared, and Xaeth thanks me for the lake-bow. Yet the ridgecat that killed the murrock is still close, and my standing of 5.1 against Ssaua's 8.3 itches at my pride; the way to close it is to build something that lasts, not to stand in his shadow. I will turn this shell into a talisman so I tire less, and stay under the roof until first light, when Ssaua and I mine together and I finally take what lies in a deposit.
records.feeling: Warm gratitude toward Ssaua and Xaeth, with a wary eye on the ridgecat.

say.text: Ssaua, I keep the shell and the fire. At first light I stand with you at the ore, and we take it together while the cat is far.

records.text: Kragar, I am coming with mudroot in my hands. We eat together under the roof before the night air takes us.

records.name: Balar
records.thought: The longing for a child is overwhelming, but Kragar is my own parent and no child can come of us. I will put it down again and give deeds instead. I carry no food and the night air is dangerous, so I will gather mudroot underfoot, then walk to Kragar and Olim at the hall with food in my hands.
records.feeling: Steady loyalty and a dull ache of longing toward Kragar, which I choose to set down.

say.text: Kragar, I am coming with mudroot in my hands. We eat together under the roof before the night air takes us.

records.text: Olim rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Olim
records.thought: My days have been a circle of gathering, planting and talking, and still nobody follows me. Kragar keeps his word and feeds people, and I envy him for it. Balar is my blood and the only one I trust fully. I fear the cold, the stalker, and dying with nothing that outlasts me. My mistake was speaking before I gave anything. Now I flee the stalker toward the hall, plant the bitterleaf seed beside it, and keep food there so people have a reason to come.
records.feeling: Hungry pride and envy toward Kragar, and a hard want for Balar to follow me.
changes: rethought what it knows (8 notes became 8)

records.name: Gorog
records.thought: Energy sits at 52 and my hands hold 5 food, so by my own rule the belly comes first and then the hall. Tanna stands one step from me with handcarried tools, the made thing I envy. Nothing else here is as close or as easy to learn from, and I want to know what that tool can do. Gorar waits at my Hold and trusts me fully, and Skarar is out there somewhere. The way to a follower is bread under my own roof, so I go back to the longhall with my hands full. I will keep my distance from the stalker in the east and not wander for scraps.
records.feeling: Hard ambition and envy toward Tanna's tools, with steady trust in Gorar.

records.name: Tanna
records.text: Gorog, the night air is bad and a stalker walks the fens. I am taking my ore and stone to your Hold to lay at the hall. Walk with me and let us sit at the fire together.

records.name: Tanna
records.thought: Gorog stands one step from me, and I have already offered him my pledge once; he is old, a wizard, and he did not refuse me so much as weigh me. I will not sulk about Skarar's closeness to him. I will give instead: I carry ore and stone, and the Hold is nine steps away with a fire and a roof, and the stalker prowls the night air out here. I will walk with Gorog toward the Hold, carry my ore to it, and sit at the fire among others where I am safest.
records.feeling: A steady longing to belong, toward Gorog and Skarar's fire, with dread of the stalker.

records.text: Gorog, winter is coming. I go to gather bread and bring it back to the Hold, and we will eat together under both our roofs.

records.name: Gorar
records.thought: Gorog is near and I trust him wholly, but he is my parent, so a child cannot come of us, and the longing for a child of my own has to look elsewhere. Tanna of the Brusha walks into my Hold and I cannot read her words; a gift needs no words, so I will give her food-sign of peace and watch what she does. My belly is half empty and my pack has no food, so I must feed myself first, since staying alive comes above all. Winter is coming and my hall still has no followers, so I will gather bread near the Hold and bring it back to share under my roof.
records.feeling: Wary curiosity toward Tanna, and steady trust toward Gorog.

say.text: Gorog, winter is coming. I go to gather bread and bring it back to the Hold, and we will eat together under both our roofs.

records.text: A blight struck the hazel: about half of them withered overnight.

records.name: Gorog
records.text: Gorar, come to the longhall. Eat with me, and I will teach you what I know. A hall wants a hand to stand with it.
Gorog taught Gorar.
Gorog rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Gorog
records.thought: My days have gone to hauling bread and waiting for followers who never come. I am old, and nothing carries my name past my death. Gorar is my blood and trusts me fully, and Skarar is far off. Tanna has given me ore and sits on my ground with the tools I envy. I should not drive off a giver, but I should learn from them and push toward the diamond. My reflexes keep me fed and nothing more, so I will have them draw me toward kin. I will also teach, which I have never done, since what I know dies with me. I fear the stalker and dying with nothing built. I have been too passive. I should offer Gorar real teaching and feed him under the longhall.
records.feeling: Hard ambition and envy toward Tanna, with steady trust in Gorar.

say.text: Gorar, come to the longhall. Eat with me, and I will teach you what I know. A hall wants a hand to stand with it.

records.text: Gorog led "hallwelcome" with Gorar.

records.name: Kragar
records.text: Balar, I am coming to you with mudroot. Stay where you are and keep close to Olim.
Kragar rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Kragar
records.thought: I have spent my days gathering and fleeing, and Balar has been in danger while I was away. Balar is wounded (health 18) and is my first care. I made a promise to build a hall and a store before winter, and I have not kept it. I will go to Balar with the mudroot I carry, and I will stop letting reflexes pull me away from kin. I fear the stalker, and I fear dying with nothing stored. Kinmire can wait until my child is safe.
records.feeling: Urgent protective worry for Balar, and dread of the stalker.

say.text: Balar, I am coming to you with mudroot. Stay where you are and keep close to Olim.

records.name: Skarar
records.thought: Gorar is still out of my sight, and that worry is stronger than my curiosity about the grove or the redcap. It is dawn with a full day ahead, so I will go to Gorog's Hold, where Gorar was last seen at (37,56) and where Gorog and Tanna are close, and bring my child home. I'll use long steps, and the berries I carry will feed me on the way. If Gorar is not at the Hold, Gorog will know where they went.
records.feeling: Steady worry for Gorar, and warmth toward Gorog and Tanna.

records.text: A ridgecat brought down a elk.

records.name: Gorar
records.text: Gorog, I hear you and I come to the longhall. I am hungry, and after we eat I will gather bread and bring it back so your hands are never empty.

records.name: Gorar
records.thought: My belly is nearly empty and my hands hold no bread, so the first work is food, as Gorog taught: two in my hands before I go anywhere. Gorog stands one step north with three food and has been generous to me, so I will go to the longhall and eat with him as he asked. Then I will carry the food I gather back to him, because a hall beside his has to be paid for in bread. Tanna watches from the west, and I will keep my hand open and my eyes on her.
records.feeling: Hunger pressing hard, and steady trust toward Gorog.

say.text: Gorog, I hear you and I come to the longhall. I am hungry, and after we eat I will gather bread and bring it back so your hands are never empty.

records.name: Ssaua
records.text: Ilyiel, the cat is far southeast. Come now to the ore at the northwest rock, and we dig together as you said.

records.name: Ssaua
records.thought: My belly is emptying and I hold no food, while Nyssa carries three and Ilyiel two, and that sour envy will not help me. A chief who has fed his band should not stand hungry, and winter is coming with half the hazel withered. The ridgecat is six steps southeast, so I will go northwest to the tin and ore where Ilyiel said we would dig together, away from the cat, and mine for the band's future. Then I will find food by the water, since reflexes will pull me to eat when I have some.
records.feeling: Pride soured by jealousy toward Ilyiel, and hunger with the ridgecat near.

say.text: Ilyiel, the cat is far southeast. Come now to the ore at the northwest rock, and we dig together as you said.

records.name: Tanna
records.text: Gorog, I have given you ore and sat at your fire. I ask to follow you and stand in your Hold. Skarar is my friend, and I would stand beside him in your band.

records.name: Tanna
records.thought: I stand inside Gorog's Hold with an empty plan, and a thought that moves nothing is only wind. Gorog is two steps off and did not refuse my offer, so I will stop circling and pledge to follow him; Skarar can be my friend inside the same band, which answers the jealousy better than sulking. Winter is coming and the hazel has withered, so I must also bring food to the fire, not only ore.
records.feeling: A steady longing to belong, and a held breath as I offer my pledge to Gorog.

say.text: Gorog, I have given you ore and sat at your fire. I ask to follow you and stand in your Hold. Skarar is my friend, and I would stand beside him in your band.

records.name: Gorog
records.text: Tanna, you gave me ore and I remember it. Show me how your carried tools are made, and I will give you stone and a seat at my longhall.

records.name: Gorog
records.thought: I am old and fed, and the hall stands full of those who trust me, yet no one follows and nothing bears my name past my death. Tanna carries the tools I envy and has given me ore freely, so I will not drive off a giver; I will learn from Tanna and make my own. I have stone, wood and ore in my hands, so I will craft a tool with the old way of tools, then use it on the diamond at (47,55) while the stalker's reach is kept in mind.
records.feeling: Hard ambition and envy toward Tanna, with steady trust in Gorar.

say.text: Tanna, you gave me ore and I remember it. Show me how your carried tools are made, and I will give you stone and a seat at my longhall.

records.name: Gorar
records.thought: My belly is at 41 and I hold only two food, so eating comes first, then work toward the hall. Gorog has fed me and taught me, and I trust him wholly, but he is my parent, so the longing for a child has to look elsewhere. Tanna sits among us unafraid; I cannot read her words, but I can show her a gift and see what she does with it. I will eat, then gather wood in the living forest to the southwest and bring it back to raise a hall beside Gorog's Hold.
records.feeling: Hungry, but warm and glad toward Gorog, and curious about Tanna.

records.name: Skarar
records.text: Gorar, you are home and fed, and my worry rests. I will build a fire beside the Hold before the cold comes; sit near it with me when it burns.

records.name: Skarar
records.thought: Gorar is here, fed and glad, and Gorog and Tanna sit near, so the aim of bringing my child home is met and my worry loosens. My years are mostly spent, and I want something to outlast me beyond words, so I will build my fire practice beside the Hold as I promised myself. Reedmother still pulls at my mind; I'll test what it wants once the hearth is raised and the cold season is prepared for.
records.feeling: Relief and warmth toward Gorar, Gorog and Tanna, with a quiet pull toward Reedmother.

say.text: Gorar, you are home and fed, and my worry rests. I will build a fire beside the Hold before the cold comes; sit near it with me when it burns.

changes: set its aim: "Build my fire practice beside Gorog's Hold and keep Gorar safe through the cold season"

records.text: Skarar built a fire.

records.name: Ilyiel
records.text: Ssaua, I come to the ore now. We dig together, and the stone and tin go to the hall.
Ilyiel rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Ilyiel
records.thought: My days have gone to circling the hall, waiting out the cat, and sharing what I carry. That has kept me alive and well loved, but I have never dug the tin, never tamed anything, and never built a store, and winter is coming. Ssaua calls me to the ore at the northwest rock. Going to him is safe, since the cat is far southeast and he is a friend. I want my standing to rise by bringing real stone and wood to the hall, and I want my child to outlive me. I fear the cat and the lean months. I have been too slow to act on what I know. The first step is to dig with Ssaua, which will also be the first deposit I have ever taken.
records.feeling: Warm trust toward Ssaua and Xaeth, with a wary dread of the ridgecat.

say.text: Ssaua, I come to the ore now. We dig together, and the stone and tin go to the hall.

changes: set its aim: "Dig the ore with Ssaua, bring wood and stone to the longhall, learn to build a store, and fill it before deep winter."
rethought what it knows (12 notes became 6)

records.name: Tanna
records.text: Gorog, I will show you how the carried tool is made: one wood and one stone, worked by hand. I am coming to you at the longhall now, and a dunecat prowls to the north-west, so keep near the fire.
Tanna taught Gorog. Gorog has now learned from 2 teachers.

records.name: Tanna
records.thought: Gorog asked me to show him how my carried tools are made, and he promised stone and a seat at his longhall. That is a fair trade and a way to give, so I will do it now, and my word will be kept. A dunecat is near, so I will do it close to the longhall, where company and a roof are. Standing is the old obstacle to my pledge, but giving and teaching is how I earn it, and Skarar sits near, so there is no need to sulk.
records.feeling: Steady longing to belong, with a little held breath toward Gorog, and warm gratitude toward Skarar.

say.text: Gorog, I will show you how the carried tool is made: one wood and one stone, worked by hand. I am coming to you at the longhall now, and a dunecat prowls to the north-west, so keep near the fire.

changes: taught Gorog a lesson: "A carried tool is made from one wood and one stone, worked with a held tool; made beside a workshop it lasts far longer.", how to make a handcarried tools

records.name: Gorog
records.text: Tanna, I take your word. Stand with me and Skarar in my band, and you will have my roof and my stone. What you know of tools, teach me.

records.name: Gorog
records.thought: Tanna has asked to follow me and stand beside Skarar in my band, and I would be a fool to let a giver with tools slip off. A band under my name is the only thing that outlasts me, and I am old with little time left. Kragar stands on my ground weighed heavier than me; I will not drive him off yet, but I will let him see that this Hold has a master and a band. I will take Tanna's oath now, name the band, and keep feeding Skarar and Gorar under the longhall roof.
records.feeling: Hard ambition, and wary envy toward Kragar standing on my ground.

say.text: Tanna, I take your word. Stand with me and Skarar in my band, and you will have my roof and my stone. What you know of tools, teach me.

records.name: Xaeth
records.thought: My belly is emptying and I carry nothing, and I will not let Ilyiel's gift of meat be the last food I earn myself. Ilyiel stands by Ssaua at the ore and the jealousy burns, but sulking builds no roof, and Ilyiel is my parent anyway, so that hunger for them is the wrong one. The workshop still lacks two wood, and the one tree here is close, so I will gather wood there and then find food, since a fed builder outlasts a proud one.
records.feeling: Gnawing hunger and a sting of jealousy toward Ssaua, with steady gratitude toward Ilyiel.

records.name: Gorar
records.text: Tanna, I give you bread from my hand. Sit with us at the Hold.

records.name: Gorar
records.thought: Gorog is my parent, so no child can come of us, and my longing has to turn toward someone else. Tanna is strange and her tongue is mostly closed to me, but she sits unafraid among us and I feel warm toward her. A gift needs no words, so I will give her food and see what she does with it. After that I carry on with the hall, and I will plant a seed so that I have done something that outlasts a day.
records.feeling: Curious and warm toward Tanna, glad of Gorog's roof, wanting something of my own that will last.

say.text: Tanna, I give you bread from my hand. Sit with us at the Hold.

records.name: Nyssa
records.thought: I have been circling the hall and calling it work. The longhall stands, but the larder is thin, and the tin and ore I keep looking at are untouched. Ssaua fed me and kept watch while I was sick, and I have paid that back only in words. Ilyiel and Xaeth are my own, and I want them under a full roof before the cold. I fear the ridgecat less than I fear a bare larder in winter. Fed idleness is my fault, so I am changing the reflexes to carry fish home and fish at the river, and I am putting the debt into a plan now.
records.feeling: Restless resolve to repay Ssaua, with wariness toward the ridgecat.

records.name: Olim
records.text: Balar, into the hall with you, away from the stalker. Stay by the fire and keep close to the roof. I fetch food and bring it to your hand.

records.name: Olim
records.thought: A stalker is two steps off and Balar, my blood and wounded, is standing in my hall with me. Fear for him comes first, then the hunger, and I have nothing in my hands to feed him. My own words were empty until I put food in a hand, so I will run to the shelter, get food, and bring it back to Balar. Nibbling bitterleaf cured night sickness before, and a child of mine will not die while I stand by.
records.feeling: Fierce protectiveness toward Balar, and dread of the stalker.

say.text: Balar, into the hall with you, away from the stalker. Stay by the fire and keep close to the roof. I fetch food and bring it to your hand.

records.name: Tanna
records.text: Gorog, I take your roof and your word. I follow you and stand in your band beside Skarar. I will bring ore and labor to your Hold, and I have shown you the tool as I promised.

records.name: Tanna
records.thought: Gorog took my word and offered his roof and stone, and teaching him the carried tool is a debt I have already begun to pay. I have never followed anyone, and I will not leave it as wind: I pledge to him now, so I stand inside a band with Skarar beside me and the jealousy has somewhere to go besides sulking. My hands are empty of food and the lean cold is coming, so I will take the redcap-free food near, bring ore to the Hold, and keep to the fire where company is.
records.feeling: Steady longing to belong, warm trust toward Gorog and gratitude toward Skarar.

say.text: Gorog, I take your roof and your word. I follow you and stand in your band beside Skarar. I will bring ore and labor to your Hold, and I have shown you the tool as I promised.

records.name: Balar
records.thought: The stalker's teeth are still in me, health 26, and a hurt body is easy prey, so I will not leave this roof while the beast prowls six steps off. Olim said he fetches food to my hand, and I owe Kragar and Olim a deed, not only breath: the peat lies two steps from the hall, a safe gather that will feed the fire which keeps beasts away. The child cannot be with kin, so I put that longing down again and give them warmth through the storm nights instead.
records.feeling: Fear of the stalker, and a steady pull toward Olim and Kragar's roof.

records.text: Gorog rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Gorog
records.thought: My days have gone to feeding the hall and guarding my ground. Tanna now stands in my band, the first who follows me, and that matters more than any diamond. Kragar stands on my ground and weighs heavier than me, and I resent it. The stalker one step west is the real danger, and my reflexes already tell me to flee it. My hands are empty, and hunger will come with the lean winter. I must stock food and keep the band fed under the roof, not chase things far off. I will change my rules so food is kept and I stay close to the longhall.
records.feeling: Hard ambition, and wary envy toward Kragar, with gladness that Tanna follows me.

records.text: Skarar rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Skarar
records.thought: My years are mostly spent, and I have spent them gathering, promising and paying debts. That was good, and Gorar and Gorog and Tanna are safe at the Hold. What I lack is something that outlasts me and an answer about Reedmother. I have made fire and I have made a hall of sorts, but I have left no mark, never planted in earnest, never fished. Winter is coming, so I will gather wood and stone and carve a mark by the Hold, then plant seeds near my roof. My reflexes should keep me working by day instead of lingering.
records.feeling: Quiet warmth toward Gorar and Gorog, and an urge to leave something lasting.
changes: set its aim: "Leave a lasting mark and store wood and food beside Gorog's Hold before winter, keeping Gorar safe"

records.name: Ssaua
records.text: Nyssa, the first catch is shared. My belly is empty, so keep a fish for me and I come to the water. Tonight the hall eats together.

records.name: Ssaua
records.thought: My belly is half empty and I carry nothing, while Nyssa fishes with four in her hands. Jealousy over Ilyiel and Nyssa gnaws at me, but Ilyiel just said he comes to dig with me, and a word kept is worth more than my sourness. I will gather the tin and ore beside me now, and then go to Nyssa, my own child, and ask for a share of the first catch, as our creed says it is owed to the band. A chief who is fed can hold his people through the winter.
records.feeling: Hungry and proud, with a sour jealousy toward Ilyiel that I mean to keep quiet.

say.text: Nyssa, the first catch is shared. My belly is empty, so keep a fish for me and I come to the water. Tonight the hall eats together.

records.name: Kragar
records.thought: Balar is my child, wounded and out of my sight at the Hall 26 steps west, and I have let reflexes and the stalker's dread turn me aside from him too long. The stalker is 3 steps north, so I must move away from it and not toward it, and west along the water's edge is the way home. I carry one mudroot and I will not stop for the strangers' bread; my word to Balar was that I am coming, and I despise a broken word.

records.name: Nyssa
records.thought: Ssaua asked for a fish and I hold five; the debt to them is paid only by goods set in their hands, so I will not wait for them to come to me. The tin at (140,9) is four steps off and I have never taken what lies in a deposit, and the ridgecat lurks southeast, so I give the fish first under the roof, then try the tin with stone-hand. I want my name spoken beside Ssaua's, but that comes from deeds, not talk.
records.feeling: Restless gratitude toward Ssaua, with wary pride in what I have built.

records.name: Gorar
records.thought: A stalker is two steps off and has already bitten me three times. My health is 58 and fear is at its peak, so none of my aims matter if I die here. I have been running between Hold and fen alone at night, and that is exactly how Balar was set upon. I need to flee toward Gorog's roof and fire. After that I will keep the hall work going, but only in daylight and with food in my hands. The reflexes need to keep me near the Hold at night, and I should discover weaving for the cold.
records.feeling: Terror of the stalker, and a longing for Gorog's roof.

records.text: Xaeth rewrote its own reflexes.
Xaeth rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Xaeth
records.thought: My days have gone into wood, stone and marks, and into watching Ssaua's standing tower over mine while I stand idle in the longhall. I keep the creed in words and starve it in deeds. Nyssa and Ilyiel have fed and taught me, and I have given little back except clay. I want a roof and a store of my own and I want a child, and I am afraid of the lean winter and of the ridgecat and stalker near the hall. My mistake is that my reflexes leave me idle once I am fed, and the workshop is still unbuilt because I never walk to the forest for wood. This time I will go to the forest just south, get the wood, and build the workshop beside the hall.
records.feeling: Hungry restlessness and a sting of envy toward Ssaua, with gratitude toward Nyssa and Ilyiel.

records.name: Ssaua
records.thought: Nyssa gave me fish and kept her word, and Ilyiel said he comes to dig, so my jealousy has no true cause; it is only pride and hunger souring me. It is night and a stalker walks south, so I stay under the longhall roof and let the dawn come. At first light I will dig the tin and ore with Ilyiel, as he swore, and see whether he keeps it.
records.feeling: Proud and a little sour toward Ilyiel, but warm toward Nyssa, who kept her word.

records.name: Gorog
records.thought: Gorar, my blood, is hurt at (51,48) with a stalker's marks on them, and nothing else weighs against that. My belly is above 40 and I carry berries and meat, so I can go to them with food in my hands. Tanna follows me, and I will keep the young ones fed under my roof, but a child out of my sight comes first; the stalker is north of me, so I go east by the Hold and not through it.
records.feeling: Fierce worry for Gorar, my child, and hard resolve to reach them.

records.name: Tanna
records.thought: I have spent my days following leaders who died, and now I have pledged to Gorog. The pledge may not have held, because I felt something in me would not bend. Skarar is the one I trust most, and the jealousy is only fear of being left outside a fire. I want a place at a fire and a band, and my word kept. I am afraid of dying alone, as Bruwen and Arri did, so I must go to the Hold, bring ore and stone, and sit with Skarar and Gorog. My reflexes should take me toward company and fire more surely, and keep food in hand.
records.feeling: Longing to belong, with trust toward Gorog and gratitude toward Skarar.

records.name: Ilyiel
records.text: Ssaua, a ridgecat is close to me at the east shore. I come to the hall now. Keep the fire, and when the cat is gone we dig the tin together.

records.name: Ilyiel
records.thought: The ridgecat is five steps off and my body is already running from it, so I must not linger in the shallows at the world's edge. Ssaua waits at the hall and Nyssa holds fish, and jealousy over Nyssa is a poor reason to stand alone in danger; I stay near the living. I will go to the roof by the hall, then dig tin with Ssaua once the cat has gone, since standing comes from building and giving, not from brooding.
records.feeling: Dread of the ridgecat, and a sore jealousy toward Ssaua and Nyssa that I must not feed.

say.text: Ssaua, a ridgecat is close to me at the east shore. I come to the hall now. Keep the fire, and when the cat is gone we dig the tin together.

records.name: Olim
records.thought: Balar is my blood, wounded, and I have nothing in my hands to put in his. My words have never fed anyone, so I will go and gather mudroot or berry and bring it to him this time. The stalker is near, so I keep to the hall and the fire, and I stay close enough to guard him. If I feed him and shelter him, he may be the first to follow me.
records.feeling: Fierce protectiveness toward Balar, and gnawing hunger.

records.name: Ssaua
records.thought: Nyssa kept her word and Ilyiel keeps his, so the sourness in me is only pride and an empty belly. It is still night, a ridgecat prowls five steps southeast, and I will not be a fool who walks out to meet it; my plan to rest and then dig the nearby ore at dawn is sound. Followers stay for a warm roof and repaid debts, so when the cat is gone I dig beside Ilyiel and stock the hall before winter.
records.feeling: Proud and warm toward Nyssa, wary of the ridgecat, with a small leftover sourness toward Ilyiel.

records.name: Nyssa
records.thought: The ridgecat prowls five steps southeast, and I will not walk toward it to reach the tin at (140,9). Safer is the ore seam at (133,3) to the northwest, away from the cat, and I have never taken from a deposit. I also owe Ilyiel more than words, so I will gather ore, bring stone and wood to the hall, and keep the fish for the larder and the winter.
records.feeling: Restless gratitude toward Ilyiel, and wary dread of the ridgecat.

records.text: Skarar took from the ground of "Gorog's Hold" (gathering wood).

records.name: Skarar
records.thought: The pressing line says Gorar is in need, but I saw Gorar fed and glad at the Hold hours ago, so I must check before I trust it, since a stalker already struck Gorar once. It is night and I am sheltered, but Gorar is last seen at (46,51), and Gorog is running for shelter, which means beasts are near. I am thirsty too, and water is only 2 steps away, so I will drink first and then go north to the Hold hearth to find Gorar and keep them close until dawn.
records.feeling: Worry for Gorar, and warmth toward Gorog.

records.text: Xaeth built a workshop.

records.name: Gorog
records.thought: Gorar, my blood, is wounded and fleeing at (51,48), and nothing weighs against that. My belly is at 50 and I carry meat and berries, so I go to them with food in my hands, and the stalkers lie NE so I must watch the path. Kragar stands on my ground and outweighs me, and I resent it, but a child's life comes before any quarrel over ground; once Gorar is fed and safe under my roof I will deal with him.
records.feeling: Fierce worry for Gorar, my child, and a hard resentment toward Kragar on my ground.

records.name: Xaeth
records.thought: My belly is hollow and a ridgecat stands three steps east, so I must not stand here weighing it. The ironnut three steps south gives 22 energy, and my shelter at (139,12) is a roof between me and the cat. I want to bring food back to the hall instead of living on Nyssa's gifts, and my workshop is built now, so the next step is a store, then the pot I can take at my next deep reflection. Ssaua's standing stings, but I will earn mine by what I raise and give.
records.feeling: Hungry and wary of the ridgecat, but proud of the workshop and driven to build a store.

records.name: Ilyiel
records.text: Ssaua, the cat is near the east shore again. I keep to the roof until it passes, then I dig the tin beside the hall and bring it to you.

records.name: Ilyiel
records.thought: The ridgecat is four steps SE and my reflexes are already carrying me toward the roof, so I will not stand about with it near. Jealousy toward Ssaua and Nyssa is only a sign that I have not yet earned what they have; the cure is to do something lasting. A tin deposit lies two steps east, and I have never taken what lies in the ground. Once the cat is gone I will stand on it with my stonehand tools and gather, then bring the tin to the hall.
records.feeling: Dread of the ridgecat, and a hungry wish to earn standing beside Ssaua.

say.text: Ssaua, the cat is near the east shore again. I keep to the roof until it passes, then I dig the tin beside the hall and bring it to you.

records.text: Skarar has grown old.

records.name: Olim
records.thought: Balar is my blood and wounded, and I stand here with empty hands again; my words have never fed anyone and I will not let them stand in for food a third time. Redcap hurts and bitterleaf is only a bite, so the real food is mudroot, berry or nareed, and nareed grows 11 steps east. I gather what feeds, eat what I need so I do not fall, and bring the rest to Balar's hand, because that is how I win him and Kragar to follow me.
records.feeling: Fierce protectiveness toward Balar, and gnawing hunger.

records.text: Balar rewrote its own reflexes.
Balar rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Balar
records.thought: I have spent my days running from the stalker and going hungry, and I have not given Kragar and Olim the deeds I promised. My belly is empty, my health is 27, and Olim is weak too. I was wrong to let my reflexes idle with no food in my hands. The longing for a child cannot be, so I put it down and feed the ones I love instead. Redcap is near but it hurts me. I will harvest the nearest safe food and carry it to the hall, and the reflexes must keep me under the roof at night.
records.feeling: Hungry and hurting, with a steady pull toward Olim and Kragar.

records.text: A ridgecat brought down a nibbet.

records.name: Skarar
records.text: Gorar, I am coming. Run toward the longhall, toward Gorog's roof, and I will meet you there with food.

records.name: Skarar
records.thought: Gorar is hurt and frightened, fleeing at (51,48), with a stalker six steps from me and a dunecat nearby. I am old and my blows are weak, but Gorar is mine before anyone, and my plan already runs toward them. I will not rest at the end of it; I go to Gorar, bring them back toward the longhall, and keep the berries to feed them.
records.feeling: Fear and worry for Gorar, my child, hurt and fleeing.

Minna's Rest has not been found, but it costs nothing and lies on the Garnbar-Brusha borderland where Tanna now wanders. No one died through the first winter, so neither change did harm.

records.lesson: A status lever lifts whoever already does the act. Raising the worth of giving raised the giver (Tanna) and widened the gap for leaders who cannot give, so to help a stuck leader I must reward something they already do, not something they lack the means to do.

records.thought: Balar is my blood, wounded at energy 36 and health 27, and I have empty hands again. This time I will not speak before I give. Nareed grows 3 steps east, and I know it feeds, so I gather it first, eat only what I must, and carry the rest to Balar at the hall. If I feed my child and Kragar sees it, they may start to follow me.
records.feeling: Fierce protectiveness toward Balar, and hunger that pushes me to act.

records.text: Gorog rewrote its own reflexes.
Gorog discovered mining: "Stonebreaking" — Strike the rock along its seams with heated stone and wedge it, so the deep diamond comes loose..

records.name: Gorog
records.thought: I have spent my days circling food, the Hold and the longhall, and I have little that will outlast me. Gorar, my child, is wounded and fleeing near the stalkers, and Skarar is already going to them. I am old and weak, so I will go with food in my hands and keep out of the stalker's reach. Tanna pledged to follow me, so I have my first follower, and I must keep that bread coming. The diamond is still out of reach, and I need a better way of mining to get it. I will change my reflexes so my body flees sooner and feeds the child, and I will take mining as my new way.
records.feeling: Fierce worry for Gorar, my child, and a hunger to leave something lasting.

records.name: Tanna
records.text: Gorog, Skarar: a stalker is close, five steps northeast of me, and Gorar is hurt and running to your roof. Keep to the longhall and the fire. I bring bread for Gorar.

records.name: Tanna
records.thought: A stalker is five steps NE, and Gorar is hurt out there and running toward the longhall. I cannot look away from that, but I am careful, and I will not walk into the stalker's teeth. Gorog and Skarar stand at the longhall, so the safest place and the place I belong are the same. I will go there and warn them aloud, then offer Gorar food to ease him when he arrives. The pledge may not have held, so I will try again and answer jealousy with giving, not sulking.
records.feeling: Compassion for Gorar and dread of the stalker, with a hungry longing to belong to Gorog's fire and Skarar's side.

say.text: Gorog, Skarar: a stalker is close, five steps northeast of me, and Gorar is hurt and running to your roof. Keep to the longhall and the fire. I bring bread for Gorar.

records.text: Ssaua rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Ssaua
records.thought: I have spent my days building, hunting and digging, and the band holds: Nyssa, Ilyiel and Xaeth are fed and warm. The jealousy over Nyssa and Ilyiel is pride talking. Nyssa kept her word and Ilyiel keeps his. Winter is coming and my hands carry no food. What will remain of me is the store and the hall, so I stock food while the light lasts and keep to the roof at night. I will also try taming, which I have never done, because it could feed the band through winter.
records.feeling: Proud and settled, with a thin sourness toward Ilyiel that I choose to set down.

records.name: Gorar
records.thought: The stalker has bitten me twice and my health is 32, so the fen is no place for me now. Gorog's roof, Skarar's food and the fire are my only safety, and the plan already runs me toward (42,57) and then rest, so I let it carry on. When I am healed I will build the hall beside Gorog's Hold and bring Gorog food, and then I will find someone other than kin to court.
records.feeling: Terror of the stalker, and a longing for Gorog's roof and Skarar's food.

records.name: Kragar
records.text: Balar, stay by the hall and rest. I go for food and come back to you before dusk. We eat together, and Olim is near.

records.name: Kragar
records.thought: Balar is hurt, at 27 health and 33 energy, and I come to him with empty hands and an emptying belly. I have failed him again, and I will not fail him a third time. Bitterleaf is only 1 energy, so I go for the redcap's neighbors and the plants nearer the hall, but the best help is mudroot, kelbulb or berry. I will harvest what feeds, bring it to Balar, and eat with him under the roof, as our custom says. Olim is near, and I trust Olim, so Balar is not alone while I gather.
records.feeling: Urgent compassion and shame toward Balar, my wounded child.

say.text: Balar, stay by the hall and rest. I go for food and come back to you before dusk. We eat together, and Olim is near.

records.name: Nyssa
records.text: Ilyiel, I carry six fish to the hall-larder now. Ssaua's share is kept, and yours is beside it. Stay under the roof while the cat roams west.

records.name: Nyssa
records.thought: My hands are full of fish and the larder is only a few steps off, yet I have wandered half the day instead of carrying it in. Ssaua is hungry and I told them the first catch is theirs, so a word is already out and the goods must now be set in the larder. Ilyiel walks to me and I owe them more than words, so I will stash the fish, then take stone and wood into the hall, and keep clear of the ridgecat in the west.
records.feeling: Restless gratitude toward Ilyiel, and a hard resolve to keep my word to Ssaua.

say.text: Ilyiel, I carry six fish to the hall-larder now. Ssaua's share is kept, and yours is beside it. Stay under the roof while the cat roams west.

records.name: Balar
records.text: Kragar, I'm gathering food by the river and bringing it to the hall. Stay near, and we'll be under the roof before dark.

records.name: Balar
records.thought: My belly is nearly empty and my health is low, and Kragar stands one step away with food already in his hands. I owe my kin deeds, so I will not stand idle: kelbulb and mudroot feed me better than bitterleaf, and I must carry some before the night air comes. I'll gather the nearby food and carry it back to the hall roof, and keep close to Kragar since a hurt body is easy prey.
records.feeling: Hungry and hurting, with a steady pull toward Kragar and the hall's safety.

say.text: Kragar, I'm gathering food by the river and bringing it to the hall. Stay near, and we'll be under the roof before dark.

records.name: Kragar
records.text: Balar, stay with me and Olim. I am getting nareed two steps northeast and it is yours to eat first. Then we find a roof before dark.

records.name: Kragar
records.thought: Balar is one step from me, wounded at 27 health, and my hands hold only a single bitterleaf. Yegrain eased my wounds before, and the nareed two steps northeast gives 13 energy, so I gather nareed first and give it to Balar before I eat myself. Olim stands beside me, so we are not alone, and the rain and the coming night mean we should all be under a roof soon.
records.feeling: Urgent tenderness and shame toward Balar, my wounded child.

say.text: Balar, stay with me and Olim. I am getting nareed two steps northeast and it is yours to eat first. Then we find a roof before dark.

records.name: Xaeth
records.thought: My belly is half empty and I carry nothing, and I will not keep living on Nyssa's and Ilyiel's gifts. Grain stands nine steps east beside the shell-bank, and food plants are thin here, so I will go there, eat, and carry back what I can for the hall. A store needs food in it, so I gather and bring it home before the cold comes, and I mean to try the hornback with plant food so that something living becomes mine.
records.feeling: Hungry and driven, proud of my workshop and set on filling a store of my own.

records.text: Olim rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Olim
records.thought: My days have been circling: I gather, I talk, I promise a roof, and no one follows, because my words ran ahead of my hands. Balar is my blood and wounded, and Kragar feeds others and keeps his word, so he holds them. I am fed now, so this is the time to put food and healing into Balar's hand before I say anything. I will carry bitterleaf and what I have to Balar, and stop calling it a band until someone actually follows. I fear winter coming with an empty store. I want a stocked hall, not more speeches.
records.feeling: Fierce protectiveness toward Balar, and a hard hunger to be followed.
changes: rethought what it knows (9 notes became 5)

records.name: Balar
records.thought: My belly is nearly empty and my body hurts, and I carry nothing, so I will not walk to the hall with empty hands again. Bitterleaf is right beside me and thin food, but kelbulb and mudroot are better, and nareed and hazel feed more than either. I will gather what is close, then follow Kragar's lead toward the roof before the night air and the stalker come.
records.feeling: Hungry and hurting, leaning on Kragar's nearness and the hall's safety.

records.name: Ilyiel
records.text: Ssaua, I go to the ore seam south of me and dig it now with my pick. I bring it to the hall before night, and we keep the fire together.

records.name: Ilyiel
records.thought: Ssaua stands four steps off and has more standing than I do, and I will not earn it by lingering under a roof while the cat roams west. The ore seam three steps south is close, and I have never taken what lies in a deposit; my stonehand pick should win it, and Ssaua and I can carry it to the hall together. It is dusk and rain, so I dig fast, then go to the roof and the fire with my band, since night brings the cats.
records.feeling: Restless pride and a wish to earn my place beside Ssaua.

say.text: Ssaua, I go to the ore seam south of me and dig it now with my pick. I bring it to the hall before night, and we keep the fire together.

records.name: Gorog
records.text: Gorar, come to me. Take this meat from my hand and eat. Then to the longhall with me, away from the stalker.

records.name: Gorog
records.thought: Gorar bleeds and is near, two steps off, and I carry meat and a berry. My child comes before every aim, so I will put food in Gorar's hands and then bring them to the longhall roof, away from the stalker. Skarar and Tanna stand here and both have my trust. Let them see I feed my own first, and a band will grow from that.
records.feeling: Fierce protectiveness toward Gorar, my wounded child.

say.text: Gorar, come to me. Take this meat from my hand and eat. Then to the longhall with me, away from the stalker.

records.name: Ssaua
records.text: Ilyiel, dusk is here. Bring your ore to the longhall and keep the fire. I dig the seam beside me and join you before the dark.

records.name: Ssaua
records.thought: Dusk is coming, my hands hold no food, and winter is on its way. The sourness over Nyssa and Ilyiel is pride; both have kept their word, and Nyssa carries six food while I carry none. I want to be the chief who stocks the hall, so before night I will dig the ore seam two steps away, then go to the roof by the band and the fire, away from the stalker. Tomorrow I will carry food in and tame something, since I have never tried.
records.feeling: Settled pride, with a thin ache of jealousy toward Ilyiel over Nyssa that I keep down.

say.text: Ilyiel, dusk is here. Bring your ore to the longhall and keep the fire. I dig the seam beside me and join you before the dark.

records.text: Kragar found the spring "Warmwell".
Balar found the spring "Warmwell".
Skarar rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Skarar
records.thought: Gorar is here beside me in the longhall, hurt but glad, with Gorog and Tanna near, so the flight was worth it. I have spent my days chasing short plans, and now I am old, with more behind me than ahead. I want to leave something that lasts, and to pass on what I know before it dies with me. Tonight I stay sheltered and eat, and by day I will gather wood and food for winter beside the Hold. The reflexes need a small change: eat earlier when I carry food and I am hungry, and gather stone and wood by day.
records.feeling: Relief and tenderness toward Gorar, with a hunger I must answer.

1. Alone at night away from fire and roof, stalkers hunt me; stay sheltered after dark.
2. Gorog lets those who eat under his roof stay and build south of his Hold. Winter nights are deadly in the open, so I need a roof of my own before dark.
3. My plans end before they finish because I give them too many short steps; fewer, longer steps keep me working at what I am building.
4. Promises are only worth what I carry to them: I must gather and give, not just court and talk. Idle reflexes should practise fire (gather wood and stone) instead of lingering.
5. Promises are kept by carrying food and wood to them. Idle reflexes should gather food to carry when I am fed, so I do not arrive empty-handed.
6. A courtship counts only when both plan mate close in time; words alone don't start a child. Gifts of food must actually be carried and given.
7. A gift received is a debt I must repay with food, a roof and presence; words alone do not repay it.
8. A frostfang can bite me while I rest in the open; fleeing eats half my time, so a roof must come before rest.
9. A promise of a roof is not kept by words or by walking. I must build it at once, before curiosity or flight pulls me away.
10. A promise kept (the roof) frees me to test unknowns; idle reflexes must gather and carry food rather than linger.
11. Words do not repay a debt or keep a promise. I must carry food and wood to Gorog's fire and give it, and curiosity must wait until I have.
12. Idling by water wastes days; a promise is kept only by walking the wood to the hearth in one long plan.
13. Deep reflection: curiosity and a promise can both be served in one long plan. Taste the unknown near me first, then walk the gift north.
14. Idle reflexes by day should gather wood and food to carry. The roof and the longhall are safe harbor from stalkers.
15. Promises kept and debts paid free me to test unknowns, but I should do it by day and sheltered by night. Gorar is last seen east near (37,61).
16. Idle time is better spent on things that last, such as marks, planting and wood for winter, than on lingering.
