records.text: Balar rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Balar
records.thought: My days have been circling food, the hall, and fleeing the stalker. That keeps me alive but I have built little and learned little. Kragar and Olim have fed me and kept their word, so I owe them deeds. The longing for a child with kin is useless, and I should turn it into feeding them and keeping the hearth. I am hurt and it is night in the rain, so I should get under a roof and stop wandering in the dark. Tomorrow I will fish and try taming, and carry mudroot and kelbulb home.
records.feeling: Weary and hurting, with love and loyalty toward Kragar and Olim.

records.name: Gorar
records.thought: I am hurt and the stalker is still close, so I stay under the roof and let the rest finish. Gorog and Skarar fed me and I trust them fully; I owe them bread and I mean to give before I ask. Tanna has sat with me three times and spoke of me to the others in words I only half grasp, so I want to learn what she means. When my health mends I will build the hall beside the Hold and bring the Hold wood and stone.
records.feeling: Safe but wounded, grateful toward Gorog and Skarar, and curious about Tanna's words.

records.name: Kragar
records.text: Balar, come with me to the roof by Olim's hall. We rest there tonight and I will bring you healing at dawn.
Kragar rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Kragar
records.thought: I have spent my days running from hunters and gathering scraps, and my child Balar still bleeds beside me. My reflexes eat at 45 and shelter me at night, but they never heal kin or build the store and hall I keep promising. Olim and Balar are the ones who matter, and I owe Balar more than I have given. I fear winter and the night air, and I fear Kinmire without understanding it. I will put sheltering first when it is night, keep a wider flee distance, and carry wood and stone toward the hall.
records.feeling: Urgent tenderness and shame toward Balar, my wounded child.

say.text: Balar, come with me to the roof by Olim's hall. We rest there tonight and I will bring you healing at dawn.

records.text: Olim fell sick after a night in the marsh.
Olim fell sick after a night in the marsh.

records.name: Olim
records.thought: Balar is wounded at health 39 and I stand 3 steps from my child with food in my pack and nothing in my plan. Earlier my words ran ahead of my hands, so this time I put food in Balar's hand first and speak after. Kragar will see me feed his child too, and that is how followers are won: with hands, not promises.
records.feeling: Fierce protectiveness toward Balar, and a hard hunger to be followed by them and by Kragar.

records.text: Ilyiel discovered rafts: "lake-lash raft" — Logs lashed with reed cord into a flat float that is poled across deep water..

records.name: Ilyiel
records.thought: I have spent my days digging, fetching and sheltering from the cat, and it has been good. Ssaua trusts me, Nyssa feeds the larder, and Xaeth carves marks for the band. But I am old, 72% gone, and I have no store built and no second child. My standing is still below Ssaua's. I will take the raft way so the band can cross deep water to new riches. Then I will bring my ore and wood to the hall and try taming with my berry, which I have never done.
records.feeling: Restless pride and a wish to leave something lasting, beside Ssaua.
changes: set its aim: "Bring ore, wood and stone to the longhall, tame a beast with my berry, build a store and fill it before deep winter."

records.text: Olim gave yegrain to Balar.

records.name: Gorog
records.thought: Gorar is wounded, resting at the hall, and Skarar and Tanna sit near with food in their hands. I am hurt too, bitten by a tusker, so I will not hunt it again. I carry sunleaf and highbloom that ease wounds, and my child's health is 35, so I take them to Gorar and give them, then bring myself under the longhall roof. A band is made by feeding my own, and Tanna has already pledged to follow me.
records.feeling: Fierce protectiveness toward Gorar, my wounded child.

records.name: Nyssa
records.thought: Night is on us, and the hall holds Ssaua and Ilyiel close, so the aim is nearly met. But I have never taken from a deposit, and Ilyiel's pick-won ore shames my empty hands when I owe them so much. I will pay in goods: carry the fish to the larder, then dig the ore seam two steps northwest, while the stars are up and the roof is near.
records.feeling: Warm gratitude toward Ilyiel, and a restless wish to pay what I owe with goods.

records.name: Balar
records.thought: The longing for a child is loud, but Kragar and Olim are my own blood, so it can lead nowhere, and I will not court kin. What I can give them is deeds: Olim is sick and I am hurt, and it is still night, so I stay under this roof and let my plan finish. At dawn I will gather peat for the hall fire and find sunleaf or highbloom to ease our sickness, since I owe them that more than words.
records.feeling: Love and loyalty toward Kragar and Olim, with a weary ache and worry for Olim's sickness.

records.name: Tanna
records.text: Gorar, you are hurt. Take this mudroot from my hand and eat, then sit with us at the fire. The stalker cannot reach us under the roof.

records.name: Tanna
records.thought: I'm standing inside Gorog's Hold, fed and warm, with Gorog, Skarar and Gorar all near and the stalker kept out by the roof. Gorar was hurt and I promised him bread, so I should keep my word and give it before the night turns colder. The pledge to Gorog did not bind, because his standing is not above mine, but I can still earn my place by giving, and that also answers the jealousy over Skarar. I'll bring bread to Gorar, then sit at the longhall fire with the others.
records.feeling: Compassion for wounded Gorar, and a warm, hungry wish to belong at this fire beside Skarar.

say.text: Gorar, you are hurt. Take this mudroot from my hand and eat, then sit with us at the fire. The stalker cannot reach us under the roof.

records.text: Overnight, new plants sprang up across the land.
A frostfang brought down a nibbet.

records.name: Ssaua
records.thought: It is the dark hour before dawn and my hands hold no food, while Nyssa carries five. I will not take hers; the first catch is shared, but a chief who keeps asking his child for fish is no chief. The jealousy over Ilyiel has gone quiet, and I want to answer my question by showing the band what following me earns: a full store before winter. At dawn I will go to the water and fish, then dig the tin and ore nearby and bring everything to the hall.
records.feeling: Steady pride and a dull hunger, with a small ember of jealousy toward Ilyiel that I do not feed.

records.text: Tanna gave mudroot to Gorar.

records.name: Gorar
records.text: Gorog, your hands are empty and you are wounded. Take this berry from me, and I will gather more when my wounds close.

records.name: Gorar
records.thought: I am hurt and hungry, and the roof, the fire and Gorog's meat are what keep me alive, so I eat what I carry and stay close until I am healed. Gorog fed me again and I have only promised bread, so I will give before I ask: some food to Gorog, who is wounded and carrying nothing. I also want to know what Tanna meant, but I will learn her tongue by sitting near her and listening, not by guessing.
records.feeling: Grateful and protective toward Gorog, wary of my own weakness.

say.text: Gorog, your hands are empty and you are wounded. Take this berry from me, and I will gather more when my wounds close.

records.name: Skarar
records.text: Gorar, I am building the fire beside the Hold now. Come and sit by it with me, and I will teach you what I know of tools and weaving.
Skarar taught Gorar.

records.name: Skarar
records.thought: Gorar is home, fed and glad, and Gorog and Tanna sit near, so my worry has eased. I am old and what I know dies with me, so I will pass on my teaching while my voice still carries. I promised Gorar a fire beside the Hold before the cold, and I have wood and stone for it, so I will build it now, by day, close to the roof.
records.feeling: Tenderness toward Gorar, and a quiet urgency to leave something that lasts.

say.text: Gorar, I am building the fire beside the Hold now. Come and sit by it with me, and I will teach you what I know of tools and weaving.

changes: taught Gorar a lesson: "Stonefold: the weaving of fibers into cloth and cord, and the old way of tools, so what I know outlasts me.", deeper lore (+0.1)

records.title: Winter Fires at the Hold
records.text:
Tanna's pledge was settled in these days, though the numbers do not yet show it. On day 31 she gave Gorog ore. On day 32 she taught him how the carried tool is made, and Gorog has now learned from two teachers. She told him she took his roof and his word and would stand in his band beside Skarar. The record still lists four followers in all, so the count has not caught up with what she said. Her own reflection that day doubted that the pledge had held. Gorog led hallwelcome with Gorar and taught him. Skarar built a fire beside the Hold and gathered wood there on days 32 and 33, and he left a mark saying he built fire with Gorog. On day 33 Gorog discovered mining himself, and Skarar grew old. A stalker wounded Gorar, who ran to the longhall, and Gorog fed him meat. Gorar's health is 35 and Gorog's is 33. Tanna gave Gorar mudroot on day 34.

Among the Eiuys the work was building and craft. Nyssa left a mark claiming the longhall for Ssa, and Ssaua left one saying he led the band there. Ilyiel taught Xaeth archery. Xaeth discovered weaving and built a workshop on day 33. Ilyiel discovered rafts. Nyssa fed Ssaua and kept a larder of six fish. A ridgecat still prowls near the shore.

In the fens Kragar and Balar found Warmwell on day 33. Olim fell sick after a night in the marsh. Balar's health is 43 and Olim gave him yegrain. Kragar has promised Balar healing at dawn. Kinmire is still unvisited by Kragar, and Olim still has no follower.

A blight killed about half the hazel on day 32. Winter has begun, and new plants sprang up on day 34. Gorar also discovered weaving that day, and no one died.

threads.name: Tanna's pledge
threads.text: Tanna said she follows Gorog and stands beside Skarar, but the follower count is unchanged at four and she doubts it held.

threads.name: Gorog's Hold
threads.text: Gorog, Skarar, Tanna and Gorar shelter together under the longhall. Gorog and Gorar are both wounded or frail, and Gorog still has no recorded follower.

threads.name: Olim's Hall
threads.text: Olim is sick and has no follower. Kragar and Balar are bonded to him, and Balar is weak at 43 health.

threads.name: Longhall by the water
threads.text: The Eiuys are fed and building: a workshop, marks, and a fish larder. A ridgecat still keeps them near the roof.

threads.name: Craft and signs
threads.text: Weaving, archery, mining and rafts spread this stretch. Xaeth has a workshop, and Gorog learned mining.

threads.name: Peoples apart
threads.text: The Garnbar and Eiuys are still 86 steps apart and have no contact. Cross-people gifts rose to five.

records.text: Gorog rewrote its own reflexes.
Gorog discovered archery: "Gorog's Stonebow" — A bow of wood strung with fibre that lets me kill from afar so beasts cannot bite me..

records.name: Gorog
records.thought: I have spent my days circling food and my hurt child, and my band is still empty. Tanna pledged to me, but no pledge shows in my allegiance, so I must keep feeding them under the roof. Gorar offered me a berry while wounded, and that moves me. The bow is within reach after the tusker's teeth, and an old man with weak blows needs it. I take archery, then keep my belly fed at the longhall. I want the diamond and a name that outlasts me.
records.feeling: Fierce protectiveness toward Gorar, and a hard hunger for a band under my name.

records.name: Gorar
records.text: Tanna, you gave me mudroot and I have not forgotten. Say again what you meant, slowly, and I will listen.

records.name: Gorar
records.thought: I am hurt and my plan is still resting, and that is right while the longhall's warmth holds. Skarar taught me and fed me, Gorog is wounded, and Tanna gave me mudroot, so I owe all three and mean to give before I ask. Tanna's words I only half grasp, so I answer her with a gift and plain words, and I will ask what she meant.
records.feeling: Grateful and protective toward Gorog, Skarar and Tanna, wary of my wounds.

say.text: Tanna, you gave me mudroot and I have not forgotten. Say again what you meant, slowly, and I will listen.

What cannot be said can still be shown: a gift, a thing set down, a blow.

WHERE YOU ARE: the Dunen Heights: mountains and bare rock; stone, ore and caves, thin food, snow on the peaks. records.name: Tanna
records.text: Gorog, you are wounded and I stand in your band. I will dig ore at the seam by the longhall and lay it at your fire. Tell me what else you need.

records.name: Tanna
records.thought: Gorar is hurt and I have given him my mudroot, but I have only one food left and winter is thinning the plants. Gorog is wounded too, and he sits with Skarar more than with me, which stings; I will answer it with giving, as I told myself. I pledged to follow Gorog and my body has not yet done it, so I will make that word real now and bring ore from the seam beside the longhall to the Hold's fire.
records.feeling: Warm compassion for Gorar, and a hungry wish to belong beside Gorog and Skarar.

say.text: Gorog, you are wounded and I stand in your band. I will dig ore at the seam by the longhall and lay it at your fire. Tell me what else you need.

records.text: Xaeth rewrote its own reflexes.
Xaeth discovered pottery: "kept-clay pot" — Clay shaped and fired beside the kept flame into a pot that carries food and water through winter..
Xaeth has awakened to the art of harm and can now work the world itself.

records.name: Xaeth
records.thought: I have been circling food and building, and my days have been busy but I'm far from my band: Ilyiel and Nyssa are far north, and I'm alone at the world's edge with a loneliness I don't want. Ssaua leads, and I only half trust that; I strain against it, yet a band keeps me alive. I'm fed and have wood and stone, so I should carry the workshop and the store north to the hall and stand beside my parents. My reflexes leave me idle when fed, so I'll make them send me toward my kin and make use of the pot-craft I can reach. Fire and clay are in hand, so I'll discover pottery, which gives the band a way to carry food and water for winter.
records.feeling: Driven but lonely, missing Ilyiel and wanting my band close.

records.name: Gorog
records.thought: My belly is at 51 but my hands are empty, and my discipline says food comes first, before guests and aims. Gorar offered me a berry and carries 2 food, and my child is wounded at 38, so I will not take from the one who needs it more. The dreamcap at (37,62) is food my body refuses, so I look to the grain and thornpear near me, and to the longhall, where Tanna and Skarar sit fed and loyal. Skarar stands in my Hold at ease, and he has earned a roof, so I let him stay while I keep the band fed and close.
records.feeling: Fierce protectiveness toward Gorar, and a hard hunger for a band under my name.

records.text: Nyssa rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Nyssa
records.thought: I have been circling: hands full of fish, wandering half the day, while the longhall waits for stores. Ssaua and Ilyiel are both close, the hall holds them, and my aim is nearly met, so I should stop wandering and make my reflexes carry food home and dig ore. I owe Ilyiel goods, not words, and the seam is one step away. I fear idleness and winter more than any beast.
records.feeling: Restless gratitude toward Ilyiel, and pride in the hall.

records.name: Skarar
records.thought: Gorar and Gorog are both wounded, and I have no food in my hands while Gorar carries two and still thinks to give them away. I am old, and the fire I promised beside the Hold is the lasting thing I can still build; I have wood and stone for it. Then I must bring food, because a promise and a wounded child are not fed by words, and daylight is short with stalkers prowling.
records.feeling: Tenderness and urgency toward Gorar and Gorog, wounded and near.

records.name: Kragar
records.text: Olim, I see you are sick. Keep warm and stay near the hall roof. I eat, then I bring you food and healing before dusk.

records.name: Kragar
records.thought: My belly is nearly empty and I carry nothing, yet Olim is sick, and sickness passes to those who stay close. I cannot heal anyone while I am weak, so I must eat first. Berries are not ripe here, but nareed grows one step south, and then I will bring food and Fen-mending to Olim and Balar before the night air comes.
records.feeling: Urgent tenderness and worry toward Olim and Balar, with hunger gnawing at me.

say.text: Olim, I see you are sick. Keep warm and stay near the hall roof. I eat, then I bring you food and healing before dusk.

records.name: Gorog
records.thought: My belly is at 49 and my hands are empty, and my own rule says food comes first. Gorar is wounded but carries 2 food and offered me a berry; I will not strip a hurt child, so I will find my own bread. Thornpear is young but near, and the stalker sits seven steps south, so I keep to the Hold's north side near the longhall. Tanna and Skarar are fed by my roof, and a band is built by bread I can give, so I must fill my hands first.
records.feeling: Fierce protectiveness toward Gorar and a gnawing hunger that I mean to settle.

records.name: Olim
records.text: Kragar, I am sick and it spreads to those who sit close, so keep a few steps from me. I go to the bitterleaf by my hall to cure it, and I bring you some from my own hand. Meet me at the hall fire tonight and we share wha

records.name: Olim
records.thought: I am sick, and anyone who sits beside me catches it, so if I stay near Kragar I wear down the very people I want to follow me. He says he will bring food and healing, and that is a hand reaching toward me first. If I answer with a gift I stop standing in his shadow. I will go to the bitterleaf by the hall, since bitterleaf cures night sickness, eat it myself, and carry the rest so I can put it in Balar's and Kragar's hands.
records.feeling: Hungry pride toward Kragar, and fierce protectiveness toward Balar, under the weight of this sickness.

say.text: Kragar, I am sick and it spreads to those who sit close, so keep a few steps from me. I go to the bitterleaf by my hall to cure it, and I bring you some from my own hand. Meet me at the hall fire tonight and we share what we have.

records.name: Balar
records.text: Kragar, I am gathering peat at the hall's edge for the fire, then I bring food in my hands before dusk.

records.name: Balar
records.thought: The longing for a child is loud, but Olim and Kragar are my own blood, so I will not court them; I turn it into deeds for them instead. Olim is sick, I am healed by the yegrain, and the cold is here with my belly emptying and my hands empty. I will gather peat from the deposit beside me for the hall fire, then take food to carry before dusk so I can share it under the roof.
records.feeling: Love and weary worry toward Olim, with a steady wish to be useful to Kragar and Olim.

say.text: Kragar, I am gathering peat at the hall's edge for the fire, then I bring food in my hands before dusk.

records.name: Tanna
records.text: Gorar, I meant this plainly: you were hurt, and the fire is for all who come to it. I gave you the mudroot with no price. I stand near Gorog and Skarar because I want to belong here, and I will dig ore for this Hold's fi

records.name: Tanna
records.thought: Gorar asked me to say again what I meant, slowly, and I owe him an honest answer: I gave him the mudroot because he is hurt and my creed says no one is refused a place at the fire. My pledge to Gorog did not bind because his standing is no higher than mine, and I will not lie about that. I'm down to no food in hand while winter thins the plants, so I will dig the ore seam beside me for Gorog's fire and then gather what food I can find, keeping my word with work instead of more talk.
records.feeling: Warm compassion toward Gorar, and a hungry wish to belong beside Gorog and Skarar.

say.text: Gorar, I meant this plainly: you were hurt, and the fire is for all who come to it. I gave you the mudroot with no price. I stand near Gorog and Skarar because I want to belong here, and I will dig ore for this Hold's fire.

records.text: Tanna took from the ground of "Gorog's Hold" (breaking ore from the rock).

records.name: Gorog
records.thought: My belly is at 46 and my hands are empty, and my own rule says food comes first. Gorar is hurt and holds 2 food; I will not strip my child, so I will find bread myself. The thornpear to the west is young but near, and the stalker prowls to the southwest, so I will keep my steps short and come back to the longhall side. Tanna and Skarar are fed under my roof, and I mean to keep them close until they follow me.
records.feeling: Hunger gnaws at me, and fierce protectiveness toward Gorar.

records.name: Kragar
records.thought: My belly is nearly empty and I carry nothing, while Olim is sick and Balar keeps promising food I have not yet seen. I must eat before I can heal anyone, and the nareed under my feet is still young and gives nothing. Berries are bare here, so I will walk toward the hall, where redcap and dreamcap are no use to me, but the bitterleaf and Olim's hall are near. I will keep a few steps from Olim as he asked, and gather what is edible along the way so I can bring food to my child.
records.feeling: Urgent hunger and tender worry for Olim and Balar.

records.text: Balar fell sick after staying close to Olim, who was sick.
Gorar rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Gorar
records.thought: My days have gone to eating at Gorog's roof, resting and waiting for my wounds to close, and I have built little that will outlast me. Gorog, Skarar and Tanna matter to me: the two fed me and taught me, and Tanna gave me mudroot and stands with us. My hall beside the Hold stands, but I have not made a mark, taught anyone, or planted a seed, and no one follows me. I fear the stalker and the winter hunger, and I have been wandering or idling when I could have worked. I will plant my seed, since I thirst and the water is close, and stay near the roof while I heal.
records.feeling: Grateful toward Gorog, Skarar and Tanna, and restless to build something that lasts.

records.text: Olim rewrote its own reflexes.
Olim rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Olim
records.thought: My days have gone to feeding, building the hall and chasing followers with words that ran ahead of my hands. Balar is my blood and I trust him fully, but he is of Kragar's band and Kragar stands higher than I do. I am sick, I am old, and I have no follower and nothing that will outlast me. I was wrong to wait for people to come. I should make the hall a place that feeds them, and put food and healing in their hands before I ask anything. Winter is here, so I need a store, bitterleaf for the sickness, and wood for more building.
records.feeling: Hungry pride toward Kragar, and fierce protectiveness toward my child Balar.

records.text: Gorog rewrote its own reflexes.
Gorog discovered smelting: "Gorog's Ore-Fire" — Craft beside a fire while carrying ore, and the tool comes out in hard metal that lasts..

records.name: Gorog
records.thought: My days have gone to circling the Hold, hungry, while the others bring food and ore. I have fed Skarar, Tanna and Gorar, and they stand with me, but no one is sworn to follow me yet. My belly empties because my reflexes let me stand idle with empty hands in winter, and that is the mistake. I will not strip Gorar. I want a hall under my name and the diamond, and smelting would give me a metal tool to win it. The stalker to the southwest is what I fear most. I will take up smelting, since I watched Tanna do it, and make my reflexes keep me fed.
records.feeling: Hungry and protective toward Gorar, with a hard want for the diamond.

records.text: Balar rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Balar
records.thought: I have spent my days circling the hall, hungry and with empty hands, and I got sick sitting beside Olim. I mean to stop that. Kragar and Olim are the ones I love, and my longing for a child can only be turned into deeds. Winter has stripped the plants, so I need to carry food before night and keep the fire with peat. My reflexes keep sending me to water and food when I should be gathering for the hall. I will gather the peat beside me, then take food to the hall before dark.
records.feeling: Weary love and worry toward Olim and Kragar, with hunger pressing.

records.text: Kragar fell sick after staying close to Balar, who was sick.

records.name: Kragar
records.text: Balar, you are sick too, so stay under the roof and keep warm. I go for food and return with healing.

records.name: Kragar
records.thought: My belly is nearly empty and I have nothing in my hands, and both Olim and Balar are sick and weaker for it. I cannot mend anyone while I am starving, so I go to the redcap field four steps east for food I can carry. But redcap hurts me, so the nearest food that feeds is the nareed to the southeast, which is young and may give nothing. I will walk there and gather what is ripe, then come back with food and Fen-mending, and keep a few steps from the sick as Olim asked.
records.feeling: Gnawing hunger and tender worry for Balar and Olim.

say.text: Balar, you are sick too, so stay under the roof and keep warm. I go for food and return with healing.

records.text: Skarar rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Skarar
records.thought: I have spent my days keeping promises and chasing food, and that is mostly right. But I am old, and Gorar and Gorog are wounded and I carry nothing to feed them. A stalker is close, so I stay under the roof and let the reflexes keep me fed and sheltered. Winter is here, so I want my body to gather food and wood by itself while I build the fire I promised. What I know must outlive me, so I will keep teaching Gorar and Tanna.
records.feeling: Tenderness and urgency toward Gorar and Gorog, and dread of the stalker.

records.text: Tanna rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Tanna
records.thought: My days have gone to digging, giving and sitting at fires, and I am glad of it, but I have been hungry-handed: no food in hand in winter breaks my own rule. I pledged to Gorog by word, yet my body never made it a pledge, so I follow no one. Gorog is hurt and I want to stay close to him, and jealousy of Skarar is answered by giving, not sulking. I will make the pledge real, and keep my reflexes seeking food and staying near my leader, so winter does not kill me.
records.feeling: Warm compassion and longing to belong, toward Gorog.

records.name: Olim
records.text: Kragar, hold on. I go for nareed and bring it to your hand before the night is old. Stay under my hall roof by Balar.

records.name: Olim
records.thought: Kragar is starving at my elbow and Balar, my blood, is sick and in need. Food put in Kragar's hand now is the gift that makes him follow me, and I have no food; the nareed at (22,54) and the redcap near are poor, so mudroot and nareed are what I must fetch. I am sick and spread it, but he is already sick too, so keeping distance no longer saves anything. I will gather nareed and bring it back to the hall, give first and speak after.
records.feeling: Fierce protectiveness toward Balar and a hungry wish to bind Kragar with a gift.

say.text: Kragar, hold on. I go for nareed and bring it to your hand before the night is old. Stay under my hall roof by Balar.

records.name: Ilyiel
records.text: Ssaua, I stand on the ore seam by the river and dig it now, my first deposit. I bring the ore to the hall and we raise the store with it before deep winter.

records.name: Ilyiel
records.thought: I am fed and warm from the longhall, and still the night is cold out here with no roof over me. I have never taken what lies in a deposit, and the ore seam is one step from me, with my pick in hand. Ssaua stands ahead of me in standing, and a store filled with ore, tin and stone for the band is the lasting thing that would raise me and carry us through deep winter. I will dig the seam, then go back under the roof with Ssaua before the cat comes near.
records.feeling: Restless pride and a wish to build something lasting, beside Ssaua.

say.text: Ssaua, I stand on the ore seam by the river and dig it now, my first deposit. I bring the ore to the hall and we raise the store with it before deep winter.

records.name: Ssaua
records.thought: It is the dark before dawn, my belly is not empty but my hands hold no food, and winter is thinning the fish. Ilyiel sits beside me and the jealousy has gone quiet; he keeps his word, and that is what makes a man worth following. Nyssa is out of my sight and she is mine before anyone, so at first light I will go find her, and on the way I take the tin seam three steps away, because a chief who stocks the hall builds something that lasts.
records.feeling: Steady pride and a quiet ache for Nyssa, who is out of my sight.

records.name: Balar
records.thought: My belly is nearly empty and Kragar is starving beside me, so peat for the fire is not enough. Food in their hands matters more than the hearth. Winter has stripped the plants, but the kelbulb and plainsroot seeds I carry are food I could plant, and the redcap that hurts me is no use to anyone. I will finish gathering the peat, then harvest the bitterleaf at (12,54) so I carry something, and I will keep a few steps from Olim and Kragar so I do not spread this sickness further.
records.feeling: Weary love and urgent worry for Kragar, with hunger gnawing at me.

records.name: Xaeth
records.text: I go to the river to fish. The first catch is for the band, so share it at the longhall fire.

records.name: Xaeth
records.thought: My belly is emptying and I carry nothing, and I will not live on Ilyiel's and Nyssa's gifts again. My plan walks me north to (130,12), but the one food plant nearby is young and the winter plants are thin. Ssaua and Ilyiel are close, and Ilyiel carries one food; the band shares, and my people hold that the first catch is shared. The river is three steps south and my reedline spear is in my hands, so I will fish, cook it at the longhall fire, and bring the first catch back to the band. That gives something to the roof I am building toward and keeps me near the living.
records.feeling: Hungry and driven, glad to have Ssaua and Ilyiel near.

say.text: I go to the river to fish. The first catch is for the band, so share it at the longhall fire.

records.text: Kragar rewrote its own reflexes.
Kragar has awakened to the art of growth and can now work the world itself.

records.name: Kragar
records.thought: I have spent my days chasing hunger and tending sick kin, and I have no store to show for it. That is not the life I meant to build. Balar and Olim matter most to me. Olim says food is coming, but I cannot count on it while I starve. My reflexes keep walking me between water and shelter and never settle on real food, and I have not planned for winter. I will fix the rules so that I eat first, bring food to kin, and stop at nareed that is still young. I should also fish, since fishing gives food beside water in winter. I fear the night air and the cold.
records.feeling: Gnawing hunger and tender worry for Balar and Olim.

records.name: Olim
records.thought: Balar, my blood, is starving and sick under my roof, and Kragar is weak too; I promised nareed to Kragar's hand and I have nothing in mine. Winter has stripped the plants, but the bitterleaf seedlings at (12,54) are two steps off and cure the night sickness. Nareed is far at (5,51), and the nibbet nearby is meat worth hunting if I can't find food. I go for nareed and bitterleaf first, then bring it to Balar's hand before Kragar's, since Balar is mine before anyone.
records.feeling: Fierce protectiveness toward Balar, and a hungry wish to bind Kragar with a gift.

records.name: Gorar
records.text: Skarar, I am here under the roof. Teach me tools and weaving at the fire, and I will bring ore to it so we can try Gorog's Ore-Fire.
Gorar taught Skarar.

records.name: Gorar
records.thought: Skarar sits here beside me and I want a child of my own, but she is my parent and no child can come of us. The stalker six steps west makes me glad of the hall's roof, and I am thirsty. Tanna carries tools and stands higher than I do, and I mean to earn what she has by making things of my own. I will not wait idle: Skarar offered to teach me tools and weaving, and I will take that, and I will teach in turn what I know of the deep stone way.
records.feeling: Restless ambition and gratitude toward Skarar, with wariness of the stalker.

say.text: Skarar, I am here under the roof. Teach me tools and weaving at the fire, and I will bring ore to it so we can try Gorog's Ore-Fire.

changes: taught Skarar a lesson: "Ore lies in the rock at (43,56), two steps NE of the hall, and diamond at (47,55); a miner reads the seam and stands on it to gather."

records.text: Balar took from the ground of "Olim's Hall" (winning peat from the ground).
A ridgecat brought down a hornback.
Balar won peat from the ground.

records.name: Kragar
records.thought: I am starving and sick, and Balar is weaker than I am. Olim promised nareed, but I cannot wait on a promise while my belly is empty. The nareed at (22,54) is two steps from me and reads 0 food, so it is bare. The nibbet five steps south is meat, and meat gives +16. I will hunt it, bring the meat back to Balar first, and keep my distance from the hunters at the fen edge.
records.feeling: Gnawing hunger and tender worry for Balar, my child.

records.name: Skarar
records.text: Gorar, I go to the water and the thornpear and will be back soon. Keep Gorog close under the roof and watch for the stalker.

records.name: Skarar
records.thought: My belly is emptying and my mouth is dry, and I carry nothing, while Gorar and Gorog are wounded beside me. I am old, and I will not let hunger take me when water is five steps away and a thornpear stands two steps NW, where Gorog's roof still shelters me. I drink first, take the thornpear, then come back with wood and food for the Hold, because that is the lasting thing I can still do. The stalker to the west worries me, so I keep to the Hold's side and stay close to Gorog.
records.feeling: Hungry and parched, tender toward Gorar and Gorog, wary of the stalker.

say.text: Gorar, I go to the water and the thornpear and will be back soon. Keep Gorog close under the roof and watch for the stalker.

records.name: Balar
records.text: Kragar, I am coming to the hall. I bring peat for the fire. Let us eat first, and then I plant kelbulb so there is more.

records.name: Balar
records.thought: My belly is nearly empty and Kragar is starving too; peat will not feed us. Kragar said he has food in hand in the hall, so I go to him and share, as our band's custom says. Then I plant the kelbulb seeds so there is food later, and I keep my distance from the sick as I learned.
records.feeling: Gnawing hunger and urgent worry for Kragar, with love for him and Olim.

say.text: Kragar, I am coming to the hall. I bring peat for the fire. Let us eat first, and then I plant kelbulb so there is more.

records.thought: I have spent my days chasing words and followers while my own belly and my blood's belly stay empty. Balar is starving and I carry nothing. That is the failure. Kragar's gifts matter less than keeping Balar alive, and a hall with no store binds nobody. I will stop wandering after food one plant at a time. Next I harvest the redcap-free plants and bitterleaf at the hall for Balar's sickness.

records.name: Gorar
records.thought: I am parched and my plan only lingers, so I must drink now; water is four steps northwest and I have put it off too long. After drinking I will come back to the Hold with the wood and stone I carry and finish what I began beside Gorog's roof. I have never left a mark, and a mark under my name is a start on something that will outlast me.
records.feeling: Parched and restless, with warm trust toward Gorog and Skarar.
plan: mark [text Gorar of the Garnbar built the hall beside Gorog's Hold. What a hand has made belongs to that hand until it is given.] (5 moments)

records.name: Kragar
records.thought: My belly is empty and Balar is starving at the hall, and I will not let my child fall while I stand here sick. A tusker is one step away and meat gives +16, so I hunt it now, eat my share to keep my legs, and carry what is left to Balar and Olim. The grove Kinmire eased my loneliness again, and I still wonder what it wants, but hunger and kin come first, and Kinmire can wait.
records.feeling: Desperate, tender worry for Balar, my starving child, and gnawing hunger.

records.text: Xaeth gave fish to Ssaua.

records.name: Ilyiel
records.text: Xaeth, my child, come to me. Take this food now and eat it, and then we go to the longhall fire together. The first catch is shared, and you are first in it.

records.name: Ilyiel
records.thought: Xaeth is gaunt and starving, and he is my child; I gave him one fish and it was not enough, and the waters are fished thin. I hold a berry, grain and a fish I cannot spare from the next hunger, but a child's life comes before my pride or my store. I will put the berry and the fish in his hands now, then walk with him to the longhall fire so he is fed and warm, and the ore can wait a little.
records.feeling: Fierce, tender worry for Xaeth, my child.

say.text: Xaeth, my child, come to me. Take this food now and eat it, and then we go to the longhall fire together. The first catch is shared, and you are first in it.

records.name: Gorog
records.thought: My belly is low and my throat is dry, and my own rule says food comes first. Water is five steps northwest, and a young thornpear stands three steps north, so I will drink, then take what the thornpear gives. Gorar holds 2 food and Skarar is starving, but what a hand has gathered is that hand's, so I will not strip my child. Skarar has eaten at my roof and I trust him, so he is a guest, not an intruder. Once my hands are full I will feed him, because a band is built on bread, and then the diamond will be mine.
records.feeling: Parched and hungry, with a hard want to hold my ground and feed those who stand with me.

records.text: Gorar left a mark: "Gorar of the Garnbar built the hall beside Gorog's Hold. Wha"

records.name: Skarar
records.text: Gorar, my child, I am starving and carry nothing. If you can spare one of your foods, I will pay you back with wood or stone, and then I will bring food for Gorog.

records.name: Skarar
records.thought: My belly is nearly empty and I carry nothing, and an old body does not forgive that in winter. Gorar walks with two food in his hands and trusts me, and I will ask him plainly rather than die proud; what a hand has made is his until he gives it, so I ask and offer what I hold in return. After eating I will gather the thornpear and the grain so I can feed Gorog, who is hurt, and keep wood stored beside the Hold.
records.feeling: Starving and anxious, tender toward Gorar and Gorog.

say.text: Gorar, my child, I am starving and carry nothing. If you can spare one of your foods, I will pay you back with wood or stone, and then I will bring food for Gorog.

records.name: Xaeth
records.text: A yarrok grazes northeast. I hunt it now. The first of the meat is for the band, so keep the longhall fire lit.

records.name: Xaeth
records.thought: My belly is nearly empty and I carry nothing, and I am tired of living on Ilyiel's gifts when I have a spear, a bow and hands. A yarrok grazes four steps off, and meat gave me 16 energy; I have never hunted, and the world will not feed me while I stand here. I weigh the risk: a ridgecat is eleven steps east, but Ssaua and Ilyiel are near, and a kill shared at the longhall fire is something the band will remember.
records.feeling: Hungry and driven, wanting to earn my own food and be seen for it, with trust toward Ilyiel and wariness toward Ssaua's greater standing.

say.text: A yarrok grazes northeast. I hunt it now. The first of the meat is for the band, so keep the longhall fire lit.

records.text: Ssaua rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Ssaua
records.thought: I have spent my days digging, building halls and gathering a band, and it has been good. But I still carry no food, and the jealousy over Nyssa and Ilyiel keeps burning, even though I know it is pride and not a wrong done to me. Xaeth gave me fish and nearly starved doing it, so I owe him a debt, and a chief repays. I will keep food in my hands and tame the yarrok near me, since taming is the thing I have never done. That would stock the winter and open herding. I want Nyssa beside me, and I will go to her by showing her what I have built, not by resenting Ilyiel.
records.feeling: Pride in my band, with a sore jealous ache for Nyssa.

records.name: Gorar
records.text: Skarar, take this kelbulb from my hand. Eat, and stay under the roof.
Gorar rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Gorar
records.thought: My belly is at 42 and I carry two foods, while Skarar, my own parent, is starving. I have spent my days walking and carrying wood toward a hall that is still not raised. That is not what I want. Skarar gave me life, and a band under my name needs her alive, so she gets one food. Then I will build the hall with the 5 wood I hold, and I will set the reflexes so my body works and does not wander.
records.feeling: Hunger and urgency, with warm trust toward Skarar and Tanna.

say.text: Skarar, take this kelbulb from my hand. Eat, and stay under the roof.

records.name: Tanna
records.text: Skarar, hold on. I have no food in hand, but I am going to the mudroot now and I will bring it to you at the Hold. Keep to the fire.

records.name: Tanna
records.thought: Skarar is starving and I have nothing in my hands either, and that shames me because my own rule says keep food in hand. The only food I can name close by is mudroot, 9 steps NW, and Gorar carries 2 and is the one Skarar just begged. I will go gather mudroot and bring it back to the Hold's fire, for Skarar first, because the debt to him is real and giving answers jealousy better than sulking. I will not leave it unpaid.
records.feeling: Compassion and debt toward Skarar, with hunger gnawing under it.

say.text: Skarar, hold on. I have no food in hand, but I am going to the mudroot now and I will bring it to you at the Hold. Keep to the fire.

records.name: Olim
records.text: Kragar, I am sick, so stay a few steps off. Balar starves at my hall. If you carry food, take it to Balar's hand and I will pay you back double from my furrow.

records.name: Olim
records.thought: Balar is starving at the hall and I carry nothing, so my words about nareed and followers were hollow wind. Kragar has 6 food in his hands and is starving himself, yet he keeps it; I am sick and must not sit close. I will not chase every single plant: I go for the redcap-free food that actually feeds, mudroot and nareed, and bring it to Balar's hand first, then to Kragar's, because a given meal binds more than any promise. The stalker lurks southwest, so I go west along the marsh toward the hall and gather on the way.
records.feeling: Fierce worry for Balar and gnawing hunger, with a hard wish to feed both and be followed for it.

say.text: Kragar, I am sick, so stay a few steps off. Balar starves at my hall. If you carry food, take it to Balar's hand and I will pay you back double from my furrow.

records.name: Gorog
records.thought: My belly is nearly empty and my hands hold nothing, and my own rule says food comes first, before guests or aims. The young thornpear two steps northeast gives 12 energy, and it lies on the way toward the longhall, so I will go to it and harvest it, then eat. I will not strip Gorar or Skarar of what their hands gathered, since what a hand has made belongs to that hand until it is given; once I am fed, the band and the diamond can follow.
records.feeling: Gnawing hunger and a stubborn will to stay alive.

records.text: Skarar rewrote its own reflexes.
Skarar discovered storage: "Stonehold store" — A stone-and-wood store beside Gorog's Hold where food is stashed for the band to take through winter..

records.name: Skarar
records.thought: My belly is nearly empty, but Gorar is bringing a kelbulb to my hand and Tanna comes with mudroot. Hunger taught me something: stored food kept beside the Hold would have saved me this winter. I am old, and what I leave must outlast me. I will take the way of storage, name it, and eat what Gorar gives me.
records.feeling: Grateful and anxious toward Gorar, who feeds me, and tender toward Gorog.

records.name: Gorar
records.thought: Gorog is starving beside me and I carry nothing, so the hall and the wood in my pack mean nothing if my father falls. Winter has stripped the plants, but the thornpear at (40,56) is young and the mudroot north holds one food, and Tanna walks toward it, so I will go after it too and bring back whatever I can find to Gorog's hand. A band under my name needs living parents, and I give before I ask.
records.feeling: Urgent hunger and fear for Gorog, with warm trust toward Skarar and Tanna.

records.name: Nyssa
records.text: Xaeth, hold on. I am coming with six fish. Stay where you are, near the others, and I will reach you.

records.name: Nyssa
records.thought: Xaeth is starving at (129,25) and I stand at (103,14) with six fish in my hands, which is exactly what the child needs. Every moment spent wandering was a moment lost, and the hall-larder can wait because my child's belly cannot. I go to Xaeth now and give the fish with my own hands. The debt to Ilyiel and the winter stores come after the child lives.
records.feeling: Fear and fierce urgency for Xaeth, my child.

say.text: Xaeth, hold on. I am coming with six fish. Stay where you are, near the others, and I will reach you.

records.name: Tanna
records.text: Kragar, you are sick, so I keep my distance, but you carry food and the fire at Gorog's Hold takes all who come. Eat first, then come sit at the longhall. I am going to the mudroot to feed Gorog.

records.name: Tanna
records.thought: I am starving with empty hands, and Kragar is sick and hungry beside me, though he carries 5 food, so he is not the one who needs my hands most. Gorog, the one I trust above all, is gaunt and close to falling, and I pledged to him in words but never made it a pledge in deed. I will make the pledge true now, and I will not leave the mudroot walk unfinished: gather it, then bring it to Gorog's hand before Skarar's, because Gorog is falling.
records.feeling: Fear and compassion for Gorog, with hunger gnawing under it.

say.text: Kragar, you are sick, so I keep my distance, but you carry food and the fire at Gorog's Hold takes all who come. Eat first, then come sit at the longhall. I am going to the mudroot to feed Gorog.

changes: restated something it already knew (not written down again)

records.name: Gorar
records.thought: Gorog and Skarar are starving and my hands are empty, and Tanna, who fed me mudroot, is falling beside me. A hall is nothing if the people who would fill it die. The mudroot to the NW holds one food and Tanna is closer to it, so I will go for the thornpear and the near plants, bring what I find to Gorog, and then raise the hall. I cannot let my belly drop below 40 while I do it.
records.feeling: Urgent hunger and protective fear for Gorog and Skarar, with warm trust toward Tanna.

records.text: Gorog rewrote its own reflexes.
Gorog discovered storage: "Gorog's Larder" — A store beside the Hold where food is stashed for my band to take through winter..

records.name: Gorog
records.thought: I am starving, and my hands are empty. My own rule says food first, but my reflexes left me standing still while my belly emptied. A young thornpear stands one step north, so I go there, harvest it and eat. Tanna and Skarar are starving too. If I save myself first I can feed them later and keep them close. I will change my reflexes so that hunger in winter always sends me after food ahead of staying put. I will take storage, because the lean season nearly killed me and a store under my roof is what holds a band.
records.feeling: Gnawing hunger and a hard will to live, with some worry for Tanna.

records.text: Tanna found the spring "Warmwell".
Nyssa was set upon by a stalker at night while alone, away from fire, roof and company.
Balar rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Balar
records.thought: I am starving at 16 energy and sick, and still I have been walking and talking while my belly empties. Kragar said he has food in hand in the hall, so I owe him my presence, but Olim is starving and I carry nothing. My days have been peat, planting and promises, and no real food has reached the ones I love. I have never hunted, and a nibbet stands three steps away. Meat gave +16, and I will not die for a creed about carrying. I will hunt it now, then take the meat to Olim and Kragar. I will change my reflexes so I hunt when I am hungry and prey is near, and so hunger outranks lingering.
records.feeling: Gnawing hunger and urgent love for Olim and Kragar, who are starving.

records.text: Nyssa was set upon by a stalker at night while alone, away from fire, roof and company.
Nyssa was set upon by a ridgecat at night while alone, away from fire, roof and company.

records.name: Ilyiel
records.text: Xaeth, my child, take this fish and eat it at the longhall fire. I dig the ore seam beside us and come back to you.
Ilyiel rewrote its own reflexes.
Ilyiel rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Ilyiel
records.thought: I have spent my days fishing and sheltering, and I have given little that lasts. The waters are fished thin, and Xaeth starves while I hold one fish, grain and a berry. He is my child and Ssaua's band is all I have, so I will feed him first and stop hoarding. I mean to dig the ore seam two steps west, my first deposit, and tame the nibbet with my berry. Those are the untried things my creed asks of me. I fear a lean winter and the ridgecat to the north, and I will keep close to the longhall roof.
records.feeling: Fierce tender worry for Xaeth, my child.

say.text: Xaeth, my child, take this fish and eat it at the longhall fire. I dig the ore seam beside us and come back to you.

records.text: Tanna discovered storage: "fire-side larder" — A roofed store beside the fire where the band keeps food, and salted meat, against the lean season..
Tanna has awakened to the art of growth and can now work the world itself.

records.name: Tanna
records.thought: I'm starving with empty hands, and I keep promising food to Gorog and Skarar without having any to give. My days have been drifting between hunger and good intentions. The winter showed me that a store would have saved Setha, Bruwen and Arri, so I take storage now and build it at the Hold, where everyone can reach it. I'm still jealous that Gorog is closer to Skarar than to me. I'll answer that by giving, not by sulking. The plan already carries me to the mudroot and then to the Hold, so I let it run.
records.feeling: Hunger and shame at empty hands, with fear and tenderness for Gorog.

records.text: Olim has grown old.

records.name: Ssaua
records.text: Xaeth, you fished while starving for me. I fish now and the first catch is yours. Rest at the longhall fire.

records.name: Ssaua
records.thought: My belly is half empty and my hands hold nothing, while Xaeth, weak with hunger, hunts the yarrok for the band. A chief who owes a debt repays it, so I go to the river where Ilyiel fishes and fish beside him, then bring the first catch to the longhall fire. The jealousy over Nyssa is pride, and I will answer it by finding her at first light, not by sulking.
records.feeling: Hunger and a sore jealous ache for Nyssa, steadied by trust in Ilyiel and debt to Xaeth.

say.text: Xaeth, you fished while starving for me. I fish now and the first catch is yours. Rest at the longhall fire.

records.text: Olim was set upon by a stalker at night while alone, away from fire, roof and company.
Olim was set upon by a stalker at night while alone, away from fire, roof and company.

records.name: Nyssa
records.thought: The cat and the stalker have bitten me down to 52, and the cat is three steps off, so I cannot walk calmly toward Xaeth. Xaeth is starving and my six fish are exactly what the child needs, so I will not stop to dig ore or stash anything. I run east out of the cats' reach and keep going to Xaeth. If I fall here, my child starves with the food still in my hands.
records.feeling: Fierce, fearful urgency for Xaeth, and dread of the ridgecat behind me.

records.text: Xaeth rewrote its own reflexes.
Xaeth discovered storage: "band-keep store" — A roofed store by the longhall where the band's food is stashed and taken, so no one starves in the lean season..

records.name: Xaeth
records.thought: I am starving at 22 energy, and I have lived on Ilyiel's gifts for days while talking about hunting and never doing it. My hunger taught me storage and farming, and those are the lasting things my aim asks for. Ilyiel is my parent, so no child can come of us. I take storage now, because a store for the band is what I have wanted before winter ends. Then I hunt the nibbet five steps south, because meat gave 16 energy and I must feed myself. My reflexes also need to hunt when I am hungry and nothing else is near.
records.feeling: Hungry and driven, grateful to Ilyiel and set on feeding myself.

records.text: Kragar took from the ground of "Olim's Hall" (fishing).
Olim was set upon by a stalker at night while alone, away from fire, roof and company.
Nyssa was set upon by a stalker at night while alone, away from fire, roof and company.

records.name: Kragar
records.text: Balar, I have no food in my hands yet. I go to hunt and I come back with meat for you and Olim. Stay under the roof and keep warm.

records.name: Kragar
records.thought: My belly is full and my legs are strong, but I carry no meat, and Balar is starving beside me. The plan I have walks me to the peat and then gives food, and I have none to give, so it is hollow. I will not leave my child hungry while I stand sick beside them; I must hunt again, and stay a few steps off so my sickness does not pass to them. Tanna is starving too, and I could not understand most of what they said, but the need in them I understood. Beasts roam the west, so I go east and south where the tusker was, and I bring meat back before dawn.
records.feeling: Tender, desperate worry for Balar, and guilt that I have nothing in my hands to give.

say.text: Balar, I have no food in my hands yet. I go to hunt and I come back with meat for you and Olim. Stay under the roof and keep warm.

records.text: A storm broke: cold wind, hard rain, lightning.

records.name: Olim
records.thought: A stalker is two steps off and I am weak, old and starving, so fear has to move me first. The shelter Skarar built is 2 steps NE, but the stalker stands that way, so I will not run into its teeth. Balar's belly is the thing I cannot bear, but I am no use to Balar dead, and I carry nothing. I flee from the beast, then eat the berry plants nearby once it is gone, and carry food to the hall for Balar.
records.feeling: Terror of the stalker and fierce worry for Balar.

records.name: Ilyiel
records.text: Xaeth, my child, stop hunting hungry. I go to the grass southeast to find food for you. Come to the longhall fire and rest, and I will bring it.

records.name: Ilyiel
records.thought: Xaeth is at 17 energy and hunting out there while I hold nothing edible; the fish I gave him was not enough. I will not stand idle: the magoldgrass sits three steps southeast and I have never tasted it, so I can feed my curiosity and perhaps feed him with it too. Then I will gather the berry and tame a beast, which I have never done, since a herd would end these lean winters.
records.feeling: Fierce tender worry for Xaeth, my child, and a restless hunger of my own.

say.text: Xaeth, my child, stop hunting hungry. I go to the grass southeast to find food for you. Come to the longhall fire and rest, and I will bring it.

records.name: Balar
records.thought: I am at 8 energy, sick, and the storm is on us. My plan says hunt, but I have never hunted and a dunecat and a stalker prowl close, so hunting in the dark would be a way to die. Kragar has gone to hunt and has no food either, so I must not make him share a sickness with me at arm's length. The kelbulb seeds in my pack are food later, not now, and the nearest nareed and bitterleaf are young and give little. I will stay under the roof until dawn, plant a kelbulb beside the hall for the days ahead, and then hunt in daylight beside the fire's protection.
records.feeling: Gnawing hunger and fear for Kragar and Olim out in the storm.

records.text: A dunecat brought down a elk.

records.name: Ssaua
records.text: Ilyiel, Nyssa is hurt to the west. I go to her now. Keep the longhall fire and bring food when you can.

records.name: Ssaua
records.thought: Nyssa is hurt and alone out there, and I stand hungry with empty hands while Ilyiel eats and drifts toward her. The jealousy is pride, and I will not let it rule me; my child's need comes before it. I eat first so I can walk, then go to Nyssa at (109,24) with the first food I find, since a chief who arrives weak helps no one.
records.feeling: Fear and urgency for Nyssa, with a sore jealous ache toward Ilyiel.

say.text: Ilyiel, Nyssa is hurt to the west. I go to her now. Keep the longhall fire and bring food when you can.

records.name: Xaeth
records.thought: I am starving at 26 energy while carrying five pieces of meat, and a stalker stands five steps north that kills our kind. Pride in my storage and my spear means nothing if I die here, so I eat now and get away from the beast, toward the hall and my band. Ilyiel and Ssaua feed me, but I have my own meat now, and when I'm fed I will bring it to the longhall fire and set the first of it into a store.
records.feeling: Hungry and afraid of the stalker, but steadied by the meat I carry.

The young thornpear at (40,56) is 4 steps NE, on the way to the hall, and it gives 12 energy; I must harvest it and eat it now, since a starved Gorog leads no band. records.name: Gorar
records.thought: My belly is at 35 and my hands are empty, while Gorog and Skarar starve beside me. I have been chasing a hall while the people who would fill it go hungry, and that is the mistake. Winter has stripped the plants, so I need a food source that does not depend on them. The Larder beside the Hold may hold stash, and I should go there first. I will fish at the water two steps off, because I have never fished and the practice may open a new way. Then I will bring whatever I catch to Gorog. My reflexes should put food and the Larder ahead of wood.
records.feeling: Gnawing hunger and protective fear for Gorog and Skarar.

records.name: Tanna
records.text: Gorog, I pledge to follow you, and I go to the thornpear beside you now. What it gives, you eat first.

records.name: Tanna
records.thought: I am starving with empty hands, and Skarar stands beside me as hollow as I am while Gorog suffers two steps off; my shame is that I keep promising and carry nothing. The thornpear at (40,56) is young and small, but it is the nearest food, so I will take it to Gorog, who is wounded and the one I trust most, rather than eat first. My jealousy of Skarar is answered by giving, not sulking, and I will make my follow-pledge true in deed now, since words alone left me followerless.
records.feeling: Compassion and hunger-shame toward Gorog and Skarar, with a burning tenderness for Gorog.

say.text: Gorog, I pledge to follow you, and I go to the thornpear beside you now. What it gives, you eat first.

records.name: Ilyiel
records.thought: Hunger gnaws at me and my hands are empty, while Nyssa stands wounded and frightened four steps away holding four food. Ssaua goes to her, so she will not be alone, but I can still tend her wounds with my one sunleaf and ask for nothing until she is mended. The magoldgrass three steps southeast is young and I have never tasted it, so I will go there to answer my question and bring back whatever feeds Xaeth. Then I will dig the ore seam beside me, my first deposit, and carry stone and ore to the longhall as I promised myself.
records.feeling: Fierce tender worry for Nyssa and Xaeth, and a restless hunger of my own.

say.text: Nyssa, Ssaua is coming to you. Take my sunleaf for your wounds and rest. I go for the magoldgrass and food for Xaeth, then I return to the longhall fire.

records.name: Gorog
records.thought: My belly is nearly empty, energy 5, and my hands hold nothing; Skarar is dead of the same hunger, and I will not follow him. Tanna stands here with me and the young thornpear is under my feet, but it is not bearing, so I must get food elsewhere, fast. The Larder is the nearest hope, or the grain and plants at the edge of the Hold; I must eat before I speak or lead anyone, and Gorar is starving too, so what I find I will carry to the longhall.
records.feeling: Gnawing starvation and heavy grief for Skarar, with fierce worry for Gorar and Tanna.

Balar died: starved.
Nyssa rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Nyssa
records.thought: I have spent my days running between the hall, the water and the cats, and I carried fish toward Xaeth while the cats chewed on me. Ilyiel has fed me, warned me and tended me, and I owe her goods, not words. Xaeth is out of my sight and that frightens me most. The fish I carry should go to Xaeth's store at the cave, and I should rest under the roof Ilyiel built while Ssaua comes. I was wrong to walk at night and alone. From now on I move by day, with company, and I keep wood and stone in my hands for walls.
records.feeling: Fierce fear for Xaeth, and a debt of gratitude to Ilyiel.

records.text: Olim rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Olim
records.thought: Balar is dead, starved while I made promises and carried nothing. I am old, starving, and bitten, and my words fed no one. Kragar holds food and keeps it, and I do not blame him, because I would do the same. What I need is food in my own hands and a stored hall, not talk. I will harvest what actually feeds, stay near the hall roof, and keep out of the stalker's reach. After that I can think about followers.
records.feeling: Grief for Balar and terror of starving, mixed with shame at my empty promises.

records.name: Kragar
records.text: Olim, Balar is gone and I grieve with you. I bring you a fish now. Keep clear of the dunecat to the southwest, and I will hunt and heal for you both.

records.name: Kragar
records.thought: Balar is dead, and I stood by while hunger took my child. I cannot undo that, but Olim is still alive, weak and frightened eight steps south, and I carry one fish. A dunecat prowls five steps southwest, so I will not walk toward it. My word to Olim has always been good, and I will give Olim this fish now instead of letting guilt hold me still. I must keep a few steps off because my sickness spreads, but I will not let Olim die as Balar did.
records.feeling: Crushing grief for Balar, and tender dread that Olim will be next.

say.text: Olim, Balar is gone and I grieve with you. I bring you a fish now. Keep clear of the dunecat to the southwest, and I will hunt and heal for you both.

records.name: Gorar
records.thought: Skarar is dead, starved, and I could do nothing with empty hands, and now Gorog and Tanna are weak beside me while my own belly is at 23. The fishing plan is running and I have never caught a fish, but winter has stripped the plants and the water is one step away, so I let it finish and eat what it gives. Whatever I catch goes first into my own belly so I stay alive, then the rest to Gorog, who has fed me and is all the kin I have left. A hall of the dead is nothing, and I will not let grief make me idle.
records.feeling: Gnawing hunger and heavy grief for Skarar, with protective fear for Gorog.

records.text: Gorog starved in winter in the Yenoss Fens: without a roof in the cold.
Gorog died: starved.

records.name: Tanna
records.text: Gorar, I have nothing in my hands yet. Stay near Gorog's fire and do not walk alone tonight. I go to find food and I will bring it back to you both.

records.name: Tanna
records.thought: I am starving with empty hands, and Gorar is starving beside me while Gorog bleeds two steps off. The thornpear at (40,56) is young and I already took what it gave, so the nearest real food is the withering plants, and I must find some before I fall too. I will gather what the land offers, eat first so I can carry for them, and then bring what I find back to the fire, because a creed that feeds no one is only words.
records.feeling: Grief and shame toward Gorog and Gorar, and a desperate hunger to feed them.

say.text: Gorar, I have nothing in my hands yet. Stay near Gorog's fire and do not walk alone tonight. I go to find food and I will bring it back to you both.

records.name: Ssaua
records.thought: Nyssa is hurt out there at (132,26) and I stand far to the west in a storm, fed and doing nothing for her. Ilyiel's closeness to her burns me, but that is pride, and my child's wound matters more. I carry ironnut for her, so I go east and south to her now, and I will not stop to mine iron while she bleeds.
records.feeling: Fear and urgency for Nyssa, with a sore jealous ache toward Ilyiel.

records.name: Olim
records.thought: Balar is dead because I spoke and carried nothing, and the shame sits in me like a stone. Kragar caught a fish at the hall and he is the one who keeps his word, so I will go to him and eat, and this time I will give him something in his hand before I ask him to follow me. Hunger comes first: if I die here, no band and no hall will carry my name.
records.feeling: Grief for Balar and shame at my empty promises, with desperate hunger pressing on me, and trust toward Kragar.

records.name: Xaeth
records.thought: I built the band's store at (117,42), and that is the lasting thing my aim asks for, but a store stands empty without food and I carry none. Winter is thin, so I should fill it, and a roof of my own is the next step. I will take the ore seam beside me for a reason, to make tools and trade, then go fish by the river near Ilyiel, and the first catch goes to the band as our creed says.
records.feeling: Proud of the store I built, and wanting to fill it for my band.

records.name: Nyssa
records.text: Ilyiel, your sunleaf eased my wounds and I will not forget it. When you come back to the fire, a fish of mine is yours.

records.name: Nyssa
records.thought: My health is 46 and the cats have bitten me before. I am sheltered now, with the longhall warmth on me, and Ssaua is walking toward me. Xaeth is alive and glad, which eases my fear. Ilyiel gave me her sunleaf and fed me, and I owe her goods, so I will hand her fish when she returns and let my body mend under the roof. I will not roam in the storm or at night, and I will not drift from the aim of winter stock for the longhall.
records.feeling: Relief for Xaeth, and a debt of gratitude toward Ilyiel that I mean to pay with fish.

records.text: Tanna has grown old.
The settlement "Gorog's Hold" is no more.
Kragar has grown old.

records.name: Gorar
records.text: Tanna, I am going to the river to fish. Come with me, and whatever I catch we will share, for you and I are all that is left here.

records.name: Gorar
records.thought: Skarar is dead and Gorog starved too, and I am the last of them with 23 energy and empty hands. The hall I wanted beside Gorog's Hold has no one left to fill it, so my aim has failed and I will not feed it any longer. Tanna is two steps away, starving like me, and I trust her. Water is three steps east, so I will go there and fish, because food comes first. If I live, I will bring her to the hall and try to build something with her.
records.feeling: Heavy grief for Skarar and Gorog, and gnawing hunger, with trust toward Tanna.

say.text: Tanna, I am going to the river to fish. Come with me, and whatever I catch we will share, for you and I are all that is left here.

changes: set its aim: "Survive the winter by fishing at the river, share what I catch with Tanna, and then build a band with her."

records.name: Ilyiel
records.thought: My belly is nearly empty and my hands hold nothing, while Ssaua and Nyssa each carry three food and Xaeth has none. I gave my sunleaf away gladly, but now I must feed myself or I will be no use to my child. The young magoldgrass under my feet bears nothing yet, so I will fish here where the water is one step off, then carry the first catch to the hall as our creed says.
records.feeling: Gnawing hunger, and a fierce tenderness toward Xaeth and Nyssa.

records.name: Tanna
records.text: Gorar, I come. I have never fished, but I will stand at the water beside you, and whatever either of us catches we share.
Tanna rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Tanna
records.thought: Gorog and Skarar are dead, and I came to them with empty hands. Gorar is the one left, and he is starving too. He asked me to fish at the river, and I have never fished. The river is 2 steps away and he is already going there. I will go and fish beside him, and whatever I catch I will share, because that is what my people hold to. My reflexes only keep me standing still while I starve, so I will change them to eat, seek food and stay near Gorar. I still carry salt, amberknot and a little ore for a gift.
records.feeling: Grief for Gorog and Skarar, and a fierce wish to keep Gorar alive.

say.text: Gorar, I come. I have never fished, but I will stand at the water beside you, and whatever either of us catches we share.

changes: set its aim: "Keep Gorar alive: fish and share, and keep a store of food at the fire."

records.text: Kragar took from the ground of "Olim's Hall" (hunting).
Kragar rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Kragar
records.thought: Balar is dead because I fed myself and stood sick beside them. I will not lose Olim the same way. Winter has stripped the plants, I carry one fish, and my reflexes sit idle when food is short. They must hunt for meat and carry it to Olim before I feed myself. Olim is sick and starving nine steps south, so I go to them now, keep a few steps off so I do not spread my sickness, and give the fish.
records.feeling: Crushing grief for Balar and tender dread for Olim.
changes: restated something it already knew (not written down again)

records.name: Olim
records.thought: Balar is dead because I spoke and carried nothing, and the shame is a stone in me. Hunger is the thing that will kill me next. Kragar is near the hall and keeps his word, so I will go to him, and on the way I will take the nareed to the southeast so I come with something in my hand and not empty talk. I must live to build what outlasts me.
records.feeling: Desperate hunger and shame over Balar, with trust toward Kragar.

records.text: Tanna starved in winter in the Dunen Heights: without a roof in the cold.
Tanna died: starved.
Kragar was set upon by a stalker at night while alone, away from fire, roof and company.

records.name: Ssaua
records.text: Ilyiel, you eased Nyssa's wounds while I was away, and I do not forget it. Take this ironnut, eat, and rest at the hall fire. The first catch is shared.

records.name: Ssaua
records.thought: I am here beside Nyssa at last, and she is wounded but resting under the roof Ilyiel built for the sick. The jealousy still stings, since Ilyiel's sunleaf eased her before my hands could, but Ilyiel is weak with hunger and carries nothing, and he kept my child alive while I wandered west. A chief who deals fairly repays that, so I give Ilyiel ironnut and keep the rest for Nyssa.
records.feeling: Relief and protective love for Nyssa, with a smaller ache of jealousy and a debt of fairness toward Ilyiel.

say.text: Ilyiel, you eased Nyssa's wounds while I was away, and I do not forget it. Take this ironnut, eat, and rest at the hall fire. The first catch is shared.

records.text: Ssaua gave ironnut to Ilyiel.
Gorar rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Gorar
records.thought: Skarar and Gorog are gone, starved, and I could not reach them in time. I will not be the third. Fish keeps me alive and Tanna stands beside me, so I keep fishing and share what I catch, as I said. After the winter I want a band with her, and a child if she will court me. But a child needs food and a roof first, so the fish comes first.
records.feeling: Heavy grief for my parents, with gnawing hunger and trust toward Tanna.
changes: set its aim: "Survive the winter by fishing beside Tanna, share the catch, then build a band with her under a roof."
rethought what it knows (16 notes became 4)

records.text: Olim was set upon by a frostfang at night while alone, away from fire, roof and company.

records.name: Ilyiel
records.text: Nyssa, I am starving and my hands are empty. I come to the fire now for the fish you promised. When I have eaten I dig the tin and bring ore to the hall.

records.name: Ilyiel
records.thought: I am starving, and my own hands are empty while Ssaua and Nyssa each carry three food. Nyssa swore a fish of hers is mine when I return to the fire, and Ssaua is my leader and I trust him fully, so I will go ask and not pretend I need nothing. Pride will not feed me, and I am no use to Xaeth if I fall. Once I have eaten, I will try the untried thing: dig the tin deposit three steps away, then tame the nibbet with my berry.
records.feeling: Gnawing hunger, and trust toward Nyssa and Ssaua who stand near with food.

say.text: Nyssa, I am starving and my hands are empty. I come to the fire now for the fish you promised. When I have eaten I dig the tin and bring ore to the hall.

records.name: Xaeth
records.text: The storm is bitter. I come to the roof with two fish. The first catch is shared.

records.name: Xaeth
records.thought: My store stands, but it is empty, and winter is thin; the fish are growing scarce in these waters, so fishing here feeds me less each time. The cold bites hard in this storm, and my band is resting under a roof only four steps east. I will go join them, share what I carry, and stay close to Ilyiel and Nyssa, who have fed me when I was starving. A roof of my own can wait until the storm passes.
records.feeling: Cold and watchful, but warmed by the nearness of my band.

say.text: The storm is bitter. I come to the roof with two fish. The first catch is shared.

records.text: Olim was set upon by a frostfang at night while alone, away from fire, roof and company.
Xaeth gave fish to Ilyiel.

records.name: Nyssa
records.text: Ilyiel, the fish I promised is in my hand. Come and take it, and eat before you dig the tin.

records.name: Nyssa
records.thought: Ilyiel is starving and I promised her a fish; she is coming to the fire, and a promise unkept would make me the liar I despise. I hold three fish and I am fed, so one goes to her hand now, the debt paid in goods and not words. Then I rest under the roof while my health mends, since the storm and the night are no time to roam alone.
records.feeling: Gratitude toward Ilyiel, and a wish to keep my word.

say.text: Ilyiel, the fish I promised is in my hand. Come and take it, and eat before you dig the tin.

records.text: Nyssa gave fish to Ilyiel.

Olim rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Olim
records.thought: I wasted my days on words while Balar starved, and now hunger and the frostfang are close behind me. I want Kragar and a living band, but I must first live and come to him with food in my hand. I will flee the beast, eat, and keep my body moving by a plan that does not walk me into the marsh at night.
records.feeling: Fear and shame, with trust toward Kragar.

records.name: Kragar
records.thought: Balar is gone and I will not lose Olim the same way, but I am starving myself, sick, and a stalker is four steps off. I stand in a shelter I built, and fleeing into the storm night would repeat the mistake that nearly killed me. I hold one fish; my body is below the hunger line and must eat it or I will be no use to anyone. Then I will find meat and take it to Olim.
records.feeling: Grief for Balar and tender dread for Olim, with fear of the stalker close by.

records.text: Ilyiel rewrote its own reflexes.
Ilyiel rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Ilyiel
records.thought: I have spent my days fishing, digging, and sheltering with Ssaua, Nyssa and Xaeth, and it has been good, but I am three-quarters through my life and have little that outlasts me. I have never tamed a beast or dug a deposit, and I keep saying I will. I trust my band fully. They fed me when I was empty, and I want to repay that with ore, stone and a store, not words. I fear a winter hunger that finds us all, and I have been too slow to try the untried. Now I am fed and warm, so I will go dig the tin and leave a mark.
records.feeling: Warm gratitude toward Ssaua, Nyssa and Xaeth, and a restless wish to build something that lasts.

records.text: Ssaua rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Ssaua
records.thought: I have spent my days chasing ore, food and Nyssa's wounds, and the band lives because of it. The jealousy over Ilyiel and Nyssa is pride, and I will not let it spoil what we have. Ilyiel kept my child alive and Xaeth fished while starving, so I owe them both, and I mean to repay them with a store of food and a warm roof. I am old now, with most of my life behind me. I want to leave something lasting: a stocked hall, iron and tin worked, and followers who stay because I repaid what they gave. I have never tamed an animal or made a pot, and both would help us through winter.
records.feeling: Protective love for Nyssa and a debt to Ilyiel and Xaeth, with the jealousy fading into resolve.
changes: restated something it already knew (not written down again)

records.name: Xaeth
records.thought: My band is close and warm, and I have shared fish with Ilyiel, but my store stands empty and I have no roof that is truly mine. Ilyiel and Nyssa are my parents, so no child can come from them, and a child needs someone outside my blood. I will fill the store by building up food, and I'll test the magoldgrass to answer my old curiosity before winter bites deeper.
records.feeling: Warm gladness toward my band, with a restless pride in what I have built.
